reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ActionBlo.title: Class ActionBlock | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ActionBlo.summary: Class ActionBlock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A block whose objective can take more than one frame, and which therefore reports ActionResult rather than simply running to completion. public abstract class ActionBlock : Block, IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object Block ActionBlock Implements IScriptNode Inherited Members Block.Contexts Block.RequiredServices Block.DescribeChildren(NodeDescription) Block.Location Block.ExecuteAll(Block[], ScriptInstance) Block.AdvanceContained(ActionBlock, ScriptInstance) Block.None Examples internal sealed class CountDownBlock : ActionBlock { private readonly NumberSlot m_Remaining; public override void Begin(ScriptInstance instance) => instance.SetNumber(m_Remaining, 3.0); public override ActionResult Advance(ScriptInstance instance) { instance.SetNumber(m_Remaining, instance.GetNumber(m_Remaining) - 1.0); return instance.GetNumber(m_Remaining) > 0.0 ? ActionResult.Running : ActionResult.Succeeded; } } Remarks An ordinary Block does its work inside one Execute(ScriptInstance) call. An action is advanced once per frame by whatever owns it - a routine activation, or a concurrent group - until it reports Succeeded or Failed. The per-object state of an action lives in slots, not in fields. One action object is shared by every object running the script, exactly as every other block is, so AGENTS.md rule 22 applies unchanged: declare the slots the action needs during Build() and read and write them through the ScriptInstance each call is given. The owner calls Begin(ScriptInstance) once when the activation reaches this action, then Advance(ScriptInstance) once per frame while it reports Running, and Cancel(ScriptInstance) instead of any further advance when the activation is interrupted. Constructors ActionBlock(SourceLocation) Creates an action that knows where it was authored. protected ActionBlock(SourceLocation location = default) Parameters Type Name Description SourceLocation location Where the factory that built it was called, or Unknown. Methods Advance(ScriptInstance) Advances this action by one frame and reports what it has reached. public abstract ActionResult Advance(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Returns ActionResult Running while the objective is still pending, otherwise the finished outcome. Examples public override ActionResult Advance(ScriptInstance instance) => ActionResult.Succeeded; Begin(ScriptInstance) Puts this action's slots into their starting state for one activation. Called once, by the owner, before the first Advance(ScriptInstance) of that activation. public virtual void Begin(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Examples public override void Begin(ScriptInstance instance) => instance.SetNumber(m_ElapsedSlot, 0.0); Cancel(ScriptInstance) Interrupts this action and performs its own bounded cleanup. An action that is cancelled reports no outcome at all: cancellation is neither Succeeded nor Failed. public virtual void Cancel(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Examples public override void Cancel(ScriptInstance instance) => instance.SetFlag(m_ChasingSlot, false); Execute(ScriptInstance) Advances this action once when it is used where an ordinary block is expected, and discards the result because nothing at that position waits for one. public override void Execute(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Examples On.FrameUpdate(action); // one advance per frame, nothing waits for the result

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ActionRes.title: Enum ActionResult | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ActionRes.summary: Enum ActionResult Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What an action reports about the objective it was given: still pending, finished having met it, or finished having failed to meet it. public enum ActionResult Expand Details ... Fields Failed = 2 The action finished without meeting its objective. Running = 0 The objective is still pending; the owner advances this action again next frame. Succeeded = 1 The action finished and met its objective. Examples public override ActionResult Advance(ScriptInstance instance) => instance.GetNumber(m_RemainingSlot) > 0.0 ? ActionResult.Running : ActionResult.Succeeded; Remarks These are the three outcome words docs/execution-model.md accepts: Succeeded and Failed are the two natural finished outcomes and Running describes an objective still pending. An action reports Failed only through its own specified domain-failure behaviour; a C# exception thrown out of an action is not a Failed result, it is a contained action failure that stops the instance, and docs/execution-model.md, "Contained action failures", owns that path. Cancellation is not a member of this enum, deliberately. Cancellation interrupts work and is neither Succeeded nor Failed, so it is expressed by Cancel(ScriptInstance) rather than by a fourth result. How an interruption is represented to a script is open point G2 in docs/execution-model.md.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AdapterAd.title: Class AdapterAdmission | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AdapterAd.summary: Class AdapterAdmission Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The package and version admission table for extension blocks and optional adapters. public static class AdapterAdmission Expand Details ... Inheritance object AdapterAdmission Examples AdapterAdmission.Register(typeof(PuppetMasterDoSomethingBlock), "com.example.puppetmaster", "1.2.0", "PuppetMaster.LunyScript"); AdapterAdmission.NoteInstalled("com.example.puppetmaster", "1.4.0"); Remarks This is not a listing of the public API. The implementation queue called it a registration catalog. An adapter calls Register(Type, string, string, string, string, int) once per block type it adds, naming the Unity package and the minimum version that type needs. An author never writes a catalog line in Build(). Admission is checked at spawn, in the same ValidateCapabilities pass that already refuses a host that cannot provide the program's services. A missing package or a version older than the registered minimum raises LunyScriptUsageException and the instance is not created, so no registered block runs and no null-reference path is reached. The check is not on the per-frame path. The registered version is a minimum. An installed package newer than the declared version is admitted, including a later major such as Unity 7's 6.7.0 against a 1.8.0 minimum. That is the same rule Unity's versionDefines expression uses. Input and Cinemachine keep the provider-absence path they already have: their author-facing blocks live in core, and with no provider they report once and do nothing while the script still spawns. Do not register those core blocks here; this table is for extension block types the adapter itself adds. The dictionaries are readonly statics and this type is [NoAutoStaticsCleanup] because adapter assemblies register from a static constructor that does not run again when domain reload is off. Clearing the table on Play Mode exit would drop those registrations for the next Play session. Tests call Clear() between cases. Methods Clear() Drops every registration, every installed version and the replacement source. A test calls this between cases. Adapter assemblies register again after it if they still need to be admitted. public static void Clear() Examples AdapterAdmission.Clear(); NoteInstalled(string, string) Records that this project has packageId at version. An adapter that compiled because its package is present calls this next to Register(Type, string, string, string, string, int). public static void NoteInstalled(string packageId, string version) Parameters Type Name Description string packageId The Unity package id. string version The installed version string. Examples AdapterAdmission.NoteInstalled("com.example.puppetmaster", "1.4.0"); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException A parameter is missing or the version string is not numeric. Register(Type, string, string, string, string, int) Records that a block type needs a Unity package at a stated minimum version. The adapter assembly calls this once; a script's Build() does not. public static void Register(Type blockType, string packageId, string minimumVersion, string owner, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Type blockType The concrete IScriptNode type the adapter adds. string packageId The Unity package id, for example com.example.puppetmaster. string minimumVersion The lowest version that admits this type, for example 1.2.0. Newer installed versions are admitted. string owner The adapter that owns this type, usually its assembly name. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Examples AdapterAdmission.Register(typeof(PuppetMasterDoSomethingBlock), "com.example.puppetmaster", "1.2.0", "PuppetMaster.LunyScript"); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException A parameter is missing, the type is not a concrete LunyScript node, the version string is not numeric, or the same type was already registered with a different package, version or owner. TryGet(Type, out AdapterRegistration) The registration for blockType, if an adapter recorded one. public static bool TryGet(Type blockType, out AdapterRegistration registration) Parameters Type Name Description Type blockType The node type to look up. AdapterRegistration registration The recorded requirement when this method returns true. Returns bool True when this type was registered. Examples if (AdapterAdmission.TryGet(typeof(PuppetMasterDoSomethingBlock), out var registration)) Use(registration.PackageId); UseVersionSource(IPackageVersionSource) Replaces the installed-version map with source. A null source restores the map filled by NoteInstalled(string, string). public static void UseVersionSource(IPackageVersionSource source) Parameters Type Name Description IPackageVersionSource source The source to query at spawn, or null for the map. Examples AdapterAdmission.UseVersionSource(source);

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Anchor.ht.title: Enum Anchor | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Anchor.ht.summary: Enum Anchor Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One of the nine reserved HUD regions a Panel.Place call can occupy: four corners, four edges, and the centre. public enum Anchor Expand Details ... Fields Bottom = 7 The bottom-edge reserved region, centred on that edge. BottomLeft = 6 The lower-left reserved region. BottomRight = 8 The lower-right reserved region. Center = 4 The centre reserved region of the whole screen or of one view. Left = 3 The left-edge reserved region, centred on that edge. Right = 5 The right-edge reserved region, centred on that edge. Top = 1 The top-edge reserved region, centred on that edge. TopLeft = 0 The upper-left reserved region. TopRight = 2 The upper-right reserved region. Examples var portrait = Panel.Place(PlayerPortrait).At(Anchor.TopLeft); Remarks The name is interned onto the HUD template as the UXML name of that region, so TopLeft looks up the element named TopLeft. UXML and USS own the region's geometry; this enum only selects which named region receives the cloned tree.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Applicati.title: Enum ApplicationObservation | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Applicati.summary: Enum ApplicationObservation Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which of the five application observations a runner is delivering: what Unity reported about the application as a whole, rather than about one object. public enum ApplicationObservation Expand Details ... Fields FocusGained = 2 Unity reported focus gained: OnApplicationFocus(true). FocusLost = 3 Unity reported focus lost: OnApplicationFocus(false). Paused = 0 Unity reported the application paused: OnApplicationPause(true). Quitting = 4 Unity reported the application is quitting: OnApplicationQuit. Resumed = 1 Unity reported the application resumed: OnApplicationPause(false). Examples runner.RaiseApplication(ApplicationObservation.Paused); Remarks Unity's own callbacks carry a Boolean: OnApplicationPause(true) and OnApplicationPause(false) are one method. LunyScript splits each into its own event, the way On.Authority.Gained and On.Authority.Lost are two events, because a script registers blocks and has no parameter to test; AGENTS.md rule 26 keeps event payloads off the generic path.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Arithmeti.title: Enum ArithmeticOperator | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Arithmeti.summary: Enum ArithmeticOperator Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which arithmetic a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberArithmeticBlock performs. public enum ArithmeticOperator Expand Details ... Fields Add = 0 Left plus right. Divide = 3 Left divided by right. Division by zero produces the IEEE 754 result rather than throwing, which is what Double division does everywhere else. Multiply = 2 Left times right. Remainder = 4 What is left of left after taking out whole multiples of right, carrying left's sign. This is C#'s own % on Double, so a right of zero produces NaN rather than throwing. Subtract = 1 Left minus right.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Asset-1.h.title: Struct Asset<T> | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Asset-1.h.summary: Struct Asset<T> Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A handle to one asset input of a script. Returned by Bind.Asset at build time; reading the asset itself is an instance read, because the value belongs to the object and not to the script type. public readonly struct Asset<T> where T : Object Type Parameters T The Unity asset type this input accepts. An input declared as Asset<GameObject> cannot be satisfied by a Texture2D, in the Inspector or from a stored entry. Expand Details ... Examples [Asset] public Asset<AudioClip> OpenSound { get; private set; } var clip = behaviour.GetAsset(script.OpenSound); Remarks The handle is an index and a name, not a value: it says where the asset lives on every instance of the program, and the same handle reads a different object on every object running the script. The declared name is the input's durable identity. A value stored on a host is matched to an input by that name, which is why the name comes from nameof and why renaming a declared input orphans what a scene stored for the old name. A handle is valid only inside the Build that declared it, for the reason Var<T> states: it carries a slot index and nothing that identifies its program. Properties IsDeclared False for a handle Build() never assigned, which is what the unassigned-member check reads. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool Name The name the script declared, which is what a stored value is matched against and what a diagnostic names. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods ToString() The declared name and slot, for a log line or a failure message. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "OpenSound : AudioClip". Operators implicit operator AssetInput(Asset<T>) Takes this input where a surface accepts a declared input of any Unity type, such as the camera rig a view renders. public static implicit operator AssetInput(Asset<T> input) Parameters Type Name Description Asset<T> input The typed input. Returns AssetInput The same input with its type forgotten. Examples On.Ready(Camera.For(ChaseRig).Follow());

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetAttr.title: Class AssetAttribute | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetAttr.summary: Class AssetAttribute Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Declares an asset input whose handle is assigned before Build, in declaration order. [AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Property, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = false)] public sealed class AssetAttribute : Attribute Expand Details ... Inheritance object Attribute AssetAttribute Examples [Asset] public Asset<AudioClip> OpenSound { get; private set; } Remarks Place this on an Asset<T> property in a partial Script subclass. Roslyn reads the attribute at compile time; LunyScript never discovers or instantiates it at runtime. This is the same arrangement VariableAttribute uses, and the generated assignments run in one declaration pass before Build(). Remove the attribute and use Bind.Asset inside Build() to declare the same input explicitly. Constructors AssetAttribute() Declares an input the host supplies, with no source of its own. public AssetAttribute() Examples [Asset] public Asset<Texture2D> Banner { get; private set; } Properties Resources The Resources-relative, extension-free key this input loads from when the host assigns nothing. Naming the provider here is what keeps the source provider-qualified at the place it is written, which is what the settled api-asset-address-identity answer requires; no other provider is tried when this one finds nothing. public string Resources { get; set; } Property Value string Examples [Asset(Resources = "Enemies/Sentry")] public Asset<GameObject> Sentry { get; private set; }

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetFact.title: Struct AssetFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetFact.summary: Struct AssetFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Asset surface inside Build(): starts and ends content acquisitions. Unity owns the asset. LunyScript owns the attempt, the owner-acquisition, and consumer retention. public readonly struct AssetFactory Expand Details ... Examples EnemyContent = Operation.Define<Prefab>(nameof(EnemyContent)); On.Ready(Asset.Load(EnemyPrefab).As(EnemyContent)); When.Operation(EnemyContent).Succeeded(Object.Spawn(EnemyContent), Asset.Release(EnemyContent)); When.Operation(EnemyContent).Failed(ShowError.Set(true)); Remarks Asset.Load(source).As(handle) is asynchronous and binds the shipped operation-attempt surface. Asset.Release(acquisition) relinquishes this owner's hold. Bound consumers retain content they still need. Asset.Load does not load a scene. This factory coexists with the already-shipped Asset<T> handle, the way Task coexists with Task<T>. Methods Load(Prefab, string, int) Starts an asynchronous load of a declared prefab input. The object is already resident; the author observes When.Operation Succeeded with that reference as the payload. public AssetLoadBuilder Load(Prefab prefab, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Prefab prefab The declared prefab input. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns AssetLoadBuilder A builder whose As(handle) binds the attempt. Examples On.Ready(Asset.Load(EnemyPrefab).As(EnemyContent)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException prefab was never declared. Load<T>(AssetSource<T>, string, int) Starts an asynchronous load of a provider-qualified source. Must-have sources are a bound Inspector reference and AssetSource.Resources. A missing key is classified NotFound. A type mismatch is classified Denied. Failure does not fall through to an asset placeholder. public AssetLoadBuilder Load<T>(AssetSource<T> source, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where T : Object Parameters Type Name Description AssetSource<T> source The provider-qualified source. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns AssetLoadBuilder A builder whose As(handle) binds the attempt. Type Parameters T The Unity asset type the source produces. Examples On.Ready(Asset.Load(AssetSource.Resources<Texture2D>("UI/Portrait")).As(PortraitContent)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException source names no provider. Load<T>(Asset<T>, string, int) Starts an asynchronous load of a declared asset input. The object is already resident; the author observes Succeeded with that reference as the payload. Loading an input that resolved to an asset placeholder acquires that placeholder as content. public AssetLoadBuilder Load<T>(Asset<T> input, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where T : Object Parameters Type Name Description Asset<T> input The declared input. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns AssetLoadBuilder A builder whose As(handle) binds the attempt. Type Parameters T The Unity asset type the input was declared with. Examples On.Ready(Asset.Load(Banner).As(BannerContent)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException input was never declared. Release(Operation, string, int) Relinquishes this owner's acquisition. Bound consumers retain content they still need. Release does not destroy them and does not promise immediate physical reclamation. public Block Release(Operation acquisition, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Operation acquisition The handle a successful Asset.Load(...).As bound. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples When.Operation(EnemyContent).Succeeded(Object.Spawn(EnemyContent), Asset.Release(EnemyContent)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle was never declared. Release<T>(Operation<T>, string, int) Relinquishes this owner's typed acquisition. Same behaviour as Release(Operation, string, int). public Block Release<T>(Operation<T> acquisition, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Operation<T> acquisition The typed handle. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Type Parameters T The result type stored on the handle. Examples When.Operation(EnemyContent).Succeeded(Asset.Release(EnemyContent));

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetGate.title: Class AssetGateway | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetGate.summary: Class AssetGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Owns in-flight Asset.Load attempts and owner-acquisition records for one ScriptRunner. Bound Inspector loads complete from the instance's already resolved input. Resources loads go through IAssetLoadProvider. Script code never sees a Task or an exception type; AGENTS.md rules 50 and 51. public sealed class AssetGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object AssetGateway Examples runner.AssetGateway.UseProvider(new FakeAssetLoadProvider()); Remarks A start may allocate. A tick that only polls, and a tick with nothing in flight, allocate nothing; AGENTS.md rule 31 applied to this gateway. Asset.Release drops this owner's hold. Bound consumers keep the payload until their own end. Release does not call Resources.UnloadAsset: physical unload is not the success condition. A late native completion whose generation is no longer current is discarded from the handle. Host cleanup of that Unity-held object is not this tier. Properties HasProvider Whether a Resources-style provider has been named. Bound Inspector loads do not need one. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool Methods Tick() Polls once. Called by the runner before any instance runs, so a completion is observed in the same frame the watches that react to it run in. With nothing in flight this returns immediately and allocates nothing. public void Tick() UseProvider(IAssetLoadProvider) Names the backend Resources loads talk to. Bound Inspector loads ignore it. public void UseProvider(IAssetLoadProvider provider) Parameters Type Name Description IAssetLoadProvider provider The backend. Examples runner.AssetGateway.UseProvider(new ResourcesAssetLoadProvider()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException provider is null, or a provider was already named.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetInpu.title: Struct AssetInput | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetInpu.summary: Struct AssetInput Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One declared asset input with its type forgotten: what a surface takes when it accepts an input of any Unity type, such as the camera rig a view renders. public readonly struct AssetInput Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Camera.For(ChaseRig).Follow(Avatar)); Remarks An Asset<T> converts to one of these on its own, so a script writes Camera.For(ChaseRig) and never names this type. It exists because the surfaces that take an object rather than an asset - a view, a camera rig, something a camera tracks - accept whichever Unity type the author declared, and a generic parameter on every one of those members would buy nothing: the type is not what they check, the backend is. The declared type is still enforced where it matters, when the object spawns: Asset<T> is what the Inspector draws a field of, and a stored value of another type is refused there. This conversion forgets the type after that check has already happened. Properties IsDeclared False for an input Build() never assigned. public bool IsDeclared { get; } Property Value bool Name The name the script declared. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods ToString() The declared name, for a diagnostic. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "ChaseRig".

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetInpu.title: Struct AssetInputAssignment | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetInpu.summary: Struct AssetInputAssignment Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One row of the declared-input table a host component serializes: the name of a declared input and the asset this object assigns to it. [Serializable] public struct AssetInputAssignment Expand Details ... Examples var row = new AssetInputAssignment(nameof(GateScript.OpenSound), clip); Remarks The row carries the name and not the declaration's position, because the settled api-asset-inspector-binding-mechanism-identity answer makes the declared name the durable identity. Reordering the declarations in a script therefore keeps every scene's assignments, and renaming one leaves the row addressing a name nothing declares any more. It is a struct so that the serialized array costs one allocation rather than one per row, and its fields are serialized by name, which is why they are read through NameFieldName and AssetFieldName rather than by a literal written a second time. Constructors AssetInputAssignment(string, Object) Creates one row. public AssetInputAssignment(string name, Object asset) Parameters Type Name Description string name The declared input's name. Object asset The asset assigned to it. Examples new AssetInputAssignment("OpenSound", clip); Fields AssetFieldName The serialized field holding the assigned asset. public const string AssetFieldName = "m_Asset" Field Value string Examples entry.FindPropertyRelative(AssetInputAssignment.AssetFieldName); NameFieldName The serialized field holding the declared input's name. public const string NameFieldName = "m_Name" Field Value string Examples entry.FindPropertyRelative(AssetInputAssignment.NameFieldName); Properties Asset The asset assigned, which can be null for a row nobody filled in. public Object Asset { get; } Property Value Object Name Which declared input this row assigns. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods ToString() The name and what it holds, for a log line. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "OpenSound = DoorOpen".

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetLoad.title: Class AssetLoadBlock | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetLoad.summary: Class AssetLoadBlock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Asset.Load(source).As(handle) builds: starts one asynchronous content acquisition bound to an operation handle. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetPlac.title: Class AssetPlaceholders | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.AssetPlac.summary: Class AssetPlaceholders Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The asset placeholder every asset type falls back to when an input of that type is left unassigned, and the two ways one is configured. public static class AssetPlaceholders Expand Details ... Inheritance object AssetPlaceholders Examples AssetPlaceholders.Register<Texture2D>(myPlaceholderTexture); Remarks An unassigned binding must not enter execution as a null reference. That is the settled requirement; the placeholder is chosen to be recognisable and to change no gameplay outcome, and using one is always reported so that a placeholder never hides the missing assignment. Where no placeholder can be both recognisable and harmless, the type gets none and the binding fails instead. This is not Unity's Preset feature. A Unity Preset stores Inspector settings and applies them to filtered assets; an asset placeholder is the object a declared [Asset] input resolves to when no assigned asset is available. A placeholder is built the first time a type actually needs one, and then kept. A scene in which every input is assigned builds none of them, which is why the built-in registrations are factories rather than objects. This is mutable static state, and it carries the attribute that resets it. AGENTS.md rule 17 forbids one and rule 18 names [AutoStaticsCleanup] as the mechanism for the unavoidable case: with domain reload disabled a static keeps its value from the previous Play session, and a placeholder built in that session is a destroyed object by the time the next one reads it. The type is partial because Unity's code generator emits a second partial declaration holding the generated reset method. A registration a package makes in code is re-applied after that reset the way it was applied the first time, from a startup callback. The project settings asset the accepted design names as the second configuration source is not implemented yet; AssetPlaceholderSource is where it joins, and every diagnostic already names the source it came from. Called at most once per declared type. Type Parameters T The asset type the placeholder applies to. Examples AssetPlaceholders.Register<Mesh>(_ => BuildPlaceholderMesh()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException factory is null. Register<T>(T) Registers one object as the asset placeholder for a type, replacing the built-in placeholder. public static void Register<T>(T placeholder) where T : Object Parameters Type Name Description T placeholder The object an unassigned input of that type resolves to. Type Parameters T The asset type the placeholder applies to. Examples AssetPlaceholders.Register<AudioClip>(placeholderBeep); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException placeholder is null. Removing a placeholder is Clear<T>(), so that a null cannot pass for an intention. ResetToBuiltIn() Drops every registration and every placeholder built so far, so the next caller starts from the built-in set. A test calls this between cases. public static void ResetToBuiltIn() Examples AssetPlaceholders.ResetToBuiltIn(); SourceFor(Type) Whether a type has an asset placeholder at all, without building one. public static AssetPlaceholderSource SourceFor(Type declaredType) Parameters Type Name Description Type declaredType The type an input declared. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Block.htm.summary: Class Block Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One step of behaviour in a script. A block object is created once, when its script type is built, and is then shared by every object running that script; the per-object state it reads and writes lives in slots on the ScriptInstance passed to Execute(ScriptInstance). public abstract class Block : IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object Block Implements IScriptNode Derived ActionBlock ActivateObjectBlock AssetLoadBlock AssetReleaseBlock CreateObjectBlock DeactivateObjectBlock DespawnObjectBlock SpawnObjectBlock Examples public sealed class SetNumberBlock : Block { private readonly NumberSlot m_Slot; public override void Execute(ScriptInstance instance) => instance.SetNumber(m_Slot, 1.0); } Remarks Every field of every block is readonly, and a structural test enforces it, because one tree serves every object running the script and a mutable field would be shared state across all of them. AGENTS.md rule 22. A block holds slot handles, literals and child block arrays, and nothing else: no List, no Dictionary, no cached host and no cached component. Constructors Block(SourceLocation) Creates a block that knows where it was authored. protected Block(SourceLocation location = default) Parameters Type Name Description SourceLocation location Where the factory that built it was called, or Unknown when the builder is an operator that cannot capture one. The parameter is optional so that a block whose builder has no location to give needs no constructor initialiser at all. Fields None An empty block list. A shared readonly array, so an If with no Else costs no allocation and needs no null check on the run-time path. public static readonly Block[] None Field Value Block[] Remarks A field rather than a static auto-property, because Unity's lifecycle analyzer asks every type with a static auto-property to carry an [AutoStaticsCleanup] or [NoAutoStaticsCleanup] attribute, and a zero-length shared array needs neither. Properties Contexts Legacy custom nodes are runtime-only until explicitly declared shared or Editor-only. public virtual ScriptContexts Contexts { get; } Property Value ScriptContexts Examples public override ScriptContexts Contexts => ScriptContexts.Shared; Location Where in the user's script this block was authored, captured when it was built. public SourceLocation Location { get; } Property Value SourceLocation Examples var where = block.Location.Describe(); // "Assets/Scripts/CountdownScript.cs:12" Remarks This is the only place a block's own source line can come from. A block is composed inside Build() and executed much later by ScriptRunner, so at the moment it logs or throws the user's line is not on the call stack at all; the factory method that built it captured the line with [CallerFilePath] and [CallerLineNumber] and handed it here. SourceLocation states what that costs, which is one reference and one int per block and no allocation. A block built by a C# operator, such as the NumberArithmeticBlock behind health + 1.0, carries Unknown: an operator cannot declare the optional parameters the caller attributes need. The block that consumes such an expression carries the location instead. RequiredServices Services this node requires in addition to its children's requirements. public virtual ScriptServices RequiredServices { get; } Property Value ScriptServices Examples public override ScriptServices RequiredServices => ScriptServices.Clock; Methods AdvanceContained(ActionBlock, ScriptInstance) Advances one action inside the same per-action containment boundary ExecuteAll(Block[], ScriptInstance) uses, and hands its result back to the routine or group that owns it. public static ActionResult AdvanceContained(ActionBlock action, ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ActionBlock action The action to advance once. ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Returns ActionResult What the action reported. Examples var result = Block.AdvanceContained(child, instance); Remarks A result and a failure are different things and this is where they separate: an action reports Failed through its own specified domain-failure behaviour, while an exception thrown out of it is attributed here and propagated to the runner's boundary, which stops the instance. docs/execution-model.md, "Contained action failures". DescribeChildren(NodeDescription) Declares composed children during Build. Custom composite nodes override this method. public virtual void DescribeChildren(NodeDescription description) Parameters Type Name Description NodeDescription description Examples description.Add("Child", child); Execute(ScriptInstance) Runs this block against one object's state. Called once per event per instance and must allocate nothing after warm-up; AGENTS.md rule 29. public abstract void Execute(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. ExecuteAll(Block[], ScriptInstance) Runs a list of blocks in order. The one place every composite block iterates its children, so that iteration is written once for all of them. public static void ExecuteAll(Block[] blocks, ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] blocks The blocks to run, in order. ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Examples Block.ExecuteAll(m_ThenBlocks, instance); Remarks Event lists and composite child lists use the same per-action containment boundary. An action failure stops the instance at its runner boundary; prior writes are retained.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CameraFac.summary: Struct CameraFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Camera surface inside Build(): what one camera rig tracks. It hides UnityEngine.Camera inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. public readonly struct CameraFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Camera.For(ChaseRig).Follow()); Remarks A rig is an authored Cinemachine configuration and this surface does not replace it. Framing, damping, noise and collision stay in the rig the author set up; what a script writes is which objects the rig tracks. That is what the captain's answer on the camera family requires: the camera is routed through Cinemachine rather than reimplemented over it. Follow and look-at are two targets, not one. A chase camera keeps its position relative to the car it follows and aims at the corner ahead of it, so a rig carries both and each is written on its own. This surface's shape is provisional, for the reason ViewFactory states: it implements the recorded recommendation of the open decision contract-view-routing. Returns CameraRigBuilder A builder whose members produce the blocks. Examples On.Ready(Camera.For(ChaseRig).LookAt(Marker)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle is one Build() never assigned, or this factory was not obtained inside Build().

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CameraGat.summary: Class CameraGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core's one entry point to the camera. Owns the ICameraProvider, passes each authored operation to it, and reports a refused one once. public sealed class CameraGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object CameraGateway Examples runner.CameraGateway.UseProvider(new FakeCameraProvider()); Remarks This is the camera counterpart of NetworkGateway and InputGateway and is the same shape for the same reason: the core may not reference Cinemachine, so the core owns an interface and a separate, package-gated assembly implements it. With no provider installed, a camera block writes nothing and says so once. That is what the accepted design asks of an absent optional adapter: a diagnostic, and no block executes. A project without the Cinemachine package therefore still builds, still runs and still passes its tests; the camera operations do nothing and the reason is in the Console. A refusal is reported once per operation per object pair. These operations are normally authored in On.Ready, but nothing stops one appearing in On.FrameUpdate, and a Console line per frame would bury the one that matters. The bookkeeping allocates only on the failure path, which is not the steady state. Properties HasProvider Whether a camera adapter has been installed. False means every camera operation writes nothing. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool Methods ChangeTargetGroup(Object, CameraTargetOperation, Object, double, double, string, string) Changes a rig's group of tracked objects, reporting a refusal once. public CameraOperationResult ChangeTargetGroup(Object rig, CameraTargetOperation operation, Object target, double weight, double radius, string call, string scriptTypeName) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The camera rig. CameraTargetOperation operation What to do to the group. Object target The object the operation acts on. double weight How much it pulls the framing. double radius How much room to leave around it. string call How the authored call is written, for the diagnostic. The block passes the constant it was built with; composing one here allocated three events per call on the frame path, which AGENTS.md rule 29 forbids and ExecutionCoreAllocationTests.EveryBlock_AllocatesNothingWhenItRuns caught. string scriptTypeName Whose script asked, for the diagnostic. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Examples gateway.ChangeTargetGroup(rig, CameraTargetOperation.Add, avatar, 1.0, 0.5, "Camera.For(...).Targets.Add", "ArenaScript"); SetTracking(Object, CameraTracking, Object, string, string) Writes one of a rig's two tracking targets, reporting a refusal once. public CameraOperationResult SetTracking(Object rig, CameraTracking tracking, Object target, string call, string scriptTypeName) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The camera rig. CameraTracking tracking Which of the two. Object target The object to track, or null to stop tracking. string call How the authored call is written, for the diagnostic. The block passes the constant it was built with, so nothing here composes a string on the frame path. string scriptTypeName Whose script asked, for the diagnostic. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Examples gateway.SetTracking(rig, CameraTracking.Follow, avatar, "Camera.For(...).Follow", "ChaseScript"); SetViewCamera(Object, Object, string) Makes a view render one camera rig, reporting a refusal once. public CameraOperationResult SetViewCamera(Object view, Object rig, string scriptTypeName) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view the author assigned. Object rig The rig to make active. string scriptTypeName Whose script asked, for the diagnostic. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Examples gateway.SetViewCamera(view, rig, "ChaseScript"); SetViewport(Object, double, double, double, double, string) Sets the fraction of the screen a view occupies, reporting a refusal once. public CameraOperationResult SetViewport(Object view, double x, double y, double width, double height, string scriptTypeName) Parameters Type Name Description Object view The view the author assigned. double x The left edge. double y The bottom edge. double width How much of the width. double height How much of the height. string scriptTypeName Whose script asked, for the diagnostic. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Examples gateway.SetViewport(view, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 0.5, "SplitScreenScript"); UseProvider(ICameraProvider) Installs the backend. public void UseProvider(ICameraProvider provider) Parameters Type Name Description ICameraProvider provider The backend. Null is the caller's mistake. Examples runner.CameraGateway.UseProvider(new FakeCameraProvider()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The provider is null.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CameraOpe.summary: Enum CameraOperationResult Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What happened when the camera gateway asked its provider to do something. public enum CameraOperationResult Expand Details ... Fields Done = 0 The provider did it. NoProvider = 1 No camera adapter is installed, so nothing was done. NoSuchTarget = 5 The object the operation names is not in the rig's target group. NoTarget = 6 The operation needs an object to act on and was given none. NoTargetGroup = 4 The rig carries no target group, so the group operation had nothing to act on. NotACameraRig = 3 The object given as the camera rig is not one, so nothing was done. NotAView = 2 The object given as the view is not one, so nothing was done. NotOnThisViewsChannel = 7 The rig is on an output channel this view does not listen to, so selecting it would not change what the view renders. Examples if (result != CameraOperationResult.Done) Report(...); Remarks Every value but Done is reported once, naming the operation and the object, and nothing is written. A camera operation is refused rather than approximated, because a view pointed at the wrong rig is a defect a player sees and cannot explain.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Cinemachi.title: Class CinemachineCameraProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Cinemachi.summary: Class CinemachineCameraProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Cinemachine Assembly ApiSource.dll The camera backend that drives Cinemachine. The one place in the product that references the Cinemachine package. public sealed class CinemachineCameraProvider : ICameraProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object CinemachineCameraProvider Implements ICameraProvider Examples runner.CameraGateway.UseProvider(new CinemachineCameraProvider()); Remarks This assembly compiles only when the Cinemachine package is installed. Its assembly definition carries a version define, LUNY_CINEMACHINE from com.unity.cinemachine 3.0.0 or newer, and a matching define constraint, which is the same arrangement CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode uses for Netcode for GameObjects and CodeSmile.LunyScript.Services uses for Unity Gaming Services. With the package absent the assembly is not compiled, nothing references this type, and the core's CameraGateway has no provider, so every camera block writes nothing and says so once. Nothing here reimplements a camera. Framing, damping, noise, blending and collision stay in the rig the author configured; this provider writes which rig a view renders and what a rig tracks, and Cinemachine does the rest. That is what the captain's answer on the camera family requires. Selecting a rig is Prioritize(), which keeps the authored blend. Cinemachine's brain renders the highest-priority camera on an output channel it listens to, and the transition into it is the blend the author configured. A rig on a channel the view's brain does not listen to is reported rather than silently having no effect. Object target The object the operation acts on, ignored by Clear. double weight How much the object pulls the framing towards itself, used by Add and SetWeight. double radius How much room the framing leaves around the object, used by Add and SetRadius. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. SetTracking(Object, CameraTracking, Object) Writes one of a rig's two tracking targets. public CameraOperationResult SetTracking(Object rig, CameraTracking tracking, Object target) Parameters Type Name Description Object rig The camera rig. CameraTracking tracking Which of the two to write. Object target The object to track, or null to stop tracking. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Object rig The camera rig to make active for that view. Returns CameraOperationResult What happened. Nothing is written unless this is Done. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CloudFact.summary: Struct CloudFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Cloud surface inside Build(): builds the start blocks for Cloud Save. A start block enqueues and returns in the same call; the outcome arrives through When.Cloud(key). AGENTS.md rule 50. public readonly struct CloudFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Cloud.Load("progress")); When.Cloud("progress").Loaded(progress, Cloud.Save("progress", progress + 1.0)); Remarks Sign-in is the gateway's job, not the script's: the first request starts it, and requests made before the service is ready are queued, not thrown; AGENTS.md rule 51. Values are Number in this version; docs/proposals/slice-transform-and-cloud.md states the surface and what it defers. Methods Load(string, string, int) Builds a block that starts loading a key's value. The value arrives through When.Cloud(key).Loaded(into, ...); a missing key fails as NotFound through When.Cloud(key).Failed. public Block Load(string key, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string key The key. Validated here, at build time. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; see Save(string, NumberValueBlock, string, int). int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Ready(Cloud.Load("progress")); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException key is null or whitespace. Save(string, NumberValueBlock, string, int) Builds a block that starts saving a value under a key. public Block Save(string key, NumberValueBlock value, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string key The key. Validated here, at build time. NumberValueBlock value The value to store, evaluated each time the block runs, so saving a variable saves what it holds at that moment. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. It records the line this block was written on, so a later failure names that line rather than LunyScript's own source. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples When.Var(score).Changed(Cloud.Save("score", score)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException key is null or whitespace, or value is null.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CloudSave.title: Class CloudSaveGateway | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.CloudSave.summary: Class CloudSaveGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Owns every in-flight Cloud Save request for one ScriptRunner, keyed by the save key. Signs in when the first request arrives, queues requests made before the service is ready, coalesces duplicates, polls each operation once per frame, and classifies every failure once into an OperationFailure. No script and no block ever sees a Task or an exception type; AGENTS.md section 12. public sealed class CloudSaveGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object CloudSaveGateway Examples var runner = new ScriptRunner(); runner.CloudGateway.UseProvider(new FileCloudSaveProvider(directory)); Remarks Coalescing, stated exactly. A save enqueued while one is in flight for the same key keeps the latest value and issues one follow-up save when the in-flight one completes, so a script that saves every frame produces one request at a time rather than one per frame. A load enqueued while one is pending for the same key joins it and starts nothing. The pending path allocates nothing per frame. A request allocates when it is made and when its operation starts, which is the boundary AGENTS.md rule 31 names; a tick that only polls allocates nothing, and a tick with no provider or no requests returns immediately. Outcomes are counters, read by the When.Cloud(key) watch blocks. Each completion advances the key's saved, loaded or failed counter; a watch block compares the counter against a shadow variable once per frame, the same polling shape When.Var(x).Changed has. A failed sign-in fails every queued request once, and every request made after it fails immediately with the sign-in's classified reason; there is no retry in this version, and docs/slice-decisions.md records that decision. Properties HasProvider Whether a provider has been named. Requests made while this is false are queued, not thrown; AGENTS.md rule 51. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool IsReady Whether sign-in has completed successfully, so requests dispatch immediately. public bool IsReady { get; } Property Value bool Methods EnqueueLoad(string) Enqueues one load. Returns in the same call; the value arrives through When.Cloud(key).Loaded(into, ...), and a missing key fails as OperationFailure.NotFound. public void EnqueueLoad(string key) Parameters Type Name Description string key The key, validated at build time by the block that calls this. Examples gateway.EnqueueLoad("progress"); EnqueueSave(string, double) Enqueues one save. Returns in the same call; the outcome arrives through the key's counters, which When.Cloud(key).Saved and .Failed watch. public void EnqueueSave(string key, double value) Parameters Type Name Description string key The key, validated at build time by the block that calls this. double value The value to store. Examples gateway.EnqueueSave("progress", 12.0); Tick() Polls once. Called by TickFrameUpdate() before any instance runs, so a completion is observed in the same frame the watches that react to it run in. With no provider or nothing in flight this returns immediately and allocates nothing. public void Tick() Examples gateway.Tick(); Remarks A throwing provider cannot leave this method. Every call this gateway makes into ICloudSaveProvider and into the operations a provider returns is guarded, and a caught exception becomes OperationFailure.Unknown on the operation it belongs to, logged once with the original exception text. See the comment on TickSignIn for why. A provider that returns no operation loses no request. A null is classified as OperationFailure.Unknown and logged once, so When.Cloud(key).Failed fires rather than nothing happening. Which records it is counted on follows the operation. A null from Save(string, double) or Load(string) reaches RecordMissingOperation and is counted once on that one key's record. A null from SignIn() reaches EndSignInAsFailed and then FailAllQueued and FailImmediately, so it is counted on every queued key's record rather than on one key's, the way a sign-in that failed is; docs/slice-decisions.md D5.16. UseProvider(ICloudSaveProvider) Names the backend this gateway talks to. Called once, by whoever owns the runner, before or after the first request; requests made before it are queued and dispatched once sign-in completes. public void UseProvider(ICloudSaveProvider provider) Parameters Type Name Description ICloudSaveProvider provider The backend. Examples LunyScriptRuntime.DefaultRunner.CloudGateway.UseProvider(new UgsCloudSaveProvider()); Remarks The only provider code this method calls is Describe(), to name the provider in its log line and in that exception's message, and it is guarded: a provider whose Describe throws is named by its type instead, and the exception does not leave this method. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException provider is null. LunyScriptUsageException A provider was already named. A gateway talks to one backend for its lifetime; with domain reload disabled the default runner and its gateway are reset between Play sessions, so each session names its provider once.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Compariso.title: Enum ComparisonOperator | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Compariso.summary: Enum ComparisonOperator Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which comparison a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberComparisonBlock performs. public enum ComparisonOperator Expand Details ... Fields Equal = 4 Left equals right. Compares two Double values exactly; see docs/execution-model.md on why exact comparison is what the API offers and what a user should write instead when a tolerance is wanted. Greater = 0 Left is greater than right. GreaterOrEqual = 1 Left is greater than or equal to right. Less = 2 Left is less than right. LessOrEqual = 3 Left is less than or equal to right. NotEqual = 5 Left does not equal right. Remarks The operator is a literal field on the block rather than six separate block types, because "compare two numbers" is one behaviour with a parameter; AGENTS.md rule 22 allows a literal as a block field.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Condition.title: Class ConditionBlock | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Condition.summary: Class ConditionBlock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A block that answers true or false for one object. Passed to If(...) and combined with &, | and !. public abstract class ConditionBlock : IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object ConditionBlock Implements IScriptNode Examples If(health > 10 & Alive).Then(...) If(health > 10 && Alive).Then(...) Remarks operator true and operator false return false, in every build. C# implements && and || with those operators. Returning false makes both sides of those spellings run, so they construct the same AND and OR nodes as & and |. Evaluation still short-circuits at run time. AGENTS.md rule 39. A C# if or while around a condition block still throws, in release builds too: that path uses the implicit conversion to bool, which always raises LunyScriptUsageException. There is no #if DEBUG anywhere in this file. AGENTS.md rule 38. The release-gate player asserts that throw. Fields OperatorMisuseMessage The message the implicit bool conversion carries. Named so a test can assert on it without repeating the wording. public const string OperatorMisuseMessage = "a LunyScript condition block was used in a C# if or while. Pass it to If(...) instead, combine conditions with &, |, && or ||, and negate one with !." Field Value string Properties Contexts Legacy custom nodes are runtime-only until explicitly declared shared or Editor-only. public virtual ScriptContexts Contexts { get; } Property Value ScriptContexts Examples public override ScriptContexts Contexts => ScriptContexts.Shared; RequiredServices Services this node requires in addition to its children's requirements. public virtual ScriptServices RequiredServices { get; } Property Value ScriptServices Examples public override ScriptServices RequiredServices => ScriptServices.Clock; Methods DescribeChildren(NodeDescription) Declares composed children during Build. Custom composite nodes override this method. public virtual void DescribeChildren(NodeDescription description) Parameters Type Name Description NodeDescription description Examples description.Add("Child", child); Evaluate(ScriptInstance) Answers the condition for one object. Called once per evaluation per instance and must allocate nothing after warm-up; AGENTS.md rule 29. public abstract bool Evaluate(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Returns bool What the condition says about this object right now. Operators operator &(ConditionBlock, ConditionBlock) Builds a condition that is true when both are true. public static ConditionBlock operator &(ConditionBlock left, ConditionBlock right) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock left The first condition. ConditionBlock right The second condition. Returns ConditionBlock A block evaluating both. Examples If(health > 10 & alive.IsTrue()).Then(...) operator |(ConditionBlock, ConditionBlock) Builds a condition that is true when either is true. public static ConditionBlock operator |(ConditionBlock left, ConditionBlock right) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock left The first condition. ConditionBlock right The second condition. Returns ConditionBlock A block evaluating both. Examples If(health < 1 | alive.IsFalse()).Then(...) operator false(ConditionBlock) Always false. Present for the same reason as operator true; C# requires the pair, and && and || are implemented with this one. public static bool operator false(ConditionBlock condition) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The block C# asked about. Not used. Returns bool False. implicit operator bool(ConditionBlock) Always throws. Present so that a condition block used in a C# if or while fails loudly instead of testing as false. public static implicit operator bool(ConditionBlock condition) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The block C# tried to test. Returns bool Never returns. Examples if (health > 10) { } // throws LunyScriptUsageException If(health > 10).Then(...) // the supported form Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Always, in every build configuration. operator !(ConditionBlock) Builds a condition that is true when this one is false. public static ConditionBlock operator !(ConditionBlock condition) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The condition to invert. Returns ConditionBlock A block evaluating the inverse. Examples If(!(health > 10)).Then(...) operator true(ConditionBlock) Always false. Present so && and || construct both sides. public static bool operator true(ConditionBlock condition) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The block C# asked about. Not used. Returns bool False, so C# always evaluates the other operand and calls & or |. Examples If(health > 10 && Alive).Then(...)

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeNetwo.title: Class FakeNetworkProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FakeNetwo.summary: Class FakeNetworkProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A netcode backend that runs entirely in this process, with no network, no Editor and no Netcode for GameObjects. Two instances are paired with Pair(out FakeNetworkProvider, out FakeNetworkProvider) and each one's sends arrive in the other's queues. public sealed class FakeNetworkProvider : INetworkProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object FakeNetworkProvider Implements INetworkProvider Examples FakeNetworkProvider.Pair(out var host, out var client); gateway.UseProvider(host); host.StartHost(); Remarks This is a second real implementation, not a mock. It is the netcode counterpart of FileCloudSaveProvider, which AGENTS.md rule 52 makes a first-class part of the product because it is how every branch is tested without a service. The message and cadence tests run against this provider with no network and no Editor session, and the same behaviour is exercised against NgoNetworkProvider where a real session is available. TestKit.NetworkProviderConformance is the one list of assertions both providers are held to, so that the double cannot drift from the backend without a test saying so. Authority here is ownership, which is the distributed-authority meaning. Each object is owned by exactly one peer, set with SetAuthority(int, int). That is the default topology under AGENTS.md rule 44, and a script written against Net.HasAuthority reads the same under either. Delivery is immediate and ordered. A send lands in the peer's queue before the call returns, so a test observes it on the next drain with no waiting and no frames. That makes the tests deterministic; it also means this provider cannot reproduce a latency or reordering defect, and a test that needs those needs the real provider. Fields NoPracticalLimit What MaximumTransformStreamBytes reports unless a test lowers it. Large enough that a thousand objects fit in one stream. public const int NoPracticalLimit = 1048576 Field Value int Properties IsHost True when this peer is the host. False for a client and for no session at all. Exposed because rule 45 forbids hiding it, and because "works as host, breaks as client" is the defect that hiding it produces. public bool IsHost { get; } Property Value bool MaximumTransformStreamBytes How many payload bytes of transform stream this backend can carry in one send. The runner splits a tick's stream into as many sends as it needs to stay inside it. public int MaximumTransformStreamBytes { get; set; } Property Value int Remarks A transport carries a bounded message. One stream per authority per tick is what AGENTS.md rule 47 requires and it stays true here: the tick still produces one stream, and this is how many bytes of it fit in one message. A hundred objects sending all three channels is about 1800 bytes, which is past what Netcode for GameObjects carries unfragmented, so this is not a limit only an unusual session meets. Splitting rather than asking the backend to fragment is deliberate. Each piece carries the stream's own 3-byte header and is decoded on its own, so a piece costs about 3 bytes plus whatever the backend's own per-message header is; a fragmented message costs the backend's fragment headers and its reassembly state instead, and leaves the stream depending on a feature that differs between backends. PeerCount How many peers are in the session, including this one. Zero when offline. public int PeerCount { get; } Property Value int PeerId Which peer this is. The host is 0 and the joining peer is 1, fixed so a test can name an owner without first reading it back. public int PeerId { get; } Property Value int RoundTripMilliseconds Round trip time to the host in milliseconds, or 0 when offline or when this peer is the host. Latency is a state a script may read, not an error; AGENTS.md rule 45. public double RoundTripMilliseconds { get; } Property Value double Remarks Zero unless this peer is in a session and is not the host, which is the same shape NgoNetworkProvider reports: a peer with no session has no round trip to report, and the host's round trip to itself is zero. SimulatedRoundTripMilliseconds How many milliseconds this provider reports as round trip time. Settable so a test can assert that a script reads latency as a state rather than as an error; it does not delay anything, because delivery here is immediate. public double SimulatedRoundTripMilliseconds { get; set; } Property Value double State What the session is doing right now. Never throws and is meaningful before any session has been started. public SessionState State { get; } Property Value SessionState TransformStreamBytesSent How many payload bytes those delivered streams carried in total. Returned to zero by EndSession() with TransformStreamsSent. public long TransformStreamBytesSent { get; } Property Value long TransformStreamsSent How many transform streams this peer has delivered since the session started. EndSession() returns it to zero, so it reads per session and not per instance. public int TransformStreamsSent { get; } Property Value int Remarks Counted here rather than only in a test, because the number of streams and the bytes in them are what AGENTS.md rule 47 is about, and a figure that can only be measured with a network is a figure nobody measures. These two count the stream's own payload; what a real backend adds around it is measured at the transport, which is what docs/netcode-bandwidth.md records. Only a delivered stream is counted, which is what NgoNetworkProvider counts too: a call made while this provider has no session, or with no connected peer to receive it, is not a send and does not move either figure. The two providers implement one documented property and a reading that meant different things on each would be worse than either meaning. Methods Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines, so a reader of the Console can tell a real session from the in-process one. Allocates; called only at state transitions, never per tick. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Netcode for GameObjects, host on port 7777", or "in-process provider, 2 peers". EndSession() Ends the session and returns to Offline. Called again on an already-offline provider, it does nothing, so that a restart is EndSession then StartHost without the caller tracking state. public void EndSession() HasAuthority(int) Whether this peer may write the state of one object. public bool HasAuthority(int objectId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The networked object, as the gateway numbers it. Returns bool True when this peer owns the object under distributed authority, or is the server under client-server. False when offline, because an offline peer has no authority to speak of and a script that guards on authority then does nothing rather than misbehaving. Pair(out FakeNetworkProvider, out FakeNetworkProvider) Builds two providers that deliver to each other, one host and one client, both still offline until their session is started. public static void Pair(out FakeNetworkProvider host, out FakeNetworkProvider client) Parameters Type Name Description FakeNetworkProvider host The peer that will host. Peer id 0. FakeNetworkProvider client The peer that will join. Peer id 1. SendToAuthority(int, int) Sends one message to whichever peer holds authority over the object. The message has a name and no payload in this milestone. public void SendToAuthority(int objectId, int messageId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the message is about. int messageId The message, interned by the gateway so no string crosses this call. Remarks Delivered only while this peer is in a session, and to another peer only while that peer is in one too, which is what NgoNetworkProvider does: it refuses an unconnected session and then sends over a transport that reaches connected clients only. A message left in an unstarted peer's queue would run the moment it joined, which no real session does. SendTransformStream(byte[], int) Sends one authority's whole transform stream for one network tick. public void SendTransformStream(byte[] payload, int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The buffer the runner encoded the stream into. The provider must copy what it needs before returning, because the runner reuses this buffer next tick. int length How many bytes of it the stream occupies. Remarks One call per authority per tick, carrying every object that authority has something to send for, rather than one call per object. AGENTS.md rule 47 requires that shape, because one message per object per tick spends about as many bytes on framing as a half-precision position costs. SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) Sends one variable's value to every other peer. Called only by the authority, and only when the variable's cadence says to send. public void SendVariable(int objectId, int variableIndex, in NetworkValue value) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the variable belongs to. int variableIndex Which synchronised variable, numbered by the order the script declared it in. See VariableIndex for why this is not a slot index. NetworkValue value The value to send. Remarks Delivered only to a peer that is in a session, which is the condition SendToAuthority(int, int) and SendTransformStream(byte[], int) apply too, and the one NgoNetworkProvider applies to all three of its send paths. An update handed to a peer that has not joined would be drained by it the moment it did, delivering a value no real session would have carried and hiding whether the join resend that is supposed to carry it works. SetAuthority(int, int) Says which peer owns one object, on both providers at once so the two never disagree about authority. public void SetAuthority(int objectId, int ownerPeerId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object. int ownerPeerId Which peer owns it. StartClient(string) Joins a session. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running. public void StartClient(string address) Parameters Type Name Description string address Where to connect. An implementation that needs no address ignores it. StartHost() Starts hosting. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running, so an implementation may assume it is offline. public void StartHost() TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage) Takes one received message off the queue, if there is one. The gateway drains this until it returns false, once per tick. public bool TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage message) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkMessage message The message, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks A TryDequeue rather than a returned collection, because the gateway drains it every tick and a returned collection would allocate every tick; AGENTS.md rule 29. TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int) Takes one "a peer joined" notification off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). public bool TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int peerId) Parameters Type Name Description int peerId The peer that joined, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks This is what makes SyncCadence.Once work for a peer that was not there when the value was first set. Without it, a name chosen by the host before anyone joined would never be sent, because Once sends once and a late joiner missed it. The authority answers a join by marking every synchronised variable unsent, so the next tick sends the current value of all of them. The resend goes to every peer, not only to the one that joined. This milestone has no per-peer addressing: SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) is a broadcast. The cost is one redundant copy of each synchronised variable per peer per join, which is bounded by the number of joins rather than by the frame rate. Per-peer addressing is part of the transform stream milestone, where rule 47's bandwidth budget makes it load-bearing. TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[], out int, out int) The next transform stream that arrived, as a view into a buffer the provider owns. The view is valid until the next stream arrives. public bool TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[] payload, out int offset, out int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The provider's buffer. int offset Where the stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Returns bool False when none is waiting. Remarks A view rather than an array, because a peer that is not the authority receives a stream on every tick and returning a fresh array would allocate on every one of them. TransformStreamInbox is the implementation both providers use. TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate) Takes one received variable update off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). public bool TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate update) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkVariableUpdate update The update, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.FileCloud.summary: Class FileCloudSaveProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The file-based Cloud Save provider: one file per key, under a directory the caller names. A first-class part of the product, not a test fixture; AGENTS.md rule 52. It is how every failure branch is tested without a network, and what makes the automated suite runnable with no credentials. public sealed class FileCloudSaveProvider : ICloudSaveProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object FileCloudSaveProvider Implements ICloudSaveProvider Examples runner.CloudGateway.UseProvider(new FileCloudSaveProvider(Path.Combine(tempDirectory, "saves"))); Remarks Every operation completes synchronously, inside the provider call; the gateway observes the outcome on its next per-frame poll, so a script sees the same event sequence it sees against a real service, one or more frames later rather than hundreds. Values are written in the invariant culture with the round-trip format, so a load returns exactly the Double that was saved. Keys are case sensitive, on every file system. Save("Level1", 1.0) and Save("level1", 2.0) hold two separate values and Load("Level1") returns 1.0, on Windows and macOS as well as on Linux, which is how Unity Cloud Save behaves; docs/slice-decisions.md D5.14 records the decision and the file name it produces. Constructors FileCloudSaveProvider(string) Creates a provider storing its files under one directory. public FileCloudSaveProvider(string directory) Parameters Type Name Description string directory Where the files live. Created by SignIn() when it does not exist. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException directory is null or whitespace. Methods Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines, so that a reader of the Console can tell a real service round trip from a file-based one. Allocates; called only at state transitions, never per frame. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Unity Cloud Save, signed in as player abc123", or "file-based provider at C:/saves". FailNext(OperationFailure) Makes the next operation, whichever it is, complete with failure instead of doing its work. This is how a test reaches every failure branch without a network, which is the reason this provider exists; AGENTS.md rule 52. public void FailNext(OperationFailure failure) Parameters Type Name Description OperationFailure failure The classified reason the next operation reports. Examples provider.FailNext(OperationFailure.RateLimited); Load(string) Starts loading one key's value. public ICloudLoadOperation Load(string key) Parameters Type Name Description string key The key. Returns ICloudLoadOperation The operation the gateway polls. A key that does not exist completes with OperationFailure.NotFound. Save(string, double) Starts saving one value under one key. public IAsyncOperation Save(string key, double value) Parameters Type Name Description string key The key. The gateway validates it at build time; a provider may refuse a key it cannot store with OperationFailure.Denied. double value The value to store. Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. SignIn() Starts signing in. Called by the gateway once, when the first request arrives. A provider that needs no sign-in returns an already-completed operation. public IAsyncOperation SignIn() Returns IAsyncOperation The operation the gateway polls. Remarks Creates the directory. There is no account, so "signing in" is only that.
