reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.INetworkP.title: Interface INetworkProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.INetworkP.summary: Interface INetworkProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What a netcode backend provides to the NetworkGateway: a session to start and end, the connection facts a script is allowed to read, and two queues the gateway drains once per tick. Script code never sees this type; it sees the Net and Sync surfaces. AGENTS.md rule 49. public interface INetworkProvider Expand Details ... Examples runner.NetworkGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNetworkProvider()); Remarks Two implementations exist, and the tests that matter run against both. FakeNetworkProvider runs two peers in one process with no network and no Editor, which is what makes the message and cadence tests runnable in Edit Mode; it is a second real implementation rather than a mock, in the same way FakeHost is for blocks. NgoNetworkProvider in CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode is the Netcode for GameObjects one, and it is the only place in the product that references that package. Authority, not "server". HasAuthority(int) answers for one object and means owner under distributed authority and server under client-server, which is why a script written against it runs unchanged in either topology. AGENTS.md rule 44. Nothing here throws because a session is not running. A provider with no session reports Offline, zero peers and no authority. Connection state is a state a script reads, not an exception it handles; AGENTS.md rule 45. Properties IsHost True when this peer is the host. False for a client and for no session at all. Exposed because rule 45 forbids hiding it, and because "works as host, breaks as client" is the defect that hiding it produces. bool IsHost { get; } Property Value bool MaximumTransformStreamBytes How many payload bytes of transform stream this backend can carry in one send. The runner splits a tick's stream into as many sends as it needs to stay inside it. int MaximumTransformStreamBytes { get; } Property Value int Remarks A transport carries a bounded message. One stream per authority per tick is what AGENTS.md rule 47 requires and it stays true here: the tick still produces one stream, and this is how many bytes of it fit in one message. A hundred objects sending all three channels is about 1800 bytes, which is past what Netcode for GameObjects carries unfragmented, so this is not a limit only an unusual session meets. Splitting rather than asking the backend to fragment is deliberate. Each piece carries the stream's own 3-byte header and is decoded on its own, so a piece costs about 3 bytes plus whatever the backend's own per-message header is; a fragmented message costs the backend's fragment headers and its reassembly state instead, and leaves the stream depending on a feature that differs between backends. PeerCount How many peers are in the session, including this one. Zero when offline. int PeerCount { get; } Property Value int RoundTripMilliseconds Round trip time to the host in milliseconds, or 0 when offline or when this peer is the host. Latency is a state a script may read, not an error; AGENTS.md rule 45. double RoundTripMilliseconds { get; } Property Value double State What the session is doing right now. Never throws and is meaningful before any session has been started. SessionState State { get; } Property Value SessionState Methods Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines, so a reader of the Console can tell a real session from the in-process one. Allocates; called only at state transitions, never per tick. string Describe() Returns string For example: "Netcode for GameObjects, host on port 7777", or "in-process provider, 2 peers". EndSession() Ends the session and returns to Offline. Called again on an already-offline provider, it does nothing, so that a restart is EndSession then StartHost without the caller tracking state. void EndSession() HasAuthority(int) Whether this peer may write the state of one object. bool HasAuthority(int objectId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The networked object, as the gateway numbers it. Returns bool True when this peer owns the object under distributed authority, or is the server under client-server. False when offline, because an offline peer has no authority to speak of and a script that guards on authority then does nothing rather than misbehaving. SendToAuthority(int, int) Sends one message to whichever peer holds authority over the object. The message has a name and no payload in this milestone. void SendToAuthority(int objectId, int messageId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the message is about. int messageId The message, interned by the gateway so no string crosses this call. SendTransformStream(byte[], int) Sends one authority's whole transform stream for one network tick. void SendTransformStream(byte[] payload, int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The buffer the runner encoded the stream into. The provider must copy what it needs before returning, because the runner reuses this buffer next tick. int length How many bytes of it the stream occupies. Remarks One call per authority per tick, carrying every object that authority has something to send for, rather than one call per object. AGENTS.md rule 47 requires that shape, because one message per object per tick spends about as many bytes on framing as a half-precision position costs. SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) Sends one variable's value to every other peer. Called only by the authority, and only when the variable's cadence says to send. void SendVariable(int objectId, int variableIndex, in NetworkValue value) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the variable belongs to. int variableIndex Which synchronised variable, numbered by the order the script declared it in. See VariableIndex for why this is not a slot index. NetworkValue value The value to send. StartClient(string) Joins a session. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running. void StartClient(string address) Parameters Type Name Description string address Where to connect. An implementation that needs no address ignores it. StartHost() Starts hosting. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running, so an implementation may assume it is offline. void StartHost() TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage) Takes one received message off the queue, if there is one. The gateway drains this until it returns false, once per tick. bool TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage message) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkMessage message The message, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks A TryDequeue rather than a returned collection, because the gateway drains it every tick and a returned collection would allocate every tick; AGENTS.md rule 29. TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int) Takes one "a peer joined" notification off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). bool TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int peerId) Parameters Type Name Description int peerId The peer that joined, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks This is what makes SyncCadence.Once work for a peer that was not there when the value was first set. Without it, a name chosen by the host before anyone joined would never be sent, because Once sends once and a late joiner missed it. The authority answers a join by marking every synchronised variable unsent, so the next tick sends the current value of all of them. The resend goes to every peer, not only to the one that joined. This milestone has no per-peer addressing: SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) is a broadcast. The cost is one redundant copy of each synchronised variable per peer per join, which is bounded by the number of joins rather than by the frame rate. Per-peer addressing is part of the transform stream milestone, where rule 47's bandwidth budget makes it load-bearing. TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[], out int, out int) The next transform stream that arrived, as a view into a buffer the provider owns. The view is valid until the next stream arrives. bool TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[] payload, out int offset, out int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The provider's buffer. int offset Where the stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Returns bool False when none is waiting. Remarks A view rather than an array, because a peer that is not the authority receives a stream on every tick and returning a fresh array would allocate on every one of them. TransformStreamInbox is the implementation both providers use. TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate) Takes one received variable update off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). bool TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate update) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkVariableUpdate update The update, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input.Inp.title: Class InputSystemProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input.Inp.summary: Class InputSystemProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input Assembly ApiSource.dll The input backend that reads Unity's Input System. The one place in the product that references that package. public sealed class InputSystemProvider : IInputProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object InputSystemProvider Implements IInputProvider Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new InputSystemProvider(actions)); Remarks This assembly compiles only when the Input System package is installed. Its assembly definition carries a version define, LUNY_INPUTSYSTEM from com.unity.inputsystem 1.8.0 or newer, and a matching define constraint, which is the same arrangement CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode uses for Netcode for GameObjects. The ownership board's P01 row is what authorises this one reference: "new O02 authorization supersedes the old all-assembly package ban for this adapter", and the core stays package-independent. The configured action asset owns the bindings and the processors. Nothing here creates an action, binds a key or applies a processor: it finds the action the script named, checks it produces the kind the script declared, and reads it. Where a PlayerInput component exists for a local player, its own actions are used, so device pairing is the Input System's and not this provider's. Every read is polled and frame-scoped. The three occurrences map to the Input System's own frame queries, so nothing is queued, nothing is replayed and no callback is subscribed. That is what keeps an occurrence from arriving outside a frame and what keeps a paused frame's edges from being delivered later. Constructors InputSystemProvider() Creates a provider that reads whichever PlayerInput components are present, and nothing else. public InputSystemProvider() Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new InputSystemProvider()); Remarks Use this when the project pairs its players with PlayerInput. A local player with no PlayerInput resolves nothing and every action of that player is reported once and reads its resting value. InputSystemProvider(InputActionAsset) Creates a provider with one action asset to fall back on for local player 0. public InputSystemProvider(InputActionAsset actions) Parameters Type Name Description InputActionAsset actions The action asset for local player 0, or null for none. Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new InputSystemProvider(actions)); Remarks A PlayerInput for a local player always wins, because that is where the Input System keeps that player's paired devices. The asset is what a single-player project uses, where there is nothing to pair and a PlayerInput component would be ceremony. The asset is enabled here, because an action that is not enabled reads its resting value forever and that reads exactly like a wrong binding. A PlayerInput's own actions are left alone: that component enables and disables them itself. Properties LocalPlayerCount How many local players this backend currently has. Zero is a valid answer and is not a failure. public int LocalPlayerCount { get; } Property Value int Remarks The number of PlayerInput components present, or 1 when this provider was given an action asset and no PlayerInput exists. Methods CancelAllRebinds() Stops every in-flight capture. A provider that is about to be replaced or dropped must call this so a RebindingOperation does not stay subscribed to Input System updates. public void CancelAllRebinds() CancelRebind(int) Stops one capture without applying an override. A missing or already-terminal identifier is a no-op. public void CancelRebind(int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int rebindId The identifier StartRebind(int, out int) produced. IsPressed(int) Whether the action is held down now. Must allocate nothing; AGENTS.md rule 29. public bool IsPressed(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. Returns bool True while the control is pressed. Occurred(int, InputPhase) Whether one occurrence happened during the frame that is running. Must allocate nothing. public bool Occurred(int actionId, InputPhase phase) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. InputPhase phase Which occurrence to ask about. Returns bool True when it happened this frame. PollRebind(int) Asks whether one capture has finished. Must allocate nothing while pending. public InputRebindPoll PollRebind(int rebindId) Parameters Type Name Description int rebindId The identifier StartRebind(int, out int) produced. Returns InputRebindPoll Pending while listening, then a terminal outcome. ReadNumber(int) The action's one-component value now. Must allocate nothing. public double ReadNumber(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. Returns double The value, which is 0 at rest. ReadVector(int, out double, out double, out double) The action's spatial value now, with unused components zero. Must allocate nothing. public void ReadVector(int actionId, out double x, out double y, out double z) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier Resolve(int, string, InputValueKind, out int) produced. double x The first component. double y The second component. double z The third component, zero for a two-component action. InputValueKind kind What the declaration says the action produces. int actionId The identifier the four reads take, meaningful only when this returns Resolved. Returns InputActionResolution Whether the action was found, and why not when it was not. Remarks Called once per declaration rather than once per read, so an implementation may do the string work here and must do none of it afterwards. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputFact.title: Struct InputFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputFact.summary: Struct InputFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Input surface inside Build(): names the local player whose actions this script reads. It hides UnityEngine.Input inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. public readonly struct InputFactory Expand Details ... Examples var move = Input.ForPlayer(0).Vector2("Move"); var fire = Input.ForPlayer(0).Button("Fire"); On.Ready(Input.Cursor.Lock(), Input.Cursor.Hide()); Remarks Action reads are always a named local player's input, never the machine's. There is no member here that reads a key or a device: an action is resolved for one local player, so a four-player split screen is four declarations and not one global read that every player shares. That is what the accepted design means by not deriving local players from global device polling. The machine cursor is the exception: Cursor is one lock and one visibility flag for the whole machine. Which backend supplies the actions is a runner service, not a script's business. The Input surface names no package. CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input is the Input System adapter and the only place in the product that references that package; with no adapter installed every action reads its resting value and says so once. This surface's shape is provisional. It implements the recorded recommendation of the open decision contract-input-actions, which is one player-scoped typed action handle for both the values and the occurrences. The alternative that decision holds open repeats the player and the name at each use instead. Nothing below this surface depends on which of the two is chosen. Properties Cursor The machine cursor: lock and visibility as two independent writes. public CursorInputFactory Cursor { get; } Property Value CursorInputFactory Examples On.Ready(Input.Cursor.Lock(), Input.Cursor.Hide()); Remarks Four local players share one cursor. This is not a member of Input.ForPlayer. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Methods ForPlayer(int, string, int) Names the local player whose actions the declarations that follow belong to. public PlayerInputFactory ForPlayer(int localPlayerIndex, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description int localPlayerIndex Which local player, from 0. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns PlayerInputFactory A builder whose four methods declare one action each. The number is what the configured backend pairs a device with. A named player is not accepted here: Define has no player kind, and a typed player identity is the open decision contract-player-identity. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build().

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputGate.title: Class InputGateway | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InputGate.summary: Class InputGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core's one entry point to player input. Owns the IInputProvider, resolves each program's declared actions once, and answers the value reads and the occurrence tests the input blocks make. public sealed class InputGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object InputGateway Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new FakeInputProvider()); Remarks This is the input counterpart of NetworkGateway and is deliberately the same shape, because it has the same problem: the core may not reference the Input System package, so the core owns an interface and a separate, package-gated assembly implements it. The ownership board's P01 row is what authorises that adapter, and it is the only place in the product where the package is named. Resolution happens once per program, not once per object. A declaration carries a local player index and a name, both written in Build(), so every object running the script resolves to the same configured action. ResolutionsFor(ScriptProgram) returns the one array of backend identifiers that program's instances share; the array is re-resolved in place when the provider changes, so an instance that already holds it keeps reading the right actions. Nothing here is per frame except the reads. Each read is one array index and one call into the backend, and allocates nothing; AGENTS.md rule 29. A declaration that does not resolve is reported once and reads its resting value. The report names the script, the declaration and why, at error severity, once per declaration per program, for the reason the asset inputs report once: the mistake is in the script's wiring or in the action asset, so a thousand objects say so once. Fields Unresolved The identifier a declaration that did not resolve carries. Every read of it produces the resting value of its kind. public const int Unresolved = -1 Field Value int Properties HasProvider Whether an input backend has been installed. False means every action reads its resting value and every occurrence test is false. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool IsLocked Whether the last cursor lock write was Lock. public bool IsLocked { get; } Property Value bool IsVisible Whether the last cursor visibility write was Show. public bool IsVisible { get; } Property Value bool LocalPlayerCount How many local players the backend has, or zero when there is none. public int LocalPlayerCount { get; } Property Value int Methods IsPressed(int) Whether one resolved action is held down now. public bool IsPressed(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier, or Unresolved. Returns bool False for an unresolved action and for no provider. Examples var pressed = gateway.IsPressed(actionId); Occurred(int, InputPhase) Whether one occurrence happened to a resolved action during this frame. public bool Occurred(int actionId, InputPhase phase) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier, or Unresolved. InputPhase phase Which occurrence to ask about. Returns bool False for an unresolved action and for no provider. Examples var fired = gateway.Occurred(actionId, InputPhase.Performed); ReadNumber(int) One resolved action's one-component value now. public double ReadNumber(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier, or Unresolved. Returns double Zero for an unresolved action and for no provider. Examples var throttle = gateway.ReadNumber(actionId); ReadVector(int) One resolved action's spatial value now. public Vec3 ReadVector(int actionId) Parameters Type Name Description int actionId The identifier, or Unresolved. Returns Vec3 The zero vector for an unresolved action and for no provider. Examples var move = gateway.ReadVector(actionId); ResolutionsFor(ScriptProgram) The backend identifiers this program's declared actions resolved to, in declaration order. Resolved the first time the program is asked for, and re-resolved in place when the provider changes. public int[] ResolutionsFor(ScriptProgram program) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptProgram program The program whose declarations to resolve. Returns int[] One identifier per declaration, Unresolved where it did not resolve. An empty array for a program that declares no action. Examples var ids = runner.InputGateway.ResolutionsFor(program); Remarks Called once per spawn and never per frame. The returned array belongs to the gateway and is shared by every instance of the program, because a declaration's player and name are the same for all of them. UseProvider(IInputProvider) Installs the backend and re-resolves every program that has already been resolved, so an instance spawned before the provider arrived starts reading real actions. public void UseProvider(IInputProvider provider) Parameters Type Name Description IInputProvider provider The backend. Null is the caller's mistake. Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new FakeInputProvider()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The provider is null.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.InstanceL.summary: Class InstanceLayout Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll How many slots of each kind one instance of a program owns, and what value each slot starts from. Built once per script type and never changed afterwards. public sealed class InstanceLayout Expand Details ... Inheritance object InstanceLayout Examples var layout = program.Layout; // one Double and one Boolean: 8 + 8 = 16 payload bytes in 2 arrays Remarks The layout is what makes a spawn's cost predictable: it names every array a ScriptInstance allocates and how many bytes of payload each one carries, so the allocation test can assert an exact figure rather than a ceiling. See AGENTS.md rule 31, boundary 1, and docs/execution-model.md. Byte counts here are payload only. A managed array also carries a header whose size differs between Mono and CoreCLR, so the layout deliberately does not include it; the allocation test measures the header on the runtime it is running on and adds SlotArrayCount of them. A header size baked in here would be right on one runtime and wrong on another. Fields Empty An empty layout: no slots, no arrays, no payload. Used by tests that need the cost of a bare ScriptInstance with nothing in it. public static readonly InstanceLayout Empty Field Value InstanceLayout Remarks A field rather than a static auto-property, for the reason given on None. Properties AllocatingTextCount Number of allocating text slots on every instance. public int AllocatingTextCount { get; } Property Value int AssetInputCount Number of asset-input slots on every instance: one for each asset input the script declared. public int AssetInputCount { get; } Property Value int Remarks An asset-input slot holds a reference rather than a value, so its payload is IntPtr.Size bytes, for the reason OwnedObjectCount gives. CollectionCount Number of list and map headers on every instance. public int CollectionCount { get; } Property Value int EnumCount How many enum slots one instance of this program holds. public int EnumCount { get; } Property Value int Examples var count = layout.EnumCount; FlagCount Number of Flag slots on every instance. public int FlagCount { get; } Property Value int NumberCount Number of Number slots on every instance. public int NumberCount { get; } Property Value int OwnedObjectCount Number of owned-object slots on every instance: one for each distinct name the script's Object.Create calls use. public int OwnedObjectCount { get; } Property Value int Remarks An owned-object slot holds a reference rather than a value, so its payload is IntPtr.Size bytes and not a fixed number written here: a 64-bit player and a 32-bit Web build disagree, and a constant baked in would be right on one and wrong on the other, which is the mistake the array-header remarks on this type describe. RandomStreamCount Number of named random streams on every instance. public int RandomStreamCount { get; } Property Value int RotationCount How many Rotation slots one instance of this program holds. public int RotationCount { get; } Property Value int Examples var count = layout.RotationCount; SlotArrayCount Number of arrays a spawn allocates. An empty slot kind costs no allocation, because the instance uses Array.Empty for it, so this is the count of kinds a program actually uses rather than the number of kinds that exist. public int SlotArrayCount { get; } Property Value int SlotBytes Payload bytes every instance's slot arrays hold together, with each array's payload rounded up to the next multiple of 8 because that is how a managed array is padded. Excludes array headers and the instance object itself; see the remarks on this type for why. public long SlotBytes { get; } Property Value long Vec2Count How many Vec2 slots one instance of this program holds. public int Vec2Count { get; } Property Value int Examples var count = layout.Vec2Count; Vec3Count How many Vec3 slots one instance of this program holds. public int Vec3Count { get; } Property Value int Examples var count = layout.Vec3Count; Methods TextCount(TextCapacity) Number of text slots of one capacity on every instance. public int TextCount(TextCapacity capacity) Parameters Type Name Description TextCapacity capacity Which capacity to count. Returns int How many text slots of that capacity a program declared. Examples var sixtyFours = layout.TextCount(TextCapacity.Bytes64); ToString() One line naming every count, for a log or a failure message. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "doubles=2 booleans=1 text32=0 text64=1 text128=0 text512=0 text4096=0 ownedObjects=0 slotBytes=104 arrays=3".

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Class LunyScriptException Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The root of every exception LunyScript throws. Catch this to catch everything the product raised and nothing else. public abstract class LunyScriptException : Exception Expand Details ... Inheritance object Exception LunyScriptException Derived LunyScriptContractException LunyScriptInternalException LunyScriptUsageException Examples try { runner.TickFrameUpdate(); } catch (LunyScriptException exception) { /* everything LunyScript raised */ } Remarks This type exists to be the one interception point. Before it, LunyScriptUsageException and LunyScriptContractException were both sealed and both derived from InvalidOperationException, so they were siblings whose only shared ancestor also catches framework failures that have nothing to do with LunyScript. A debugger filter, a catch block or a diagnostic layer could not select "everything LunyScript threw"; now one type name does it. The .NET argument types are deliberately not kept. C# has single inheritance, so an exception cannot be both an ArgumentNullException and a LunyScriptException, and the choice between them was made in favour of the base class: a user of a scripting API is not writing general .NET code against these types and should almost never catch one at all, because they name a mistake to fix rather than a condition to handle. Recorded in docs/api-changes.md. An exception that knows the authored location presents it as the topmost stack frame. A block is composed inside Build() and executed much later, so the user's script line is not on the call stack when the block fails. A throw out of Build() carries the location from its own call site; a throw while a block runs is given the running block's location by ScriptRunner.ReportBlockFailure, through AttachBlockContext, because the checks that raise it are too far from the block to name it themselves; which of the two wins, and when there is neither, is docs/console-navigation.md's "Which authored location a diagnostic carries". StackTrace prepends Location in Unity's own stack-frame format, which is what UnityEngine.StackTraceUtility.ExtractStringFromExceptionInternal reads through this virtual property, so the Console prints the user's own line as the topmost frame. It does not navigate there. A Console entry's double-click target is the file and line Unity fills in from the live call stack when the entry is written; where that lands differs by path and is measured in docs/console-navigation.md. See SourceLocation for how the location is captured. Constructors LunyScriptException(string) Creates an exception that names no script, no block and no location. protected LunyScriptException(string message) Parameters Type Name Description string message What went wrong, and what to do instead. LunyScriptException(string, string, string, SourceLocation) Creates an exception carrying the context a debugging window reads. protected LunyScriptException(string message, string scriptTypeName, string blockTypeName, SourceLocation location) Parameters Type Name Description string message What went wrong, and what to do instead. string scriptTypeName The script type's name, or null. string blockTypeName The block type's name, or null. SourceLocation location Where the block was authored, or Unknown. Properties BlockTypeName The name of the block type this concerns, or null. public string BlockTypeName { get; } Property Value string Location Where in the user's script the block was authored, captured at build time. public SourceLocation Location { get; } Property Value SourceLocation ScriptTypeName The name of the Script subclass this concerns, or null. public string ScriptTypeName { get; } Property Value string StackTrace The runtime stack, with the authored location prepended as its topmost frame when this exception has one. public override string StackTrace { get; } Property Value string Examples // CountdownScript:Build() (at Assets/Scripts/CountdownScript.cs:12) // CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptRunner:TickFrameUpdate() (at ...) Remarks The added line is Unity's own frame format, Type:Method() (at path:line), which is what StackTraceUtility produces, so a reader of the Console text sees the user's own line first. Nothing is removed: the real frames follow, so the failure is still diagnosable by a maintainer. This changes what the entry prints and not where a double-click on it goes. Unity chooses that target from the live call stack at log time rather than from this string. docs/console-navigation.md records the measurement. Where that target lands depends on who wrote the entry, and this property moves it on neither path. Where ScriptRunner.ReportBlockFailure reports the failure, LunyScript writes the entry itself, so it navigates to the line that reported the exception. Where the exception escapes instead - out of ScriptRunner.RaiseReady into LunyScriptBehaviour.Start, or out of Build() - LunyScript writes no entry and no error line at all, so there is no link of ours: Unity logs it, and the entry opens whatever called into the code that threw. The frame this property prepends is printed either way, and Unity links every printed frame that carries source information. Methods ToLogRecord() This exception as the same structured record the logging surface carries, so a debugging window reads a failure and a log entry through one shape. public LunyScriptLogRecord ToLogRecord() Returns LunyScriptLogRecord The record, at Error. Examples LunyScriptLog.Write(exception.ToLogRecord());

If they do, it is a LunyScript defect and not something they did. Every concrete block type is internal with an internal constructor, built by the factories and never by user code, so a null argument there is the product's mistake; that is the audience split AGENTS.md rule 71 records, and it is why these do not share a type with the mistakes a user can make. Most of these are raised through CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScriptContract, whose guards are compiled out when DEBUG is not defined, so those cost a release build nothing and can be met only in the Editor and in a development player. Two sites are not those, and throw this type in every build: CompletedOperation.Failed and CompletedLoadOperation.FailedLoad. A guard is allowed to be conditional only where the failure its removal gives up is loud; breaking those two makes IsSuccess true on a failed cloud call, which is a silent wrong value rather than a crash. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Class LunyScriptLog Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The one place LunyScript writes to the Unity console. Unity log lines are formatted here; the LunyScript console reads the retained structured fields. public static class LunyScriptLog Expand Details ... Before this class existed the prefix "LunyScript <area> | " was written out again as a string literal at every call site, in ten files, so changing the format meant editing every literal and a missed one was invisible. SourceRuleTests.NoCodeOutsideTheLoggingSurfaceCallsUnityDebugLog is what makes that a failing test rather than a convention. Every method here carries [HideInCallstack], and that attribute is what makes a log entry open the caller's own line. Unity skips a hidden frame both when it prints the stack and when it chooses the entry's double-click target, so the first frame it accepts is the one that called this class. Deleting the attribute was measured moving that target off the caller and into Write(in LunyScriptLogRecord, Object) in this file; docs/console-navigation.md. It hides frames and cannot reveal one, which is why the authored location is carried in the record rather than looked for on the stack; see SourceLocation. The console and runtime debugger share this structured record contract. Write(in LunyScriptLogRecord, Object) takes a LunyScriptLogRecord with the area, the script, the block and the authored location as separate fields, and formatting is the last thing that happens to it. A window that traces calls reads the record; the Console gets the string. Logging is not on the run-time path and this class does not pretend otherwise. Composing a message concatenates strings, which AGENTS.md rule 33 forbids on the run-time path. Every call site here is a failure path, a build-time path or a once-per-operation path; no block's Execute logs. A block that needed to log every frame would be a design defect, not a reason to make this allocation-free. Fields Prefix What every LunyScript log line starts with. The product's name, never the repository's; AGENTS.md section 1. public const string Prefix = "LunyScript " Field Value string Separator What separates the area from the message, and one context field from the next. public const string Separator = " | " Field Value string Properties EditorRecords Editor-session diagnostics, retained even with the console window closed. Returns string The formatted line. Examples var line = LunyScriptLog.Compose(record); // "LunyScript core | a block threw ..." Remarks The shape is LunyScript <area> | <message>, then the script and block names when the record names them, then the authored location when it has one. In the Editor the location is written as a Unity rich-text hyperlink. Unity subscribes EditorGUI_OpenFileOnHyperLinkClicked to its own EditorGUI.hyperLinkClicked event for every console message, and that handler opens the href at the line attribute. Writing the authored location as such a link is therefore what makes a click open the user's own script line, per log entry and with nothing to match up afterwards. Outside the Editor the same location is written as plain text, because a player log and a gate log are read as text and the markup would be noise there. A LunyScriptException presents the authored location as the topmost frame of that stack, so the entry prints the user's own line first. A double-click on that entry opens the line that called this method, not the authored line. Unity chooses a Console entry's target from the live call stack when the entry is written, and [HideInCallstack] skips this method's own frame but cannot reach a frame that has already unwound. The authored location reaches the user through the entry's printed text. docs/console-navigation.md holds the measurement. AGENTS.md rule 17 forbids mutable static state and rule 18 names [AutoStaticsCleanup] as the mechanism for the unavoidable one: with domain reload disabled, a static keeps its value from the previous Play session, and this attribute is what puts it back. Gate 3 in docs/gates.md measured the attribute working on this editor version. The type is partial because Unity's code generator emits a second partial declaration holding the generated reset method; a non-partial declaration fails to compile with error CS0260. A test that wants its own runner creates one directly with new ScriptRunner() and never touches this type. Nothing here is needed to run blocks. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.LunyScrip.summary: Class LunyScriptUsageException Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Thrown when script code asks LunyScript for something the API does not offer: a C# if around a condition block, an arithmetic operator on a text variable, a builder finished twice. public sealed class LunyScriptUsageException : LunyScriptException Expand Details ... Inheritance object Exception LunyScriptException LunyScriptUsageException Inherited Members LunyScriptException.ScriptTypeName LunyScriptException.BlockTypeName LunyScriptException.Location LunyScriptException.StackTrace LunyScriptException.ToLogRecord() Examples // throws LunyScriptUsageException: a condition block was used in a C# if if (health > 10) { } Remarks Every message names the mistake and the supported alternative, because this exception is read by a user of the product rather than by a maintainer of it. Most of these are raised at build time, which runs once per script type at launch, so a script that can throw one of those throws it on the first run. Seven cases are raised at run time instead, and two of them can fire long after launch. The implicit conversion of a condition block to bool, AGENTS.md rule 38, which throws in release builds too when a C# if or while tests the block. The text-capacity check in ScriptInstance.SetText, reached from SetTextBlock and CopyTextBlock. Build time checks only the 509-byte literal limit and does not know the target variable's TextCapacity, so a 37-byte literal written into a TextCapacity.Bytes32 variable (29 usable bytes) builds clean and throws on the first frame that block executes, which may be long after launch if it sits behind an If. The slot-range check in ScriptInstance, reached from GetNumber, SetNumber, GetFlag, SetFlag and every text accessor. A Var<T> handle carries a slot index and a kind and nothing that identifies its program, so a handle declared by a different script type addresses this script's slot of the same index; where that index is past the end of this instance's array for its kind, the access throws and the message names that cause. It fires on the first frame the block executes, which may be long after launch. docs/slice-decisions.md entries D4.31 and D4.32 record the accepted edge and the shape of the check. ScriptRunner.RaiseReady called twice for one spawn. An invalid Script type selected for serialization. A C# read or Send on LunyScriptBehaviour after the object is destroyed, or before Awake. The message names the object and the call. Other evaluated outside a contact event. The block is built in Build() and runs later, so a read in On.FrameUpdate throws when that event runs. The message names the call and the six contact events that may use it. This derives from LunyScriptException and no longer from InvalidOperationException. That base is the one interception point a debugger filter or a diagnostic layer uses to select everything LunyScript threw; docs/api-changes.md records the change and why the .NET type was not kept. SourceLocation location Where the block was authored, or Unknown.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.MathFacto.summary: Struct MathFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core numeric functions, written as Math.Abs(...) inside a script's Build(). Every member returns an expression that is evaluated each time the block holding it runs; none of them writes anything. public readonly struct MathFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.FrameUpdate(Distance.Set(Math.Clamp(Distance + Step, 0.0, 100.0))); Remarks Every function here has a second, writing form on the variable itself. The API semantics board's C01 answer, 2026-09-13, requires both: Math.Abs(Offset) computes a magnitude and leaves Offset alone, while Offset.Abs() writes the magnitude back into Offset. Reach for the expression when the result feeds something else and for the write when the variable is the destination. What this surface holds, and what it deliberately does not. The board's C04 answer is a small core plus named packages: Abs, Min, Max, Clamp, Floor, Ceiling, Truncate, Round and Lerp are the core, and remap, easing, curve, spatial and trigonometric functions live in separate first-party Math packages that this one does not carry. That is an organisation choice rather than a refusal to own them. The five arithmetic operators are not members here. Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and remainder are written + - * / %, which is their expression form; Health.Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide and Remainder are their writing form. A Math.Subtract would be a third spelling of something C# already spells. Methods Abs(NumberValueBlock, string, int) The magnitude of a number, with no sign. public NumberValueBlock Abs(NumberValueBlock value, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock value The expression to read. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. It records the line this block was written on, so a later failure names that line rather than LunyScript's own source. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns NumberValueBlock A number expression. Examples On.FrameUpdate(Speed.Set(Math.Abs(Velocity))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException value is null, or this factory was not obtained inside Build(). Returns NumberValueBlock A number expression. Clamp(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) A number held between two bounds. The bounds are applied in order, the minimum first and the maximum second, so a reversed pair produces the maximum rather than throwing. NumberValueBlock minimum The lower bound. NumberValueBlock maximum The upper bound. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Examples On.FixedUpdate(Motion.MoveTo(Pad).AtSpeed(4.0)); On.FixedUpdate(Motion.AddForce(Thrust).InWorldSpace()); On.Ready(Motion.TeleportTo(Spawn)); Remarks Motion is not Transform. Transform.MoveBy writes pose immediately, with no physics. Motion.MoveBy selects a CharacterController, a kinematic Rigidbody, or a direct transform, and refuses a dynamic Rigidbody. Dynamic bodies use AddForce(Vec3ValueBlock, string, int), AddImpulse(Vec3ValueBlock, string, int), SetVelocity(Vec3ValueBlock, string, int) and StopMotion(string, int). Relocation that is not traversed movement is TeleportTo(Vec3ValueBlock, string, int). API-semantics M20. Kinematic displacement, every physical input, and a Rigidbody teleport belong in On.FixedUpdate. Written in any other event they are reported once and ignored; they are not transferred to a later step. API-semantics M12. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetFactor.title: Struct NetFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetFactor.summary: Struct NetFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Net surface a script reads the session through: who has authority, whether there is a session, how many peers, how far behind a value is, and the one way to ask the authority to do something. public readonly struct NetFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Net.HasAuthority).Then(Score.Add(1.0))); Remarks Everything here is a state, and none of it throws when there is no session. AGENTS.md rule 45: authority, ownership, connection state and latency are what a networked script gets wrong, and a design that hides them produces the "works as host, breaks as client" defect. An offline peer has no authority, is not connected, has zero peers and a round trip of zero, and a script that guards on any of those then does nothing rather than misbehaving. Authority, not "server". HasAuthority means owner under distributed authority, which is the default topology, and server under client-server. The same script runs unchanged in either; AGENTS.md rule 44. The three session facts are conditions and the two numbers are number expressions. A condition goes into If(...) and is negated with !, the way every other condition in this API is; a number expression is compared and combined the way every other number is. The proposal this milestone was written from wrote If(Net.HasAuthority == false), which would have needed a second way to negate a condition alongside the ! operator that already exists. If(!Net.HasAuthority) is the same sentence with the operator the API already has. Properties HasAuthority True on the peer that may write this object's synchronised variables. public ConditionBlock HasAuthority { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Net.HasAuthority).Then(Health.Add(-1.0))); Remarks Owner under distributed authority, server under client-server; false while there is no session, and false on every peer for an object that was never bound to a networked object. This is the guard a write to a synchronised variable belongs behind: without it the write is refused on every peer but one, with the message ScriptInstance raises. IsConnected True while a session is connected, as host or as client. public ConditionBlock IsConnected { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(!Net.IsConnected).Then(Status.Set("offline"))); Remarks Connecting is not connected, and neither is disconnected. The three are separate states because a script that shows "connecting" and one that shows "offline" are showing a player different things; AGENTS.md rule 45. IsHost True on the peer that is hosting the session. public ConditionBlock IsHost { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Net.IsHost).Then(Role.Set("host"))); Remarks Exposed rather than hidden because hiding it is what produces a script that works for whoever is hosting while they test it. It is not the same question as HasAuthority, which is asked per object. PeerCount How many peers are in the session, including this one. Zero while offline. public NumberValueBlock PeerCount { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Net.PeerCount > 1.0).Then(Crowded.Set(true))); RoundTripMilliseconds Round trip time to the host in milliseconds. Zero on the host and while offline. public NumberValueBlock RoundTripMilliseconds { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Net.RoundTripMilliseconds > 200.0).Then(ShowLagWarning.Set(true))); Remarks Latency is a state, not an exception; AGENTS.md rule 45. A script may show it, may refuse to start a timed action above a threshold, and may do neither. Send Where a message to the authority is written. public NetSendFactory Send { get; } Property Value NetSendFactory Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(!Net.HasAuthority).Then(Net.Send.ToAuthority(nameof(RequestReady)))); Methods SecondsSinceUpdate(TransformChannel, string, int) How many seconds since a value for one transform channel arrived from the authority. Zero on the authority itself, whose transform is the one being sent. public NumberValueBlock SecondsSinceUpdate(TransformChannel channel, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description TransformChannel channel The channel to ask about, which this script must synchronise. string callerFilePath Filled in by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Filled in by the compiler. Returns NumberValueBlock A value block reading the age in seconds. Examples If(Net.SecondsSinceUpdate(TransformChannel.Position) > 0.5).Then(Ghosted.Set(true)) Remarks Latency is a state a script reads rather than an exception it handles; AGENTS.md rule 45. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This script does not synchronise that channel, so nothing ever arrives for it and there is no age to report. SecondsSinceUpdate<T>(Var<T>, string, int) How many seconds ago this peer last received a value for one synchronised variable. Zero on the peer with authority, whose own value is never behind. public NumberValueBlock SecondsSinceUpdate<T>(Var<T> variable, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where T : struct Parameters Type Name Description Var<T> variable The synchronised variable to ask about. It has to have been declared with Var.DefineSynced or Var.DefineSyncedText in this same script. string callerFilePath Filled in by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Filled in by the compiler. Returns NumberValueBlock A number expression, in seconds. Type Parameters T Number, Flag or Text. Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Net.SecondsSinceUpdate(Health) > 1.0).Then(FadeHealthBar.Set(true))); Remarks This is the per-variable half of rule 45's "latency is a state". A rate-capped variable is stale between sends by design and a SyncCadence.Once variable is stale from the moment after it arrives; both are correct, and this is how a script can say by how much rather than assume. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The variable is not one this script synchronises, so there is no arrival for it to be counting from.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetSendFa.title: Struct NetSendFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetSendFa.summary: Struct NetSendFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Net.Send: the one way a peer without authority asks the authority to do something. public readonly struct NetSendFactory Expand Details ... Examples Net.Send.ToAuthority(nameof(RequestReady)) Remarks There is no "send to everyone" and no "send to one peer" in this milestone. A message goes to the authority over the object it was sent from, because that is the peer allowed to change the object's state, and state reaches the other peers as a synchronised variable rather than as a second message. That keeps one direction of travel: a request goes up to the authority, and state comes back down through the cadences. Methods ToAuthority(string, string, int) Builds a block that sends one named message to the peer with authority over this object. The message carries its name and no payload. public Block ToAuthority(string messageName, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string messageName What the message is called. Use nameof, so that a rename moves the send and the matching On.Message together. string callerFilePath Filled in by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Filled in by the compiler. Returns Block The block. Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(!Net.HasAuthority).Then(Net.Send.ToAuthority(nameof(RequestReady)))); Remarks Sending while offline does nothing: there is no authority to send to, and that is a state rather than a mistake. Sending on the peer that already has authority delivers the message to itself, so a script does not need two paths for "ask" and "do". Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The name is null or whitespace. A name that no On.Message in this script receives is refused too, at the end of Build() rather than here, because the receive may be written below the send.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode.L.title: Class LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode.L.summary: Class LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode Assembly ApiSource.dll Binds the script instance on this object to the object's network identity, so that its synchronised variables and its messages reach the same object on every peer. [RequireComponent(typeof(LunyScriptBehaviour))] [AddComponentMenu("LunyScript/LunyScript Network Behaviour")] public sealed class LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour : NetworkBehaviour Expand Details ... Inheritance object Object Component Behaviour MonoBehaviour NetworkBehaviour LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour Examples // On a networked object, alongside NetworkObject and LunyScriptBehaviour. gameObject.AddComponent<LunyScriptNetworkBehaviour>(); Remarks This is the whole bridge between Netcode for GameObjects and the LunyScript core. It translates one fact, the network object id, and does nothing else: no state is copied here, no value is serialised here, and the core is told nothing about NGO. AGENTS.md rule 49. The object needs a NetworkObject, a LunyScriptBehaviour that has already been given a script, and this component. The order that matters is that the script is named before LunyScriptBehaviour.Awake runs, which is what spawns the instance. The demo prefab carries its assignment in Script To Run. Despawn unbinds. An id that outlived its object would make an arriving message reach an instance that is no longer the object it names, so the binding ends where the spawn ends rather than where the GameObject is destroyed. Properties LunyScriptObjectId The LunyScript network object id this component binds its instance to. public int LunyScriptObjectId { get; } Property Value int Remarks NGO-ASSUMPTION: NetworkObjectId is a UInt64 that NGO assigns from a counter starting at 1 and increasing, so the value fits an Int32 for any session this product can produce. The narrowing is stated here rather than hidden; a session that spawned more than two billion objects would need INetworkProvider's object id to widen, and the MaxObjectId check below is what would report that rather than silently binding to a wrong id. Methods OnNetworkDespawn() public override void OnNetworkDespawn() OnNetworkSpawn() public override void OnNetworkSpawn()

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode.N.title: Class NgoNetworkProvider | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode.N.summary: Class NgoNetworkProvider Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode Assembly ApiSource.dll The Netcode for GameObjects backend for INetworkProvider: starts and ends a session on NetworkManager, answers the connection facts a script may read, and carries LunyScript's messages and synchronised variables over one named message channel. public sealed class NgoNetworkProvider : INetworkProvider Expand Details ... Inheritance object NgoNetworkProvider Implements INetworkProvider Examples runner.NetworkGateway.UseProvider(new NgoNetworkProvider()); runner.NetworkGateway.StartHost(); Remarks This is the only type in the product that references Netcode for GameObjects, and every load-bearing line below carries an NGO-ASSUMPTION comment saying which fact about that package it depends on. AGENTS.md rule 49. The core references neither this assembly nor that package, so replacing the netcode stack is writing a sibling of this file rather than editing everything. One named message channel, not one NetworkVariable per variable and not one RPC per message. Every LunyScript message and every synchronised variable travels as a payload on the channel named ChannelName, tagged with what it is. That is what lets the core decide the cadence and lets this file stay a transport. It is also the shape the transform stream needs, which AGENTS.md rule 47 requires to be one stream per authority per tick rather than one message per object; this milestone does not build that stream, and rule 47's bandwidth benchmark is still owed with it. Topology. HasAuthority(int) reads NetworkObject.HasAuthority, which NGO defines for both topologies, so a script written against Net.HasAuthority is already correct under either; AGENTS.md rule 44. What this milestone assumes is narrower and is stated at each send: the peer with authority is the server, which is the client-server case NGO runs by default. Routing a message to a client that holds authority under distributed authority is the next step and is marked where it belongs. Fields ChannelName The named message channel every LunyScript payload travels on. public const string ChannelName = "LunyScript" Field Value string DefaultPort The port used when an address carries none. public const ushort DefaultPort = 7777 Field Value ushort Properties IsHost True when this peer is the host. False for a client and for no session at all. Exposed because rule 45 forbids hiding it, and because "works as host, breaks as client" is the defect that hiding it produces. public bool IsHost { get; } Property Value bool MaximumTransformStreamBytes How many payload bytes of transform stream this backend can carry in one send. The runner splits a tick's stream into as many sends as it needs to stay inside it. public int MaximumTransformStreamBytes { get; } Property Value int Remarks A transport carries a bounded message. One stream per authority per tick is what AGENTS.md rule 47 requires and it stays true here: the tick still produces one stream, and this is how many bytes of it fit in one message. A hundred objects sending all three channels is about 1800 bytes, which is past what Netcode for GameObjects carries unfragmented, so this is not a limit only an unusual session meets. Splitting rather than asking the backend to fragment is deliberate. Each piece carries the stream's own 3-byte header and is decoded on its own, so a piece costs about 3 bytes plus whatever the backend's own per-message header is; a fragmented message costs the backend's fragment headers and its reassembly state instead, and leaves the stream depending on a feature that differs between backends. PeerCount How many peers are in the session, including this one. Zero when offline. public int PeerCount { get; } Property Value int RoundTripMilliseconds Round trip time to the host in milliseconds, or 0 when offline or when this peer is the host. Latency is a state a script may read, not an error; AGENTS.md rule 45. public double RoundTripMilliseconds { get; } Property Value double State What the session is doing right now. Never throws and is meaningful before any session has been started. public SessionState State { get; } Property Value SessionState TransformStreamBytesSent How many payload bytes those streams carried, before Netcode for GameObjects adds its own message and batch framing around them. public long TransformStreamBytesSent { get; } Property Value long TransformStreamsSent How many transform streams this peer has sent since the session started. The counterpart of FakeNetworkProvider's, and what the bandwidth measurement divides the transport's byte count by. public int TransformStreamsSent { get; } Property Value int Methods Describe() Names this provider for the gateway's log lines, so a reader of the Console can tell a real session from the in-process one. Allocates; called only at state transitions, never per tick. public string Describe() Returns string For example: "Netcode for GameObjects, host on port 7777", or "in-process provider, 2 peers". EndSession() Ends the session and returns to Offline. Called again on an already-offline provider, it does nothing, so that a restart is EndSession then StartHost without the caller tracking state. public void EndSession() HasAuthority(int) Whether this peer may write the state of one object. public bool HasAuthority(int objectId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The networked object, as the gateway numbers it. Returns bool True when this peer owns the object under distributed authority, or is the server under client-server. False when offline, because an offline peer has no authority to speak of and a script that guards on authority then does nothing rather than misbehaving. SendToAuthority(int, int) Sends one message to whichever peer holds authority over the object. The message has a name and no payload in this milestone. public void SendToAuthority(int objectId, int messageId) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the message is about. int messageId The message, interned by the gateway so no string crosses this call. SendTransformStream(byte[], int) Sends one authority's whole transform stream for one network tick. public void SendTransformStream(byte[] payload, int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The buffer the runner encoded the stream into. The provider must copy what it needs before returning, because the runner reuses this buffer next tick. int length How many bytes of it the stream occupies. Remarks One call per authority per tick, carrying every object that authority has something to send for, rather than one call per object. AGENTS.md rule 47 requires that shape, because one message per object per tick spends about as many bytes on framing as a half-precision position costs. SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) Sends one variable's value to every other peer. Called only by the authority, and only when the variable's cadence says to send. public void SendVariable(int objectId, int variableIndex, in NetworkValue value) Parameters Type Name Description int objectId The object the variable belongs to. int variableIndex Which synchronised variable, numbered by the order the script declared it in. See VariableIndex for why this is not a slot index. NetworkValue value The value to send. StartClient(string) Joins a session. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running. public void StartClient(string address) Parameters Type Name Description string address Where to connect. An implementation that needs no address ignores it. StartHost() Starts hosting. Refused by the gateway when a session is already running, so an implementation may assume it is offline. public void StartHost() TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage) Takes one received message off the queue, if there is one. The gateway drains this until it returns false, once per tick. public bool TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage message) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkMessage message The message, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks A TryDequeue rather than a returned collection, because the gateway drains it every tick and a returned collection would allocate every tick; AGENTS.md rule 29. TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int) Takes one "a peer joined" notification off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). public bool TryDequeuePeerJoined(out int peerId) Parameters Type Name Description int peerId The peer that joined, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty. Remarks This is what makes SyncCadence.Once work for a peer that was not there when the value was first set. Without it, a name chosen by the host before anyone joined would never be sent, because Once sends once and a late joiner missed it. The authority answers a join by marking every synchronised variable unsent, so the next tick sends the current value of all of them. The resend goes to every peer, not only to the one that joined. This milestone has no per-peer addressing: SendVariable(int, int, in NetworkValue) is a broadcast. The cost is one redundant copy of each synchronised variable per peer per join, which is bounded by the number of joins rather than by the frame rate. Per-peer addressing is part of the transform stream milestone, where rule 47's bandwidth budget makes it load-bearing. TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[], out int, out int) The next transform stream that arrived, as a view into a buffer the provider owns. The view is valid until the next stream arrives. public bool TryDequeueTransformStream(out byte[] payload, out int offset, out int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The provider's buffer. int offset Where the stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Returns bool False when none is waiting. Remarks A view rather than an array, because a peer that is not the authority receives a stream on every tick and returning a fresh array would allocate on every one of them. TransformStreamInbox is the implementation both providers use. TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate) Takes one received variable update off the queue, if there is one. Drained the same way and for the same reason as TryDequeueMessage(out NetworkMessage). public bool TryDequeueVariable(out NetworkVariableUpdate update) Parameters Type Name Description NetworkVariableUpdate update The update, when this returns true. Returns bool False when the queue is empty.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetworkGa.title: Class NetworkGateway | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.NetworkGa.summary: Class NetworkGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core's one entry point to netcode. Owns the INetworkProvider, refuses the session calls that are a user mistake, and drains the provider's two queues once per tick. AGENTS.md rules 44 to 49. public sealed class NetworkGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object NetworkGateway Examples runner.NetworkGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNetworkProvider()); runner.NetworkGateway.StartHost(); Remarks This is the netcode counterpart of CloudSaveGateway and is deliberately the same shape, because rule 49 poses the same problem rule 52 already solved: the core may not reference the backend, so the core owns an interface and a separate assembly implements it. This type is one of exactly five places the zero-allocation rule relaxes, named as "the services and network gateway" in AGENTS.md rule 31. What that rule permits is narrow: a request may allocate below a stated ceiling, and a pending request must allocate zero per tick. Tick is on the per-frame path and allocates nothing, which is why both queues are drained with TryDequeue rather than by iterating a returned collection. No session method throws because the network is unavailable. They throw only for a user mistake, which is starting a session while one is running. Being offline is a state a script reads through Net.IsConnected; rule 45. Fields DefaultMaximumTransformStreamBytes What a gateway with no provider reports. Chosen to be smaller than what any ordinary transport carries, so that a test running without one still exercises the split. public const int DefaultMaximumTransformStreamBytes = 1024 Field Value int DefaultTicksPerSecond The tick rate a gateway starts with: 30 a second, which is the rate the replaced NetworkTransform runs at. public const double DefaultTicksPerSecond = 30 Field Value double SmallestUsefulTransformStreamBytes The smallest budget that can carry one object: the stream's header and the largest an object's entry can be. public const int SmallestUsefulTransformStreamBytes = 31 Field Value int Properties HasProvider Whether a provider has been set. False means every session call is refused and every state reads as offline. public bool HasProvider { get; } Property Value bool IsConnected True when connected as host or client. False with no provider. public bool IsConnected { get; } Property Value bool IsHost True when this peer is the host. False with no provider. public bool IsHost { get; } Property Value bool MaximumTransformStreamBytes How many payload bytes of transform stream one send may carry. The provider's answer, or DefaultMaximumTransformStreamBytes when there is no provider. public int MaximumTransformStreamBytes { get; } Property Value int Remarks A provider that answers with less than one object's worth is corrected up to SmallestUsefulTransformStreamBytes, because a budget below that would put the runner in the position of either sending nothing or sending over the budget every tick, and sending over a budget the backend set is the provider's business to report rather than the runner's to hide. PeerCount Peers in the session including this one, or 0 with no provider. public int PeerCount { get; } Property Value int RoundTripMilliseconds Round trip time to the host in milliseconds, or 0 offline or on the host. public double RoundTripMilliseconds { get; } Property Value double State What the session is doing. Offline when no provider has been set, so a script may read this before anything is configured. public SessionState State { get; } Property Value SessionState TicksPerSecond How many times a second the transform stream is sent, whatever the frame rate is. 30 by default, which is the rate the replaced NetworkTransform runs at and the rate docs/netcode-bandwidth.md measured both stacks at. public double TicksPerSecond { get; set; } Property Value double Remarks AGENTS.md rule 47 says one stream per authority per tick, and this is what "tick" means: a rate of its own, not the frame rate. A game running at 120 frames a second sends 30 streams a second, and one running at 20 sends 20, because a tick cannot be sent in a frame that does not happen. Synchronised variables are not on this rate. Fields Abs = 0 The magnitude of the first operand, with no sign. Add = 10 The first operand plus the second. Ceiling = 2 The smallest whole number that is not less than the first operand. Clamp = 7 The first operand held between the second and the third. Divide = 13 The first operand divided by the second. Floor = 1 The largest whole number that is not greater than the first operand. Lerp = 8 The first operand moved towards the second by the fraction the third names, with no limit on that fraction. Max = 6 The larger of the first two operands. Min = 5 The smaller of the first two operands. Multiply = 12 The first operand times the second. Remainder = 9 What is left of the first operand after taking out whole multiples of the second. Round = 4 The whole number nearest the first operand, resolving a midpoint by the block's RoundingMode. Subtract = 11 The first operand minus the second. Truncate = 3 The first operand with its fractional part dropped, towards zero. Examples var block = new NumberFunctionBlock(NumberFunction.Abs, value, null, null, RoundingMode.ToEven); Remarks One enum serves both shapes deliberately: every function in the API semantics board's C01 answer has two documented forms, an expression that computes a value and a write that stores the result back into the variable it read, and both forms must mean the same thing. NumberMath is where each one is computed, once. The four arithmetic entries are here as well as on ArithmeticOperator, and the two tables are not redundant. ArithmeticOperator is what the C# operators + - * / % build, where both operands are written at the call site; this table is what a write applies to the variable's own value, where the first operand is the slot and is never written down. Health.Subtract(1.0) and Health.Set(Health - 1.0) reach the same arithmetic through the two tables.
