reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ObjectLif.summary: Struct ObjectLifetimeFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Object surface inside Build(): builds the blocks that create, activate, deactivate and end objects this script owns. public readonly struct ObjectLifetimeFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Object.Create("Shield")); On.Disabled(Object.Deactivate("Shield")); On.FrameUpdate(If(Health <= 0.0).Then(Object.Despawn())); Remarks The type is not called ObjectFactory, because UnityEditor.ObjectFactory already exists and this project's editor assembly uses it; two types of that name in scope make the editor assembly fail to compile. The script-facing surface is still written Object, which is what the settled contract-object-lifecycle answer names, and the type name is never written in a script. Self by omission. Omitting the name acts on the object the script runs on. Passing a name acts on an object Create(string, string, int) created under that name, in this same script. Create(string, string, int) and Spawn(Prefab, string, int) are the two calls that produce an object, and they are not the same call. Create(string, string, int) takes no asset and produces a bare, empty object under a name. Spawn(Prefab, string, int) produces one from a declared prefab input, and its chain places it, parents it and optionally holds it under a name. Both fill the same owned-object slot, so one name is produced by one of the two and addressed by the rest of this surface. The blocks reach the object through IScriptObjectLifetime, never through a UnityEngine.GameObject; AGENTS.md rule 24. A host that does not implement that interface cannot run a script containing these blocks, and the spawn is refused rather than the block failing later. Methods Activate(string, string, int) Builds a block that activates an object: the one this script runs on, or one this script created. public Block Activate(string name = null, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name its Create(string, string, int) used, or null for the object this script runs on. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: it is what records the line of the script this block was written on. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Enabled(Object.Activate("Shield")); On.Disabled(Object.Activate()); Remarks Omitting the name acts on the object the script runs on. That form records a LifetimeRequest, and the runner applies it after the current dispatch, which is what delivers On.Enabled between event invocations rather than inside one. Activating an already-active object delivers nothing. Passing a name acts on the object Create(string, string, int) created under it, and takes effect where it is written, because an owned object runs no LunyScript and raises no observation. A name for which the slot is empty is left alone. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException name is whitespace. A name no Create(string, string, int) in this script uses is refused when Build() finishes. Create(string, string, int) Builds a block that creates a new, empty, active object called name, owned by the instance that runs the block. public Block Create(string name, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name What the created object is called, and how this script addresses it. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: it is what records the line of the script this block was written on. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.Ready(Object.Create("Shield")); Remarks Owned means the API owns its lifetime: the object is destroyed when the instance that created it is despawned, by every path that despawns one. The name is both what the object is called in the scene and how the other calls on this surface address it; a scene object's name is one of the three kinds of literal AGENTS.md exempts from the nameof rule, because no C# member carries it. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException name is null or whitespace, or this script already creates an object under that name. Deactivate(string, string, int) Builds a block that deactivates an object: the one this script runs on, or one this script created. public Block Deactivate(string name = null, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name its Create(string, string, int) used, or null for the object this script runs on. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Health <= 0.0).Then(Object.Deactivate())); On.Disabled(Object.Deactivate("Shield")); Remarks Omitting the name acts on the object the script runs on. That form records a LifetimeRequest, and the runner applies it after the current dispatch, which is what delivers On.Disabled. Deactivating an already-inactive object delivers nothing. Passing a name acts on the owned object immediately. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException name is whitespace. Despawn(string, string, int) Builds a block that ends an object: the one this script runs on, or one this script created. public Block Despawn(string name = null, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name its Create(string, string, int) used, or null for the object this script runs on. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.LateUpdate(If(Fuse <= 0.0).Then(Object.Despawn())); On.Despawned(Object.Despawn("Shield")); Remarks Omitting the name ends the object the script runs on. That form records a LifetimeRequest, and the runner applies it after the current dispatch: it despawns the instance, which delivers On.Disabled and then On.Despawned while the object still exists, and destroys the object afterwards. Despawning an instance that is already despawned delivers nothing. Passing a name destroys that owned object and empties its slot, where it is written. A slot that is already empty is left alone: the owner's own despawn empties every slot, so despawning an owned object twice is ordinary rather than a failure. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException name is whitespace. Spawn(Operation<Prefab>, string, int) Starts a spawn from a succeeded prefab acquisition. The payload is readable after When.Operation(handle).Succeeded only. A spawn before Succeeded is refused at run. public SpawnBuilder Spawn(Operation<Prefab> acquisition, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Operation<Prefab> acquisition The typed handle a successful Asset.Load bound. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnBuilder A builder that takes a placement, a parent and a name, and converts to a block. Examples When.Operation(EnemyContent).Succeeded(Object.Spawn(EnemyContent)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException acquisition was never declared. Spawn(Prefab, string, int) Starts a spawn: builds an object from a declared prefab input, which the returned builder can place, parent and hold. public SpawnBuilder Spawn(Prefab prefab, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Prefab prefab The declared prefab input to produce an object from. Declared with [Asset] public Prefab X { get; private set; } or with Bind.Prefab. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: it is what records the line of the script this block was written on. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnBuilder A builder that takes a placement, a parent and a name, and converts to a block. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform..summary: Interface IGameClock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform Assembly ApiSource.dll A clock that drives a running game, so it carries the game's time scale and can be paused as well as read. Time.Scale, Time.IsPaused, Time.SetScale, Time.Pause and Time.Resume reach the clock through this interface. public interface IGameClock : ITimeSource Expand Details ... Inherited Members ITimeSource.DeltaSeconds ITimeSource.ElapsedSeconds ITimeSource.UnscaledDeltaSeconds ITimeSource.UnscaledElapsedSeconds Examples var clock = (IGameClock)runner.TimeSource; clock.Pause(); Remarks Why this is separate from ITimeSource. Every clock can report how much time passed; only a clock that governs a game's speed can be asked to change it. The editor session's clock reports elapsed edit-time seconds and governs no game, so it implements ITimeSource alone and a script that pauses the game cannot run on an editor runner. UnityTimeSource and TestKit.ManualTimeSource implement this one. This clock's pause is a time scale of zero, and resume restores the last positive scale this clock was set to. Time.IsPaused reads the runner flag, not this property: Time.Pause sets the flag and calls Pause(), and Time.SetScale(0) calls SetScale(double) without setting the flag. A scale set outside this clock - Unity's own Time.timeScale written by other code - changes what Scale reports and does not change what Resume() restores, because this clock did not set it. .NET 10 seam. ITimeSource's row in AGENTS.md section 4 is unchanged by this interface: System.TimeProvider replaces the reading half, and the scale and the pause stay the engine's, because no BCL type carries a game time scale. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform..title: Struct XorshiftRandomSource | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform..summary: Struct XorshiftRandomSource Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript.Platform Assembly ApiSource.dll The runtime IRandomSource: an explicit-state xorshift32 generator whose sequence is a function of its seed alone. public struct XorshiftRandomSource : IRandomSource Expand Details ... Implements IRandomSource Examples var first = new XorshiftRandomSource(42); var second = new XorshiftRandomSource(42); var a = first.NextDouble(); var b = second.NextDouble(); Remarks This is the consumer IRandomSource existed without. It does not read UnityEngine.Random, which is a static with hidden global state. It does not use System.Random either: that type's sequence is not the same on Mono, IL2CPP and CoreCLR, so a test that replayed a seed would not replay the draws. The algorithm is the xorshift32 Unity.Mathematics.Random uses; the core does not reference that package. A seed of zero is replaced with 0x6E624EB7 before the first step, because a zero state never leaves zero. That is the same substitution Unity.Mathematics.Random's default seed is. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Prefab.ht.title: Struct Prefab | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Prefab.ht.summary: Struct Prefab Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A handle to one prefab input of a script. Returned by Bind.Prefab at build time; what the input holds is an instance read, because the value belongs to the object and not to the script type. public readonly struct Prefab Expand Details ... Examples [Asset] public Prefab Sentry { get; private set; } On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Sentry).At(new Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)).Into("Guard")); Remarks This is the declared asset input of Asset<T>, narrowed to a prefab. It occupies an asset slot, it is declared in the same table, and it is resolved by the same three steps at spawn. The two differences are stated here because they are the whole reason the type exists. A prefab input refuses a GameObject that is not a prefab. An Asset<GameObject> is satisfied by any GameObject, including one dragged out of the Hierarchy, and a scene object assigned to an input a script spawns from is a mistake that shows up as a duplicated scene object rather than as a message. A value the host assigned that is not a prefab asset is refused at spawn, and the input then resolves as if nothing had been assigned. Object.Spawn takes this type and nothing else, so passing an Asset<AudioClip> or an Asset<GameObject> to a spawn does not compile. The declared name is the input's durable identity, the way it is for Asset<T>: a value stored on a host is matched to an input by that name, which is why the name comes from nameof and why renaming a declared input orphans what a scene stored for the old name. A handle is valid only inside the Build that declared it, for the reason Var<T> states: it carries a slot index and nothing that identifies its program. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReleaseGa.title: Class ReleaseGate | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReleaseGa.summary: Class ReleaseGate Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Gate 4. Runs inside a standalone player built without DEBUG and asserts what only that build can show: that operator true and operator false on a condition block still throw, that the [Conditional] contract guards are gone, and that the two guards written out unconditionally are not. public static class ReleaseGate Expand Details ... Inheritance object ReleaseGate Remarks AGENTS.md rule 38 says the two operators throw in release builds as well as debug, and that wrapping them in #if DEBUG is not allowed. Every run the Test Runner can produce defines DEBUG: the Editor does, and Player mode builds a development player. So the rule cannot be checked by a test alone, and this entry point exists instead. The gate is compiled in only when LUNY_RELEASE_GATE is defined, which PlayerBackendSettings.SetReleaseGate does and nothing else does. It quits the player with exit status 0 when every check passed and 1 when any failed, and writes one line per check so the log says which. Its first check is its own premise: it fails when DEBUG turns out to be defined, because a pass under DEBUG would prove nothing about a release build. Two of its checks are a matched pair and neither means much without the other. CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReleaseGate.ContractGuardsAreCompiledOut() passes when a [Conditional] guard does not throw in a build without DEBUG; CodeSmile.LunyScript.ReleaseGate.UnconditionalGuardsStillThrow() passes when the two guards that are deliberately unconditional do throw in that same build. Together they are what makes AGENTS.md rule 71's "a guard may be conditional only where the failure its removal gives up is loud" a measured rule rather than a stated one. Fields LogPrefix Prefix every line this gate logs carries, so a caller can find them in the player log. public const string LogPrefix = "LunyScript release gate | " Field Value string Remarks Tools/run-tests.sh greps the player log for this exact phrase, so it is composed from the one logging surface rather than written out again here; AGENTS.md rule 60. Changing either half changes what gate 4 reports. Methods Run() Runs the checks and returns how many failed. Callable from a test as well, which is what makes the same assertions visible in the Editor and in the development players; only the first check can differ between them, and it is the one the release build exists for. public static int Run() Returns int Number of failed checks. 0 means every check passed. Examples Assert.That(ReleaseGate.Run(), Is.Zero); RunOperatorChecks() Runs only the two operator checks, without the check that DEBUG is absent. A test calls this, because the Editor and every development player define DEBUG and would fail the premise check while the operators themselves behave correctly. public static int RunOperatorChecks() Returns int Number of failed checks. 0 means the implicit bool conversion threw and && constructed an AND node. Examples Assert.That(ReleaseGate.RunOperatorChecks(), Is.Zero);

Examples var facing = Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0); var reversed = facing.Inverse; Remarks The four components are readable and none of them is writable. Three of the four are not independent of the fourth: a quaternion that is not of length one is not an orientation, so writing one component alone produces a value that rotates and stretches. The API semantics board ruled on 2026-09-13 that a rotation is changed through its constructors or Compose(Rotation) rather than through its components. An input that names no orientation produces Identity. A quaternion of length zero and one carrying a NaN or an infinity are both refused that way rather than stored, so nothing downstream reads a value that is not a rotation. Euler(double, double, double) takes degrees and applies them in the order Z, then X, then Y, which is the order Unity's own euler-angle rotation uses, so a script that computes an orientation here and one that reads it off a transform agree. Constructors Rotation(double, double, double, double) Builds an orientation from four quaternion components, scaling them to length one. Components that name no orientation - a length of zero, or a NaN or an infinity among them - produce Identity. public Rotation(double x, double y, double z, double w) Parameters Type Name Description double x The first component. double y The second component. double z The third component. double w The fourth component. Examples var upright = new Rotation(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0); Fields Identity The orientation that turns nothing. public static readonly Rotation Identity Field Value Rotation Examples var upright = Rotation.Identity; Properties Inverse The orientation that undoes this one. public Rotation Inverse { get; } Property Value Rotation Examples var undone = facing.Inverse; W The fourth component of the quaternion. public float W { get; } Property Value float Examples var w = facing.W; X The first component of the quaternion. public float X { get; } Property Value float Examples var x = facing.X; Y The second component of the quaternion. public float Y { get; } Property Value float Examples var y = facing.Y; Z The third component of the quaternion. public float Z { get; } Property Value float Examples var z = facing.Z; Methods AngleTo(Rotation) How far apart two orientations are, in degrees, between 0 and 180. public double AngleTo(Rotation other) Parameters Type Name Description Rotation other The orientation to measure to. Returns double The angle in degrees. Examples var offBy = facing.AngleTo(wanted); Remarks An orientation and its four negated components name the same orientation, so the angle between them is zero rather than 360. That is what "antipodal equality" means here, and a tolerance comparison is written a.AngleTo(b) <= tolerance. ApplyTo(Vec3) A spatial value turned by this orientation. The value's length is unchanged. public Vec3 ApplyTo(Vec3 value) Parameters Type Name Description Vec3 value The value to turn. Returns Vec3 The turned value. Examples var worldOffset = facing.ApplyTo(new Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)); Compose(Rotation) This orientation applied after another one. public Rotation Compose(Rotation first) Parameters Type Name Description Rotation first The orientation applied first. Returns Rotation The combined orientation. Examples var combined = yaw.Compose(pitch); Remarks The argument is applied first and this one second, so yaw.Compose(pitch) pitches and then yaws. Equals(Rotation) Whether two values name the same orientation. Four negated components name the same orientation, so they compare equal. public bool Equals(Rotation other) Parameters Type Name Description Rotation other The orientation to compare against. Returns bool True when the components match exactly, or match exactly after negation. Examples var unchanged = facing.Equals(lastFacing); Equals(object) Whether this is an equal orientation of the same type. public override bool Equals(object obj) Parameters Type Name Description object obj What to compare against. Returns bool True when it is a Rotation naming the same orientation. Examples var same = facing.Equals((Object)other); Euler(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock) Builds an orientation expression out of three angle expressions, applied in the order Z, then X, then Y. public static RotationValueBlock Euler(NumberValueBlock xDegrees, NumberValueBlock yDegrees, NumberValueBlock zDegrees) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock xDegrees The angle around the first axis. NumberValueBlock yDegrees The angle around the second axis. NumberValueBlock zDegrees The angle around the third axis. Returns RotationValueBlock An orientation expression. Examples On.FrameUpdate(Facing.Set(Rotation.Euler(0.0, Heading, 0.0))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Any operand is null. Euler(double, double, double) Builds an orientation from three angles in degrees, applied in the order Z, then X, then Y. public static Rotation Euler(double xDegrees, double yDegrees, double zDegrees) Parameters Type Name Description double xDegrees The angle around the first axis. double yDegrees The angle around the second axis. double zDegrees The angle around the third axis. Returns Rotation The orientation those three angles name. Examples var facing = Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0); GetHashCode() A hash of the orientation, taken from the form whose first non-zero component is positive, so two values that compare equal hash equal. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int The hash. Examples var hash = facing.GetHashCode(); Slerp(Rotation, Rotation, double) An orientation a stated fraction of the way from one to another along the shortest arc. The fraction is not limited, matching scalar Math.Lerp. public static Rotation Slerp(Rotation from, Rotation to, double fraction) Parameters Type Name Description Rotation from Where the fraction 0 sits. Rotation to Where the fraction 1 sits. double fraction How far along to go. Returns Rotation The interpolated orientation. Examples var mid = Rotation.Slerp(from, to, 0.5); ToEuler() The three euler angles in degrees that name this orientation, in the order Unity writes them: Z, then X, then Y. public Vec3 ToEuler() Returns Vec3 X, Y and Z degrees. Examples var degrees = facing.ToEuler(); ToString() The four components, so a log line naming one reads as it was written. public override string ToString() Returns string The components in brackets. Examples var described = facing.ToString();

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.RoundingM.title: Enum RoundingMode | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.RoundingM.summary: Enum RoundingMode Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll How Math.Round and Var<Number>.Round resolve a value exactly halfway between two whole numbers. public enum RoundingMode Expand Details ... Fields AwayFromZero = 1 A midpoint goes away from zero: 0.5 becomes 1 and -0.5 becomes -1. This is what System.MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero does. ToEven = 0 A midpoint goes to the nearer even whole number: 0.5 and 1.5 both become 0 and 2. This is the default, and it is what System.MidpointRounding.ToEven does. Examples On.Ready(Score.Set(Math.Round(2.5))); // 2, midpoint to even On.Ready(Score.Set(Math.Round(2.5, RoundingMode.AwayFromZero))); // 3 Remarks The default is ToEven, which is the rule the API semantics board settled on 2026-09-13: "Round midpoint-to-even unless an explicit mode is supplied". Pass AwayFromZero to get the school rule instead.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.RoutineBu.title: Struct RoutineBuilder | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.RoutineBu.summary: Struct RoutineBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Routine(name) returns. Its one call, Run(params Block[]), takes the steps the routine runs in order and produces the block that starts an activation of it. public readonly struct RoutineBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Routine("Rescue").Run(InParallel(carry, callForHelp).UntilOneFinishes())); Remarks The block Run(params Block[]) returns is where the routine is started, not where it runs: executing it starts one activation on the object the block ran against, and the runner advances that activation once per frame until its last step finishes. Starting an activation while one is already running replaces it, cancelling the first. Methods Run(params Block[]) The steps this routine runs, in the order they are written. Each one finishes before the next begins. public Block Run(params Block[] steps) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] steps The steps. An ordinary block is one step and finishes in the call that runs it; an ActionBlock, such as a group, is advanced once per frame until it reports a result. Returns Block The block that starts one activation of this routine. Examples On.Ready(Routine("Patrol").Run(walkOut, waitAtPost, walkBack)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The step list is null, holds a null, is empty, or this builder was never obtained from a script's own Routine(name) call.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.RoutineGr.title: Struct RoutineGroupBuilder | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.RoutineGr.summary: Struct RoutineGroupBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What InParallel(...) returns: a concurrent group with no ending clause yet. public readonly struct RoutineGroupBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Routine("Open").Run(InParallel(slideDoor, playSound))); Remarks Used as it is, the group runs every child and waits for all of them, reporting Succeeded only if every child succeeded and Failed otherwise; a failure does not stop it early. The two clause calls replace that with an early ending. docs/execution-model.md, "Shared outcomes and concurrent groups", is the contract this shape implements. Properties Canceled A condition that is true once this group was cancelled before it produced a result. Cancellation is neither a success nor a failure, so Succeeded and Failed are both false for the same group. public ConditionBlock Canceled { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples var open = InParallel(slideDoor, playSound); On.Ready(Routine("Open").Run(open, If(open.Canceled).Then(retry.Set(true)))); Failed A condition that is true once this group has ended Failed. A group that was cancelled has no result, so neither this nor Succeeded is true for it; Canceled is what is true for that group. public ConditionBlock Failed { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples var open = InParallel(slideDoor, playSound); On.Ready(Routine("Open").Run(open, If(open.Failed).Then(alarm.Set(true)))); Succeeded A condition that is true once this group has ended Succeeded, for the routine steps written after it. public ConditionBlock Succeeded { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples var open = InParallel(slideDoor, playSound); On.Ready(Routine("Open").Run(open, If(open.Succeeded).Then(entered.Set(true)))); Methods UntilOneFinishes() The first child to reach a natural result, of either kind, ends this group with that result. Among children that became eligible in the same frame, the earliest declared one wins. public RoutineGroupEndingBuilder UntilOneFinishes() Returns RoutineGroupEndingBuilder The group, with that ending clause. Examples var race = InParallel(reachExit, timeOut).UntilOneFinishes(); UntilOneSucceeds() The first child to succeed ends this group Succeeded. A child that fails ends nothing on its own; the group ends Failed only when every child has failed. public RoutineGroupEndingBuilder UntilOneSucceeds() Returns RoutineGroupEndingBuilder The group, with that ending clause. Examples var anyRoute = InParallel(frontDoor, backDoor, window).UntilOneSucceeds(); Operators implicit operator Block(RoutineGroupBuilder) Finalises this group as a step of a routine. A bare composite that already describes buildable work needs no terminal call of its own. public static implicit operator Block(RoutineGroupBuilder builder) Parameters Type Name Description RoutineGroupBuilder builder The group. Returns Block Examples On.Ready(Routine("Open").Run(InParallel(slideDoor, playSound)));

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.RoutineGr.summary: Struct RoutineGroupEndingBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A concurrent group that carries an early-ending clause. Its one further call decides what happens to the children that had not finished when the group published its result. public readonly struct RoutineGroupEndingBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Routine("Race").Run(InParallel(reachExit, timeOut).UntilOneFinishes())); Remarks Without OthersKeepRunning() those children are cancelled at the moment the result is published. Properties Canceled A condition that is true once this group was cancelled before it produced a result. Cancellation is neither a success nor a failure, so Succeeded and Failed are both false for the same group. public ConditionBlock Canceled { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples var race = InParallel(reachExit, timeOut).UntilOneFinishes(); On.Ready(Routine("Race").Run(race, If(race.Canceled).Then(retry.Set(true)))); Failed A condition that is true once this group has ended Failed. public ConditionBlock Failed { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples var race = InParallel(reachExit, timeOut).UntilOneFinishes(); On.Ready(Routine("Race").Run(race, If(race.Failed).Then(caught.Set(true)))); Succeeded A condition that is true once this group has ended Succeeded. public ConditionBlock Succeeded { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples var race = InParallel(reachExit, timeOut).UntilOneFinishes(); On.Ready(Routine("Race").Run(race, If(race.Succeeded).Then(escaped.Set(true)))); Methods OthersKeepRunning() Leaves the children that had not finished running when this group published its result. The enclosing routine activation owns them from that moment, advances them while it runs, and cancels them when it ends or is itself cancelled. public RoutineGroupSurvivorBuilder OthersKeepRunning() Returns RoutineGroupSurvivorBuilder The group, with that ownership clause. Examples var arrival = InParallel(moveCamera, fadeMusic).UntilOneFinishes().OthersKeepRunning(); On.Ready(Routine("Arrival").Run(arrival, fadeInArrivalPanel)); Remarks What those children go on to report changes nothing: a published result is final. In the example, fadeInArrivalPanel remains Running for several frames, so the unfinished camera movement or music fade continues during that following routine step. Inheritance object RunnerDiagnostics Examples var current = runner.Diagnostics.ReadCurrent(runner.Diagnostics.GetIdentity(instance)); Remarks Caller-owned snapshots allocate only on explicit observation. Current-only Shallow coverage is the default. BeginTrace explicitly collects ordered action records; current snapshots do not contain historical values or a condition preview. Service work before a runtime provider is ready retains the existing gateway queue contract. Properties FailedBuildScript Script type associated with the latest failed Build. public string FailedBuildScript { get; } Property Value string Examples var script = runner.Diagnostics.FailedBuildScript; LatestBuildFailure Most recent failed Build, available even though no program or lifetime was created. public DiagnosticFault LatestBuildFailure { get; } Property Value DiagnosticFault Examples var error = runner.Diagnostics.LatestBuildFailure; LatestDriverFailure Latest outer failure. A contained block error appears on its instance snapshot instead. public DiagnosticFault LatestDriverFailure { get; } Property Value DiagnosticFault Examples var error = runner.Diagnostics.LatestDriverFailure; Methods Apply(DiagnosticCommand) Rechecks admission and applies backing state once without delivering gameplay or editor events. public void Apply(DiagnosticCommand command) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticCommand command Examples diagnostics.Apply(command); BeginTrace(DiagnosticIdentity, DiagnosticBuffer) Starts bounded action capture for a live target at an idle boundary. One attachment per lifetime is permitted. Non-development players require LUNYSCRIPT_TRACE when compiled. public DiagnosticTrace BeginTrace(DiagnosticIdentity target, DiagnosticBuffer buffer) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target DiagnosticBuffer buffer Returns DiagnosticTrace Examples var trace = diagnostics.BeginTrace(target, new DiagnosticBuffer(1024)); GetIdentity(ScriptInstance) Captures the identity before pooling can reuse the instance. public DiagnosticIdentity GetIdentity(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance Returns DiagnosticIdentity Examples var target = runner.Diagnostics.GetIdentity(instance); LiveLifetimes() Copies live identities; discovering them neither builds nor starts scripts. public DiagnosticIdentity[] LiveLifetimes() Returns DiagnosticIdentity[] Examples var targets = runner.Diagnostics.LiveLifetimes(); ReadCatalog(ScriptProgram) Returns immutable declarations built with the program, without executing blocks. public DiagnosticCatalog ReadCatalog(ScriptProgram program) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptProgram program Returns DiagnosticCatalog Examples var catalog = runner.Diagnostics.ReadCatalog(program); ReadCurrent(DiagnosticIdentity) Reads coherent stored state at an idle boundary. Busy, ended and failed boundaries report unavailable. public DiagnosticSnapshot ReadCurrent(DiagnosticIdentity target) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target Returns DiagnosticSnapshot Examples var current = runner.Diagnostics.ReadCurrent(target); Submit(DiagnosticIdentity, int, DiagnosticValue, bool, int) Admits a single typed live edit without applying it. Refusals carry an explicit reason. public DiagnosticCommand Submit(DiagnosticIdentity target, int variable, DiagnosticValue value, bool isLive = true, int major = 1) Parameters Type Name Description DiagnosticIdentity target int variable DiagnosticValue value bool isLive int major Returns DiagnosticCommand Examples var command = diagnostics.Submit(target, 0, DiagnosticValue.FromNumber(15.0)); Remarks Admission is synchronous. Up to 64 unapplied receipts can be retained; a full admission queue refuses new work. This is a pending-command bound, not a history retention policy.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Script.ht.summary: Class Script Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The runtime entry: a subclass whose Build() composes blocks that run on a game object. Editor workflows subclass EditorScript instead. [Serializable] public abstract class Script : ScriptBase Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptBase Script Inherited Members ScriptBase.Var ScriptBase.Define ScriptBase.Shared ScriptBase.Bind ScriptBase.When ScriptBase.Math ScriptBase.Random ScriptBase.Operation ScriptBase.Asset ScriptBase.If(ConditionBlock, string, int) ScriptBase.ForEach<T>(ListHandle<T>, string, int) ScriptBase.ForEach<TKey, TValue>(MapHandle<TKey, TValue>, string, int) ScriptBase.Routine(string, string, int) ScriptBase.InParallel(params Block[]) ScriptBase.Run(Block, string, int) ScriptBase.Run(Block, Block, params Block[]) ScriptBase.Choose(string, string, int) ScriptBase.Option(NumberValueBlock, string, int) ScriptBase.Seconds(double) ScriptBase.Milliseconds(double) ScriptBase.Minutes(double) ScriptBase.Hours(double) ScriptBase.Build() ScriptBase.DefineVariables() ScriptBase.DefineAssets() ScriptBase.RequireContext(string) Examples public sealed partial class CountdownScript : Script { [Variable(3)] public Var<Number> Health { get; private set; } [Variable(true)] public Var<Flag> Alive { get; private set; } protected override void Build() { On.FrameUpdate(If(Alive).Then(Health.Add(-1.0)).Else(Alive.Set(false))); } } Properties Audio Plays clips and controls authored Unity audio components. It hides UnityEngine.AudioSource inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. Available only inside Build(). protected AudioFactory Audio { get; } Property Value AudioFactory Examples On.CollisionEnter(Audio.PlayOneShot(BreakClip)); On.Ready(Audio.For(MotorSource).Play()); Remarks A one-shot plays on a runner-owned pooled voice. A bound source is the AudioSource already on an object. Mixer writes are a third surface. docs/proposals/audio.md is the family. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Body Observations of what physics actually did to this object. Available only inside Build(). protected BodyFactory Body { get; } Property Value BodyFactory Examples On.FixedUpdate(Travelled.Set(Body.PositionDelta)); Remarks Reading Body.PositionDelta in Build() is what opts this script type into the post-step copy. A script type that never reads it stores no previous position. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Camera What a camera rig tracks. It hides UnityEngine.Camera inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. Available only inside Build(). protected CameraFactory Camera { get; } Property Value CameraFactory Examples On.Ready(Camera.For(ChaseRig).Follow()); Remarks Runtime-only, and routed through Cinemachine; see View. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Cloud Builds the Cloud Save start blocks. Outcomes arrive through When.Cloud(key). Available only inside Build(). protected CloudFactory Cloud { get; } Property Value CloudFactory Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Gate Opens and closes named gates that suppress input or camera for every script on this runner. Available only inside Build(). protected GateFactory Gate { get; } Property Value GateFactory Examples On.Ready(Gate.Open("SceneLoad", GateCategory.Input | GateCategory.Camera)); Remarks A gate does not skip scripts. Pause is a separate system. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Input Declares the player input this script responds to, one local player at a time. It hides UnityEngine.Input inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. Available only inside Build(). protected InputFactory Input { get; } Property Value InputFactory Examples Move = Input.ForPlayer(0).Vector2("Move"); Remarks Runtime-only. Which backend supplies the actions is a runner service: CodeSmile.LunyScript.Input is the Input System adapter and the only place in the product that references that package. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Motion Builds blocks that move a kinematic or CharacterController body, push a dynamic body, or relocate the object. Available only inside Build(). protected MotionFactory Motion { get; } Property Value MotionFactory Examples On.FixedUpdate(Motion.MoveTo(Pad).AtSpeed(4.0)); On.FixedUpdate(Motion.AddForce(Thrust).InWorldSpace()); Remarks Motion is not Transform. Transform.MoveBy writes pose immediately, with no physics. Motion.MoveBy is component-directed and refuses a dynamic Rigidbody. Dynamic bodies use AddForce, AddImpulse, SetVelocity and StopMotion. Relocation that is not traversed movement is TeleportTo. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Net The session, authority and message surface. Available only inside Build(). protected NetFactory Net { get; } Property Value NetFactory Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Net.HasAuthority).Then(Score.Add(1.0))); Object Creates, activates, deactivates and ends objects this script owns. Available only inside Build(). protected ObjectLifetimeFactory Object { get; } Property Value ObjectLifetimeFactory Examples On.Ready(Object.Create("Shield")); Remarks The member hides System.Object for simple-name lookup inside a Script subclass. That is the settled surface name from the contract-object-lifecycle answer, and a subclass that needs the type writes System.Object, which this codebase does not do on the run-time path anyway. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). On Registers blocks against the runner's events. Available only inside Build(). This surface has no EditorUpdate; that lives on EditorScript. protected OnFactory On { get; } Property Value OnFactory Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Other The other collider of the contact event currently running. Available only inside Build(), and the blocks it builds run only inside a contact event. protected OtherFactory Other { get; } Property Value OtherFactory Examples On.CollisionEnter(If(Other.HasTag("Player")).Then(Score.Add(1.0))); On.TriggerStay(HitAt.Set(Other.WorldPosition)); Remarks The same members exist on all six contact events, because they are properties of the other collider. A read outside those events throws when the block runs. docs/proposals/physics-contact-events.md is the surface. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Panel Binds, places and opens UI Toolkit panels. It hides PanelRenderer inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. Available only inside Build(). protected PanelFactory Panel { get; } Property Value PanelFactory Examples var health = Panel.Label("health"); health.BindText(Text.Format("{0}% HP", Health)); Remarks Runtime-only. The supported scene component is PanelRenderer; UIDocument is not probed. A scene-free editor host reports once and writes nothing. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Sync Which parts of this object's transform cross the network, and how often each one is sent. Available only inside Build(). protected SyncFactory Sync { get; } Property Value SyncFactory Examples Sync.Position(SyncCadence.EveryTick); Time The running game's clock and its time scale, available only inside Build(). It hides UnityEngine.Time inside a script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform: inside a Script, Time means this one. protected TimeFactory Time { get; } Property Value TimeFactory Examples On.FrameUpdate(Age.Add(Time.Delta)); Remarks Runtime-only. An explicitly owned editor runner's clock governs no game, so it has no scale to read or stop; EditorTime.Elapsed() is that session's own reading. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Transform Builds blocks that move and rotate the object this script runs on. Available only inside Build(). protected TransformFactory Transform { get; } Property Value TransformFactory Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). View Chooses what a local player sees: which camera rig a view renders, and how much of the screen it takes. Available only inside Build(). protected ViewFactory View { get; } Property Value ViewFactory Examples On.Ready(View.For(Screen).SetCamera(ChaseRig)); Remarks Runtime-only, and routed through Cinemachine: with that package absent no provider is installed and every block on this surface writes nothing and says so once. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Methods SetProcessMode(Process, string, int) Sets this script type's default process mode. Inherit, the default, walks the Unity transform parent chain and is Pausable when the walk ends. protected void SetProcessMode(Process mode, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Process mode Whether instances of this type tick while the runner is paused. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Examples SetProcessMode(Process.WhenPaused); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Called outside Build(), called twice, or mode is not a defined Process value.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBas.title: Class ScriptBase | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBas.summary: Class ScriptBase Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Shared infrastructure for Script and EditorScript. One instance of a concrete subclass is compiled into one ScriptProgram, once, and every object running that script shares it. [Serializable] public abstract class ScriptBase Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptBase Derived EditorScript Script Examples public sealed partial class CountdownScript : Script { [Variable(3)] public Var<Number> Health { get; private set; } [Variable(true)] public Var<Flag> Alive { get; private set; } protected override void Build() { On.FrameUpdate(If(Health > 0.0).Then(Health.Add(-1.0)).Else(Alive.Set(false))); When.Var(Alive).Changed(Health.Set(0.0)); } } Remarks Build() runs once per script type, before any object exists. It cannot read an inspector value, an object name or anything else about a particular object; declare a variable and fill it at spawn instead. AGENTS.md rule 25. Calls made while Build() runs construct the shared Script program once per Script type. The blocks those calls return execute later, per event and per Script instance. Confusing those phases is the largest defect class in this design. AGENTS.md rule 43. Properties Asset Starts and ends content acquisitions. Available only inside Build(). protected AssetFactory Asset { get; } Property Value AssetFactory Examples EnemyContent = Operation.Define<Prefab>(nameof(EnemyContent)); On.Ready(Asset.Load(EnemyPrefab).As(EnemyContent)); Remarks Asset.Load(source).As(handle) is an asynchronous attempt. Declared [Asset] inputs remain spawn-time resolution and are not this factory. Asset.Load does not load a scene. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Bind Declares the assets this script needs. Available during generated asset-input declaration or Build(). protected BindFactory Bind { get; } Property Value BindFactory Examples OpenSound = Bind.Asset<AudioClip>(nameof(OpenSound)); Remarks What an input holds belongs to the object, not to the script type: it is resolved when an object spawns, from what that object assigns, then the input's own declared source, then the default registered for its type. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Define Declares this script's variables with the author spelling Round 06 settled. Available during generated variable initialization or Build(). protected DefineFactory Define { get; } Property Value DefineFactory Examples Health = Define.Number(nameof(Health), 100); TeamScore = Define.Number(nameof(TeamScore), 0).Shared(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Math The core numeric functions, available only inside Build(). It hides System.Math inside a script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform: inside a Script, Math means this one. protected MathFactory Math { get; } Property Value MathFactory Examples On.FrameUpdate(Health.Set(Math.Clamp(Health + Healing, 0.0, 100.0))); Operation Declares operation handles with one observable attempt each, available only inside Build(). protected OperationFactory Operation { get; } Property Value OperationFactory Examples LoadingArena = Operation.Define(nameof(LoadingArena)); When.Operation(LoadingArena).Failed(ShowError.Set(true)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Random Named random streams and draws that store a result, available only inside Build(). protected RandomFactory Random { get; } Property Value RandomFactory Examples var loot = Random.Stream("loot", 42); On.Ready(Random.Number().From(loot).In(1.0, 100.0).Into(Roll)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Shared Operations on a shared store. Available only inside Build(). protected SharedFactory Shared { get; } Property Value SharedFactory Examples On.Ready(Shared.Clear()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Var Declares this script's variables. Available during generated variable initialization or Build(). protected VarFactory Var { get; } Property Value VarFactory Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). When Registers blocks against a change in state. Available only inside Build(). protected WhenFactory When { get; } Property Value WhenFactory Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Methods Build() protected abstract void Build() Choose(string, string, int) Opens a scored choice. Highest names the options; optional Bias and Hold follow; used as a block it starts the selector. protected ChooseBuilder Choose(string subject, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string subject What this selector is called in a diagnostic and in the runtime inspector. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns ChooseBuilder The builder whose Highest call takes the options. Examples On.Ready(Choose("needs").Highest( Option(WorkScore).Then(Work), Option(RestScore).Then(Rest)).Bias(0.1).Hold(Seconds(1))); DefineAssets() Assigns generated asset-input handles before Build, after the variables. Source-generated overrides call the base implementation first so inherited declarations keep their order. protected virtual void DefineAssets() Remarks Written by the same generator that writes DefineVariables(). Use [Asset] properties in a partial Script subclass, or keep explicit Bind.Asset calls inside Build. It is a second hook rather than more lines in the first because the two declare different things: a variable is storage this script owns and an asset input is a value an object supplies. Both run before Build(), which is what lets Build() use either. DefineVariables() Assigns generated variable handles before Build. Source-generated overrides call the base implementation first so inherited declarations keep their order. protected virtual void DefineVariables() Remarks Written by the LunyScript variable generator. Use [Variable] properties in a partial Script subclass, or keep explicit Var.Define calls inside Build. ForEach<T>(ListHandle<T>, string, int) Visits each list entry present at loop entry. Nested ForEach is refused. protected ForEachListBuilder<T> ForEach<T>(ListHandle<T> list, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where T : struct Parameters Type Name Description ListHandle<T> list The list to visit. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns ForEachListBuilder<T> A builder whose Do takes the visit body. Type Parameters T The list element kind. Examples On.FrameUpdate(ForEach(Slots).Do(id => Hits.Add(id))); ForEach<TKey, TValue>(MapHandle<TKey, TValue>, string, int) Visits each map pair present at loop entry, in insertion order. Nested ForEach is refused. protected ForEachMapBuilder<TKey, TValue> ForEach<TKey, TValue>(MapHandle<TKey, TValue> map, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) where TKey : struct where TValue : struct Parameters Type Name Description MapHandle<TKey, TValue> map The map to visit. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns ForEachMapBuilder<TKey, TValue> A builder whose Do takes the visit body. Type Parameters TKey TValue Examples On.FrameUpdate(ForEach(Scores).Do((key, value) => Hits.Add(value))); Hours(double) An elapsed duration of this many hours, for Hold. protected Elapsed Hours(double amount) Parameters Type Name Description double amount How many hours. Returns Elapsed Examples Hold(Hours(1)) If(ConditionBlock, string, int) Starts a conditional block. protected IfBuilder If(ConditionBlock condition, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description ConditionBlock condition The condition to test, built from a variable's operators. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: this is where the whole If chain records the line it was written on, because Then and Else take a params array and C# allows no parameter after one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns IfBuilder A builder whose Then names the blocks to run. Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(health > 0.0).Then(health.Add(-1.0))); InParallel(params Block[]) A concurrent group: every child advances each frame, in the order they are written, inside one step of a routine. protected RoutineGroupBuilder InParallel(params Block[] children) Parameters Type Name Description Block[] children The children, in declaration order. Returns RoutineGroupBuilder The group, ready to be used as a routine step or given an ending clause. Examples On.Ready(Routine("Open").Run(InParallel(slideDoor, playSound))); Remarks As written, the group runs every child and waits for all of them, reporting Succeeded only if every child succeeded. UntilOneFinishes() and UntilOneSucceeds() replace that with an early ending, and OthersKeepRunning() follows either of those to keep the unfinished children running under the enclosing routine activation. This factory takes a params array, so C# allows it no parameter after the children and it captures no authored line; AGENTS.md rule 72. The routine step that carries the group is what a diagnostic names. Milliseconds(double) An elapsed duration of this many milliseconds, for Hold. protected Elapsed Milliseconds(double amount) Parameters Type Name Description double amount How many milliseconds. Returns Elapsed Examples Hold(Milliseconds(500)) Minutes(double) An elapsed duration of this many minutes, for Hold. protected Elapsed Minutes(double amount) Parameters Type Name Description double amount How many minutes. Returns Elapsed Examples Hold(Minutes(2)) Option(NumberValueBlock, string, int) One scored option of a Choose selector. Then names the action that runs while this option is selected. protected UtilityOptionBuilder Option(NumberValueBlock score, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock score The current score. All finite signed scores are legal; the largest wins. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns UtilityOptionBuilder The builder whose Then call takes the action. Examples Option(WorkScore).Then(Work) RequireContext(string) protected ScriptBuildContext RequireContext(string surface) Parameters Type Name Description string surface Returns ScriptBuildContext Routine(string, string, int) Opens a sequential routine: steps that run in the order they are written, each one finishing before the next begins, over as many frames as they need. protected RoutineBuilder Routine(string name, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name What this routine is called in a diagnostic and in the runtime inspector. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler; the file the call was written in. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler; the line the call was written on. Returns RoutineBuilder The builder whose Run call takes the steps. Examples On.Ready(Routine("Patrol").Run(walkOut, waitAtPost, walkBack)); Run(Block, Block, params Block[]) Opens independently advanced repeating work whose body has more than one block. This overload takes a params array, so it captures no authored line; AGENTS.md rule 72. protected RunWorkBuilder Run(Block first, Block second, params Block[] more) Parameters Type Name Description Block first The first block of the body. Block second The second block of the body. Block[] more Any further blocks, in order. Returns RunWorkBuilder The builder whose For, Every, Start and Stop finish the chain. Examples var pulse = Run(windUp, Hits.Add(1.0)).For(3).Seconds(); Run(Block, string, int) Opens independently advanced repeating work. Qualifiers name a duration, a cadence, or a repetition count. Start() starts one activation; declaration does not. protected RunWorkBuilder Run(Block body, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description Block body The blocks each activation runs, in order. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns RunWorkBuilder The builder whose For, Every, Start and Stop finish the chain. Examples var pulse = Run(Hits.Add(1.0)).For(3).Seconds(); var tick = Run(Hits.Add(1.0)).Every(3).Seconds(); var burst = Run(Hits.Add(1.0)).Every(3).Seconds().For(5).Times(); var continuous = Run(Hits.Add(1.0)); On.Ready(pulse.Start(), tick.Start(), burst.Start(), continuous.Start()); Seconds(double) An elapsed duration of this many seconds, for Hold. protected Elapsed Seconds(double amount) Parameters Type Name Description double amount How many seconds. Returns Elapsed Examples Hold(Seconds(1))

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBui.title: Class ScriptBuildContext | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBui.summary: Class ScriptBuildContext Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The state one Build() accumulates: the slots its variables declared and the blocks its event registrations produced. Exists for the duration of one build and is then turned into an immutable ScriptProgram. public sealed class ScriptBuildContext Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptBuildContext Remarks Everything here allocates, and that is correct: a build runs once per script type at launch, never per object and never per frame. Calls made while Build() runs construct that shared program; the blocks they return execute later, per event and per Script instance. AGENTS.md rule 21 and rule 43. Properties ScriptType The script type being built. Named in every diagnostic this build can raise. public Type ScriptType { get; } Property Value Type
