[Flags] public enum ScriptContexts Expand Details ... Fields Editor = 2 Explicitly owned edit-time execution. None = 0 No permitted execution context. Runtime = 1 Game execution, including Editor Play Mode. Shared = Runtime | Editor Both execution contexts. Examples public override ScriptContexts Contexts => ScriptContexts.Shared;

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptIns.title: Class ScriptInstance | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptIns.summary: Class ScriptInstance Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One object's state for one program: the slot arrays the program's layout asked for, and the host the blocks act on. The blocks themselves are shared by every instance of the program and hold no per-object state at all. public sealed class ScriptInstance Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptInstance Examples var instance = runner.Spawn(program, host); instance.SetNumber(health.NumberSlot, 100.0); Remarks "Swapping the context" means passing a different ScriptInstance to the same block object. Nothing is copied and nothing is rebound. See AGENTS.md rule 21 and docs/execution-model.md. An instance is reusable: Rebind(IScriptHost) points it at another host and ResetToDefaults() puts every slot back to its declared starting value, both without allocating. That is what makes pooling a memory copy rather than a spawn. Constructors ScriptInstance(ScriptProgram, IScriptHost) Allocates the slot arrays the layout asks for and copies the declared defaults into them. This is the one allocation the spawn boundary permits, and its size is exactly what SlotBytes predicts plus one array header per SlotArrayCount. public ScriptInstance(ScriptProgram program, IScriptHost host) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptProgram program The program this instance runs. IScriptHost host The object the blocks act on. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException program or host is null. Fields NoNetworkObject What NetworkObjectId holds while this instance is bound to no networked object. public const int NoNetworkObject = 0 Field Value int Properties AssetInputCount How many asset inputs this instance holds, which is how many its script declared. public int AssetInputCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(instance.AssetInputCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); CanProcess Whether process events run on this instance given the runner's paused flag and this instance's effective process mode. Cached next to IsEnabled; recomputed when the runner pauses, when this instance is spawned, and when it is reparented, never every frame. public bool CanProcess { get; } Property Value bool HasNetworkAuthority True when this peer holds authority over the object this instance runs on. False for an instance bound to no networked object, and for every peer while there is no session. public bool HasNetworkAuthority { get; } Property Value bool Remarks Refreshed once per tick by ScriptRunner, so every block that reads it within one frame reads the same answer. AGENTS.md rule 45 requires that authority is visible rather than hidden, and an answer that could change between two blocks of one frame would be visible and useless. Host The object this instance's blocks act on. Never a GameObject directly; see AGENTS.md rule 24. public IScriptHost Host { get; } Property Value IScriptHost IsEnabled Whether the runner runs this instance's per-frame blocks. Driven by the host's own enable and disable, which Unity owns; LunyScript re-implements none of it. public bool IsEnabled { get; } Property Value bool IsFaulted True after an action failure, until explicitly re-enabled or respawned. public bool IsFaulted { get; } Property Value bool Examples if (instance.IsFaulted) runner.SetEnabled(instance, true); IsPooled Whether this instance is currently in a pool rather than attached to a live object. public bool IsPooled { get; } Property Value bool IsReady Whether On.Ready has already run for this instance. public bool IsReady { get; } Property Value bool NetworkObjectId Which networked object this instance is bound to, or NoNetworkObject when it is bound to none. public int NetworkObjectId { get; } Property Value int Remarks Assigned by ScriptRunner.BindNetworkObject, which the Netcode assembly calls when Netcode for GameObjects spawns the object. An instance with no binding takes no part in the network tick: it sends nothing, receives nothing, and its writes are never refused. OwnedObjectCount How many owned-object slots this instance has. public int OwnedObjectCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(instance.OwnedObjectCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); PendingLifetime What an authored Object.Activate(), Object.Deactivate() or Object.Despawn() asked for and the runner has not applied yet. public LifetimeRequest PendingLifetime { get; } Property Value LifetimeRequest Examples Assert.That(instance.PendingLifetime, Is.EqualTo(LifetimeRequest.None)); Remarks One request at a time: a later request in the same dispatch replaces an earlier one, because the last thing the script said is what it means. LifetimeRequest states why the request is recorded rather than applied on the spot. Program The program whose blocks run against this instance. public ScriptProgram Program { get; } Property Value ScriptProgram Methods AppendTextSlot<TDestination>(in TextSlot, ref TDestination) Appends one text slot's bytes onto the end of a fixed-capacity buffer, rather than replacing what the buffer holds the way ReadText<TDestination>(in TextSlot, ref TDestination) does. public FormatError AppendTextSlot<TDestination>(in TextSlot slot, ref TDestination destination) where TDestination : unmanaged, INativeList<byte>, IUTF8Bytes Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot slot The text slot to read. TDestination destination The buffer to append onto. Returns FormatError FormatError.None, or FormatError.Overflow when the buffer is too small for what this slot holds. Type Parameters TDestination The fixed-string type of the buffer. Examples var error = instance.AppendTextSlot(slot, ref buffer); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance, or its capacity is not one of the five. CopyTextSlot(in TextSlot, in TextSlot) Copies one text slot into another. Allocates nothing. public void CopyTextSlot(in TextSlot destination, in TextSlot source) Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot destination The slot written. TextSlot source The slot read. Examples instance.CopyTextSlot(lastWinner.TextSlot, playerName.TextSlot); Remarks Copying a slot onto itself does nothing and leaves the text as it was. The check is required rather than tidy: SetText reaches FixedString.CopyFrom, which empties the destination before it appends the source, so a self-copy without this early return would clear the variable and report no error. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The source text does not fit in the destination's declared capacity. The destination is left unchanged. GetAsset(int) The asset in one input slot, by index. The tooling path, for a caller holding a program and a slot rather than a typed handle. public Object GetAsset(int slotIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int slotIndex The slot, as AssetInputIndex(string) reports it. Returns Object The asset that slot resolved to. Examples var asset = instance.GetAsset(program.AssetInputIndex("OpenSound")); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This program has no slot of that index. GetAsset<T>(in Asset<T>) The asset one of this script's declared inputs holds on this object. public T GetAsset<T>(in Asset<T> input) where T : Object Parameters Type Name Description Asset<T> input The handle Build() assigned to the script's own property. Returns T The asset this object resolved that input to. Type Parameters T The asset type the input was declared with. Examples var clip = behaviour.GetAsset(script.OpenSound); Remarks The value is never null and is always of the declared type. It was resolved when this object spawned, from what the host stored, then the input's declared source, then the asset placeholder for its type; an input that none of the three could supply refused the spawn, so an instance that exists has every input filled. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle was never declared, or it addresses a slot this program does not have, which is what a handle borrowed from another script does. GetEnum(in EnumSlot) Reads one enum slot as its stored integer code. public long GetEnum(in EnumSlot slot) Parameters Type Name Description EnumSlot slot Which slot to read. Returns long The declared enum integer code. Examples var code = instance.GetEnum(slot); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. GetFlag(in FlagSlot) Reads a Flag slot. public bool GetFlag(in FlagSlot slot) Parameters Type Name Description FlagSlot slot Which slot to read. Returns bool The value this instance currently holds in that slot. Examples var alive = instance.GetFlag(isAlive.FlagSlot); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is not one of this instance's, which almost always means the handle was declared by a different script type. GetNumber(in NumberSlot) Reads a Number slot. public double GetNumber(in NumberSlot slot) Parameters Type Name Description NumberSlot slot Which slot to read. Returns double The value this instance currently holds in that slot. Examples var current = instance.GetNumber(health.NumberSlot); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is not one of this instance's, which almost always means the handle was declared by a different script type. GetRotation(in RotationSlot) Reads one orientation slot. public Rotation GetRotation(in RotationSlot slot) Parameters Type Name Description RotationSlot slot Which slot to read. Returns Rotation What the slot holds. Examples var facing = instance.GetRotation(slot); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. GetVec2(in Vec2Slot) Reads one two-component spatial slot. public Vec2 GetVec2(in Vec2Slot slot) Parameters Type Name Description Vec2Slot slot Which slot to read. Returns Vec2 What the slot holds. Examples var stick = instance.GetVec2(slot); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. GetVec3(in Vec3Slot) Reads one spatial slot. public Vec3 GetVec3(in Vec3Slot slot) Parameters Type Name Description Vec3Slot slot Which slot to read. Returns Vec3 What the slot holds. Examples var position = instance.GetVec3(slot); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. InputOccurred(int, InputPhase) Whether one occurrence happened to one of this script's declared input actions during the frame that is running. public bool InputOccurred(int declarationIndex, InputPhase phase) Parameters Type Name Description int declarationIndex Which declaration, as the handle carries it. InputPhase phase Which occurrence to ask about. Returns bool True when it happened this frame. Examples var fired = instance.InputOccurred(0, InputPhase.Performed); IsInputPressed(int) Whether one of this script's declared input actions is held down now. public bool IsInputPressed(int declarationIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int declarationIndex Which declaration, as the handle carries it. Returns bool False while the control is at rest, and for an action that did not resolve. Examples var pressed = instance.IsInputPressed(0); OwnedObject(int) The object one owned-object slot holds, or null when the slot is empty. public IScriptHost OwnedObject(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index The slot, as OwnedObjectIndex(string) reports it. Returns IScriptHost The host naming the created object, or null. Examples var shield = instance.OwnedObject(program.OwnedObjectIndex("Shield")); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The index is not one of this instance's slots. ReadInputNumber(int) One of this script's declared input actions, as a number. public double ReadInputNumber(int declarationIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int declarationIndex Which declaration, as the handle carries it. Returns double The value, 0 at rest and for an action that did not resolve. Examples var throttle = instance.ReadInputNumber(0); ReadInputVector(int) One of this script's declared input actions, as a spatial value. public Vec3 ReadInputVector(int declarationIndex) Parameters Type Name Description int declarationIndex Which declaration, as the handle carries it. Returns Vec3 The value, the zero vector at rest and for an action that did not resolve. A two-component action leaves the third component zero. Examples var move = instance.ReadInputVector(0); ReadTextAsString(in TextSlot) Reads a text slot as a managed string. Allocates one string per call and exists for diagnostics and tests only; no block calls it. Use ReadText<TDestination>(in TextSlot, ref TDestination) on the run-time path. public string ReadTextAsString(in TextSlot slot) Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot slot Which slot to read. Returns string The slot's text. Examples Assert.That(instance.ReadTextAsString(playerName.TextSlot), Is.EqualTo("Player One")); ReadText<TDestination>(in TextSlot, ref TDestination) Copies a text slot into a caller-provided fixed string. Allocates nothing. public CopyError ReadText<TDestination>(in TextSlot slot, ref TDestination destination) where TDestination : unmanaged, INativeList<byte>, IUTF8Bytes Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot slot Which slot to read. TDestination destination Where the text is written. Its previous content is replaced. Returns CopyError CopyError.None, or CopyError.Truncation when the destination is too small, in which case the destination is unchanged. Type Parameters TDestination A Unity.Collections fixed-string type. Examples var buffer = new FixedString128Bytes(); instance.ReadText(playerName.TextSlot, ref buffer); Rebind(IScriptHost) Points this instance at another host, so that a pooled instance can be respawned on a different object without allocating. public void Rebind(IScriptHost host) Parameters Type Name Description IScriptHost host The object the blocks act on from now on. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException host is null. ResetToDefaults() Puts every slot back to the value its variable declared, without allocating. A pooled instance is respawned by calling Rebind(IScriptHost) and then this. public void ResetToDefaults() Examples instance.Rebind(newHost); instance.ResetToDefaults(); // allocates nothing SetEnum(in EnumSlot, long) Writes one enum slot as an integer code. public void SetEnum(in EnumSlot slot, long code) Parameters Type Name Description EnumSlot slot Which slot to write. long code The declared enum integer code. Examples instance.SetEnum(slot, 1); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. SetFlag(in FlagSlot, bool) Writes a Flag slot. public void SetFlag(in FlagSlot slot, bool value) Parameters Type Name Description FlagSlot slot Which slot to write. bool value The value to store. Examples instance.SetFlag(isAlive.FlagSlot, false); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is not one of this instance's, which almost always means the handle was declared by a different script type. SetNumber(in NumberSlot, double) Writes a Number slot. public void SetNumber(in NumberSlot slot, double value) Parameters Type Name Description NumberSlot slot Which slot to write. double value The value to store. Examples instance.SetNumber(health.NumberSlot, 100.0); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is not one of this instance's, which almost always means the handle was declared by a different script type. SetRotation(in RotationSlot, in Rotation) Writes one orientation slot. public void SetRotation(in RotationSlot slot, in Rotation value) Parameters Type Name Description RotationSlot slot Which slot to write. Rotation value What to store. Examples instance.SetRotation(slot, Rotation.Identity); Remarks There is no authority guard here, for the reason SetVec3(in Vec3Slot, in Vec3) states. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. SetText<TSource>(in TextSlot, in TSource) Writes a text slot from any fixed string, whatever its capacity. Allocates nothing. public void SetText<TSource>(in TextSlot slot, in TSource value) where TSource : unmanaged, INativeList<byte>, IUTF8Bytes Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot slot Which slot to write. TSource value The text to store. Type Parameters TSource A Unity.Collections fixed-string type. Examples var name = new FixedString64Bytes("Player One"); instance.SetText(playerName.TextSlot, in name); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The text does not fit in the slot's declared capacity. The slot is left unchanged. SetVec2(in Vec2Slot, in Vec2) Writes one two-component spatial slot. public void SetVec2(in Vec2Slot slot, in Vec2 value) Parameters Type Name Description Vec2Slot slot Which slot to write. Vec2 value What to store. Examples instance.SetVec2(slot, new Vec2(1.0, 0.0)); Remarks There is no authority guard here, for the reason SetVec3(in Vec3Slot, in Vec3) states. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. SetVec3(in Vec3Slot, in Vec3) Writes one spatial slot. public void SetVec3(in Vec3Slot slot, in Vec3 value) Parameters Type Name Description Vec3Slot slot Which slot to write. Vec3 value What to store. Examples instance.SetVec3(slot, new Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)); Remarks There is no authority guard here, because a spatial variable cannot be synchronised in this version: Var.DefineSynced refuses the two spatial kinds where they are declared, so no spatial slot is ever a synchronised one. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The slot is outside this instance. TextEquals<TOther>(in TextSlot, in TOther) Whether a text slot holds exactly this text. Allocates nothing. public bool TextEquals<TOther>(in TextSlot slot, in TOther other) where TOther : unmanaged, INativeList<byte>, IUTF8Bytes Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot slot Which slot to compare. TOther other The text to compare against. Returns bool True when the slot's bytes and length match. Type Parameters TOther A Unity.Collections fixed-string type. Examples var expected = new FixedString64Bytes("Player One"); var same = instance.TextEquals(playerName.TextSlot, in expected); TextLength(in TextSlot) How many UTF-8 bytes a text slot currently holds. public int TextLength(in TextSlot slot) Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot slot Which slot to measure. Returns int The slot's current length in bytes, which is 0 for an empty one. Examples var bytes = instance.TextLength(playerName.TextSlot); TextSlotsEqual(in TextSlot, in TextSlot) Whether two text slots hold the same text. Allocates nothing. public bool TextSlotsEqual(in TextSlot left, in TextSlot right) Parameters Type Name Description TextSlot left The first slot. TextSlot right The second slot. Returns bool True when both slots hold the same bytes. Examples var same = instance.TextSlotsEqual(playerName.TextSlot, lastWinner.TextSlot);

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptPro.title: Class ScriptProgram | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptPro.summary: Class ScriptProgram Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One script type, built. Holds the immutable block tree, the On.* event table and the instance layout, and is shared by every object running that script. public sealed class ScriptProgram Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptProgram Examples var program = runner.GetOrBuildProgram(new PlayerScript()); var instance = runner.Spawn(program, host); Remarks A program is built once per script type, not once per object. The predecessor called Build() once per object, at roughly ninety managed allocations per spawn, which made it unusable for a game that spawns enemies and pickups. AGENTS.md rule 21; docs/execution-model.md has the whole model. Nothing on a program is mutable. Per-object state lives in slots on a ScriptInstance, and running the same block against a different instance is all that "swapping the context" means. Properties AssetInputCount How many asset inputs this script declares. public int AssetInputCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(program.AssetInputCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); AuthorityGainedBlockCount Number of blocks On.Authority.Gained registered. public int AuthorityGainedBlockCount { get; } Property Value int AuthorityLostBlockCount Number of blocks On.Authority.Lost registered. public int AuthorityLostBlockCount { get; } Property Value int BuiltScript The one object of ScriptType whose Build() produced this program, and therefore the one object whose variable properties were assigned. Read a variable from this object; every other object of the same script type keeps its variable properties at their defaults, because Build() runs once per script type. public ScriptBase BuiltScript { get; } Property Value ScriptBase Examples var script = (PlayerScript)instance.Program.BuiltScript; var health = instance.GetNumber(script.Health.NumberSlot); Remarks Script returns this object from Awake onward, which is how a component reaches it without holding a program. docs/slice-decisions.md D4.42 records the decision, what it costs, and the one ordering hazard: a component with a negative DefaultExecutionOrder that caches behaviour.Script in its own Awake caches the prototype in the serialized field, because LunyScriptBehaviour.Awake has not run yet. FrameUpdateBlockCount Number of blocks On.FrameUpdate registered. public int FrameUpdateBlockCount { get; } Property Value int InputActionCount How many input actions this script declared. public int InputActionCount { get; } Property Value int Examples var count = program.InputActionCount; Remarks A declaration belongs to the script type rather than to the object, so this is also how many entries InputGateway.ResolutionsFor produces for this program. IsNetworked True when this script declares at least one synchronised variable, which is what makes an instance of it take part in the network tick at all. public bool IsNetworked { get; } Property Value bool Layout How many slots of each kind every instance of this program owns. public InstanceLayout Layout { get; } Property Value InstanceLayout MessageCount How many distinct message names this script sends or receives. public int MessageCount { get; } Property Value int OwnedObjectCount How many owned objects this script declares, one per distinct name its Object.Create calls use. public int OwnedObjectCount { get; } Property Value int Examples Assert.That(program.OwnedObjectCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); ProcessMode The type default process mode SetProcessMode wrote, or Inherit. public Process ProcessMode { get; } Property Value Process ReadyBlockCount Number of blocks On.Ready registered. public int ReadyBlockCount { get; } Property Value int RoutineCount Number of routines this script declared. Every one of them is advanced once per frame per instance, and a routine whose activation has not started returns on its first line. public int RoutineCount { get; } Property Value int ScriptType The Script subclass this program was built from. public Type ScriptType { get; } Property Value Type SyncedTransformChannelCount How many transform channels this script synchronises: at most three, one each for position, rotation and scale. public int SyncedTransformChannelCount { get; } Property Value int SyncedVariableCount How many synchronised variables this script declared. public int SyncedVariableCount { get; } Property Value int TimedWorkCount Number of timed-work declarations this script built. Every one of them is advanced once per frame per instance, and a work whose activation has not started returns on its first line. public int TimedWorkCount { get; } Property Value int UtilityCount Number of utility selectors this script declared. Every one of them is advanced once per frame per instance, and a selector whose activation has not started returns on its first line. public int UtilityCount { get; } Property Value int WatchCount Number of When.Var(x).Changed watches registered. public int WatchCount { get; } Property Value int Methods AssetInputIndex(string) The slot one asset-input name addresses. public int AssetInputIndex(string name) Parameters Type Name Description string name The declared name. Returns int The slot index, or -1 when this script declares no input by that name. Examples var slot = program.AssetInputIndex(nameof(GateScript.OpenSound)); AssetInputNameAt(int) What one asset input is called. The name is what a host's stored value is matched against and what the Inspector derives its label from. public string AssetInputNameAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Its position in declaration order. Returns string The declared name. Examples var name = program.AssetInputNameAt(0); AssetInputTypeAt(int) Which Unity asset type one asset input accepts. The Inspector draws a field of this type, which is what stops an asset of another kind being assigned. public Type AssetInputTypeAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Its position in declaration order. Returns Type The declared type. Examples var type = program.AssetInputTypeAt(0); FindVariable<T>(string) Finds a variable this script declared, by the name it was declared with, and returns its handle. public Var<T> FindVariable<T>(string name) where T : struct Parameters Type Name Description string name The name the script declared, which nameof produced. Returns Var<T> The same handle Build() assigned to the script's own property. Type Parameters T Number, Flag or Text, matching how the variable was declared. Examples var health = program.FindVariable<Number>(nameof(PlayerScript.Health)); Remarks This is the tooling path, not the fix for reading a variable from the wrong object. It exists so that code holding a program and a name - a runtime inspector, a debugging window, a test - can reach a variable without holding a Script object at all. Ordinary code reads the variable from BuiltScript, which Script returns. docs/slice-decisions.md D4.42 records both and which is which. It is never read on the run-time path: a block holds the handle its build gave it. The search is a linear scan over the script's declarations, which number in the tens. The shadow slots a When.Var(x).Changed watch and a synchronised variable add are refused rather than returned. Their names are in angle brackets and no script wrote them, so returning one would hand out a slot the caller cannot have meant. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException No variable of that name was declared, the name belongs to a slot LunyScript added rather than the script, or the variable was declared with a different kind than T. InputActionKindAt(int) What one declared input action produces. public InputValueKind InputActionKindAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Which declaration, in declaration order. Returns InputValueKind The declared kind. Examples var kind = program.InputActionKindAt(0); InputActionNameAt(int) The name one declared input action carries. public string InputActionNameAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Which declaration, in declaration order. Returns string The action's name as the script declared it. Examples var name = program.InputActionNameAt(0); InputActionPlayerAt(int) Which local player one declared input action belongs to. public int InputActionPlayerAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Which declaration, in declaration order. Returns int The local player index. Examples var player = program.InputActionPlayerAt(0); MessageNameAt(int) The name of one message, for a diagnostic and for the runtime inspector. public string MessageNameAt(int messageId) Parameters Type Name Description int messageId Which message. Returns string The name the script wrote. OwnedObjectIndex(string) The slot one owned-object name addresses. public int OwnedObjectIndex(string name) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name an Object.Create used. Returns int The slot index, or -1 when this script names no owned object by that name. Examples var shield = instance.OwnedObject(program.OwnedObjectIndex("Shield")); OwnedObjectNameAt(int) What one owned-object slot is called. public string OwnedObjectNameAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index The slot. Returns string The name its Object.Create used. Examples var name = program.OwnedObjectNameAt(0); SyncedTransformChannelAt(int) One transform channel's declaration. public TransformSyncDeclaration SyncedTransformChannelAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Its position in SyncedTransformChannelCount. Returns TransformSyncDeclaration The declaration. SyncedVariableAt(int) One synchronised variable's declaration, by declaration order. public SyncDeclaration SyncedVariableAt(int index) Parameters Type Name Description int index Which one, from 0 to SyncedVariableCount minus one. Returns SyncDeclaration The declaration. ToString() One line naming the type and its counts, for a log or a failure message. public override string ToString() Returns string For example: "PlayerScript ready=2 frameUpdate=1 watches=1 doubles=2 booleans=1 ...". VariableNames() Names of every variable this script declared, including the shadow slots a watch adds. For diagnostics and the future runtime inspector; never read on the run-time path. public string[] VariableNames() Returns string[] A new array, so a caller cannot change the program. Examples var names = program.VariableNames();

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptRun.title: Class ScriptRunner | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptRun.summary: Class ScriptRunner Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Owns the built programs, the live instances and the instance pool, and runs each event kind across every instance. public sealed class ScriptRunner Expand Details ... Inheritance object ScriptRunner Examples var runner = new ScriptRunner(); var program = runner.GetOrBuildProgram(new CountdownScript()); var instance = runner.Spawn(program, new FakeHost(1)); runner.RaiseReady(instance); runner.TickFrameUpdate(); Remarks A runner names no Unity type at all. The one place it reports a block failure goes through LunyScriptLog, which is the only class in the product that calls UnityEngine.Debug. That is what lets every block be tested in Edit Mode against FakeHost, with no scene and no frame; AGENTS.md rule 53. Build() runs once per script type, and this cache is what makes that true. GetOrBuildProgram(ScriptBase) compiles a script type the first time it is asked for and returns the same program afterwards, so spawning a hundred objects of one script type compiles it once. Structural changes and reentrant dispatch are refused while a runner executes authored actions. The one removal the runtime loop does make is its own: it drops an instance whose host no longer exists and steps its index back for it. Constructors ScriptRunner(int, ScriptContexts) Creates a runner. public ScriptRunner(int expectedInstanceCapacity = 64, ScriptContexts context = ScriptContexts.Runtime) Parameters Type Name Description int expectedInstanceCapacity How many live instances to make room for up front. The list grows past it, at a spawn, which is a boundary where the allocation rule permits allocation; presizing keeps a measured spawn free of that growth. ScriptContexts context Examples var runner = new ScriptRunner(expectedInstanceCapacity: 128); Properties AssetGateway The one gateway this runner's Asset.Load and Asset.Release blocks talk to. Bound Inspector loads do not need a provider. Resources loads need UseProvider(IAssetLoadProvider). Available on runtime and editor runners. public AssetGateway AssetGateway { get; } Property Value AssetGateway Examples runner.AssetGateway.UseProvider(new FakeAssetLoadProvider()); AudioGateway The one audio gateway every instance this runner spawns writes through for one-shots, named bound sources, and mixer writes. Bound playback on the object a script runs on lives on the host instead. public AudioGateway AudioGateway { get; } Property Value AudioGateway Examples var audio = runner.AudioGateway; CameraGateway The one camera gateway every instance this runner spawns writes through. Whoever owns the runner names its backend with UseProvider(ICameraProvider); with none, every camera block writes nothing and says so once. public CameraGateway CameraGateway { get; } Property Value CameraGateway Examples runner.CameraGateway.UseProvider(new FakeCameraProvider()); CloudGateway The one gateway this runner's cloud blocks talk to. Whoever owns the runner names its provider with UseProvider(ICloudSaveProvider); requests made before that are queued, not thrown. TickFrameUpdate() polls it once per frame, before any instance runs, so a completion is observed in the same frame the watches that react to it run in. public CloudSaveGateway CloudGateway { get; } Property Value CloudSaveGateway Examples runner.CloudGateway.UseProvider(new FileCloudSaveProvider(directory)); Context The runner's execution context. Editor Play Mode game runners are Runtime. public ScriptContexts Context { get; } Property Value ScriptContexts Examples var runner = new ScriptRunner(context: ScriptContexts.Editor); Diagnostics Ordinary local observation and control, independent of authored execution. public RunnerDiagnostics Diagnostics { get; } Property Value RunnerDiagnostics Examples var snapshot = runner.Diagnostics.ReadCurrent(target); InputGateway The one input gateway every instance this runner spawns reads through. Whoever owns the runner names its backend with UseProvider(IInputProvider); a script that reads input before that reads the resting value of every action and says so once. public InputGateway InputGateway { get; } Property Value InputGateway Examples runner.InputGateway.UseProvider(new FakeInputProvider()); Remarks Resolution happens once per program, at the first spawn of that program, because a declaration names a local player and an action name and both are written in Build(). InstanceCount How many instances this runner is currently running. public int InstanceCount { get; } Property Value int IsPaused True while Time.Pause has set the runner flag. This is what Time.IsPaused reads. It is not whether the time scale is zero. public bool IsPaused { get; } Property Value bool NetworkGateway The one netcode gateway every instance this runner spawns talks to. Give it a provider before starting a session. public NetworkGateway NetworkGateway { get; } Property Value NetworkGateway Examples runner.NetworkGateway.UseProvider(new FakeNetworkProvider()); runner.NetworkGateway.StartHost(); Remarks The runner drains this gateway twice per tick: once before the instances run, to refresh authority and apply what arrived, and once after, to send what the cadences say to send. AGENTS.md rule 45 is why the refresh is first: a block that reads Net.HasAuthority reads the answer this tick opened with, and every block in the frame reads the same one. NetworkTicksElapsed How many network ticks this runner has taken, whatever the frame rate is. A tick is counted only on a frame where the session is connected AND at least one instance is bound to a networked object, so a runner that has never had a session reports zero. public int NetworkTicksElapsed { get; } Property Value int Remarks A tick is not one message. One tick produces one stream, sent in as many pieces as the backend's message budget needs, or in none at all when no channel had anything to send. Divide this into a byte total for a per-tick figure; it is not a message count. Read by AGENTS.md rule 47's bandwidth measurement, which divides the bytes a window sent by the ticks that window took. It is a counter rather than a figure derived from elapsed time because the two are not the same: the runner's tick accumulator is driven by its own time source, and a measurement that assumed a tick rate rather than counting ticks would report a per-tick figure for a number of ticks that never happened. That mistake was made and caught on 2026-09-06, by dividing this runner's bytes by a netcode backend's tick count. NetworkedInstanceCount How many instances this runner has bound to a networked object. public int NetworkedInstanceCount { get; } Property Value int ProgramCount How many script types this runner has built. public int ProgramCount { get; } Property Value int RandomSeed The session seed unseeded random streams are derived from. Tests supply one through UseRandomSeed(uint) so a failing run can be replayed. public uint RandomSeed { get; } Property Value uint TimeSource The clock a rate-capped SyncCadence counts its cooldown down against, and the one the Time surface's blocks read. public ITimeSource TimeSource { get; } Property Value ITimeSource Remarks Time.Scale, Time.IsPaused, Time.SetScale, Time.Pause and Time.Resume need this to be an IGameClock, which UnityTimeSource and TestKit.ManualTimeSource both are; Time.Delta and Time.Elapsed read any clock. UiGateway The one UI Toolkit gateway every instance this runner spawns writes through. Element lookup is spawn-time cache, not per-use Q. public UIGateway UiGateway { get; } Property Value UIGateway Methods BindNetworkObject(ScriptInstance, int) Binds one instance to a networked object, so that it takes part in the network tick: its authority is refreshed every frame, its synchronised variables are sent while it has authority, and messages and updates addressed to that object reach it. public void BindNetworkObject(ScriptInstance instance, int networkObjectId) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance, as Spawn(ScriptProgram, IScriptHost, bool) returned it. int networkObjectId The object's network id, which the netcode backend assigns and which is the same number on every peer. Examples runner.BindNetworkObject(instance, 7); Remarks Called by CodeSmile.LunyScript.Netcode when Netcode for GameObjects spawns the object, and by a test that pairs two runners by hand. The core knows nothing about how the id is produced; AGENTS.md rule 49. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The instance is null, the id is ScriptInstance.NoNetworkObject, or another live instance already holds that id. Despawn(ScriptInstance) Stops running an instance and keeps it for the next spawn of the same program. public void Despawn(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance to stop. Examples runner.Despawn(instance); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException instance is null. FindNetworkedInstance(int) The instance bound to one network object id, or null when no instance is. public ScriptInstance FindNetworkedInstance(int networkObjectId) Parameters Type Name Description int networkObjectId The id. Returns ScriptInstance The instance, or null. Examples var instance = runner.FindNetworkedInstance(7); GetOrBuildProgram(ScriptBase) Returns the program for this script type, building it the first time it is asked for. public ScriptProgram GetOrBuildProgram(ScriptBase prototype) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptBase prototype An instance of the script type. Build() reads nothing from it, because it is object-independent, but the first object of a script type is the object Build() runs on and the program keeps it as BuiltScript for as long as the program lives; docs/slice-decisions.md D4.42. A later object of the same type reaches nothing: the cached program is returned unchanged. Returns ScriptProgram The one program every object of that script type shares. Examples var program = runner.GetOrBuildProgram(new CountdownScript()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException prototype is null. HasProgram(Type) Whether this runner has already built a program for a script type, without building one. public bool HasProgram(Type scriptType) Parameters Type Name Description Type scriptType The script type to ask about. Returns bool True when GetOrBuildProgram(ScriptBase) would return a cached program. Examples var built = runner.HasProgram(typeof(CountdownScript)); PooledCount(ScriptProgram) How many pooled instances are waiting for a respawn of one program. public int PooledCount(ScriptProgram program) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptProgram program The program to ask about. Returns int The pool's size, or 0 when nothing of that program has been despawned. Examples var pooled = runner.PooledCount(program); RaiseApplication(ApplicationObservation) Delivers one of the five On.Application observations to every enabled instance. public void RaiseApplication(ApplicationObservation observation) Parameters Type Name Description ApplicationObservation observation What Unity reported. Examples runner.RaiseApplication(ApplicationObservation.Paused); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The runner is already dispatching, or it is an editor runner. RaiseCollisionEnter(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.CollisionEnter blocks. Unity raises OnCollisionEnter on the contact component; tests call this without a scene. public void RaiseCollisionEnter(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseCollisionEnter(instance); RaiseCollisionExit(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.CollisionExit blocks. public void RaiseCollisionExit(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseCollisionExit(instance); RaiseCollisionStay(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.CollisionStay blocks. public void RaiseCollisionStay(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseCollisionStay(instance); RaiseReady(ScriptInstance) Delivers Ready once. An action error disables that instance and is reported once. public void RaiseReady(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance Examples runner.RaiseReady(instance); RaiseTriggerEnter(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.TriggerEnter blocks. public void RaiseTriggerEnter(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseTriggerEnter(instance); RaiseTriggerExit(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.TriggerExit blocks. public void RaiseTriggerExit(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseTriggerExit(instance); RaiseTriggerStay(ScriptInstance) Runs this instance's On.TriggerStay blocks. public void RaiseTriggerStay(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance whose blocks run. Examples runner.RaiseTriggerStay(instance); SetEnabled(ScriptInstance, bool) Turns an instance's per-frame blocks on or off, following the host's own enabled state. Unity owns that state and LunyScript re-implements none of it; AGENTS.md rule 54. public void SetEnabled(ScriptInstance instance, bool enabled) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The instance. bool enabled Whether its per-frame blocks run. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SourceLoc.summary: Struct SourceLocation Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Where in a user's script a block was authored: the file and the line of the Build() call that created it. public readonly struct SourceLocation Expand Details ... Examples // Transform.MoveBy captures the caller's file and line, so this block knows it came from here. On.FrameUpdate(Transform.MoveBy(0.02, 0, 0)); Remarks This is captured at build time and never at failure time, because at failure time the user's line is not on the call stack at all. A block is composed inside Build(), which runs once per script type at launch, and is executed later by ScriptRunner; by the moment it logs or throws, the only frames on the stack are LunyScript's own. [CallerFilePath] and [CallerLineNumber] on the block factory methods are what put the authored line into the block, and this struct is what the block holds. Construction allocates nothing. [CallerFilePath] hands the compiler's own path literal, which lives in the assembly's string table, so this struct stores that reference and an int and does no string work. The project-relative form a user reads is produced by ProjectRelativePath(), which allocates and is called only when a diagnostic is actually produced. That split is what lets every block carry a location without touching the allocation rule; AGENTS.md rule 29. A block built by a C# operator carries Unknown: an operator cannot declare the optional parameters the caller attributes need. health + 1.0 therefore has no location of its own, and the block that consumes it does. Fields Unknown A location that names nothing, which is what a block built by a C# operator carries. public static readonly SourceLocation Unknown Field Value SourceLocation UnknownDescription What Describe() returns for a location that names nothing. public const string UnknownDescription = "an unknown location" Field Value string Properties CompilerPath The path exactly as the compiler recorded it, absolute and unnormalised. public string CompilerPath { get; } Property Value string IsKnown Whether this location names a file and a line. public bool IsKnown { get; } Property Value bool Line The one-based line number of the call that built the block, or 0 when unknown. public int Line { get; } Property Value int Methods Describe() The location as one readable token, for a message a user reads. public string Describe() Returns string Assets/.../SliceScript.cs:45, or a phrase saying the location is unknown. Examples message += $" authored at {location.Describe()}"; Equals(SourceLocation) Indicates whether the current object is equal to another object of the same type. public bool Equals(SourceLocation other) Parameters Type Name Description SourceLocation other An object to compare with this object. Returns bool true if the current object is equal to the other parameter; otherwise, false. Equals(object) Indicates whether this instance and a specified object are equal. public override bool Equals(object obj) Parameters Type Name Description object obj The object to compare with the current instance. Returns bool true if obj and this instance are the same type and represent the same value; otherwise, false. FromCaller(string, int) Builds a location from the caller attributes a factory method declares. Allocates nothing. public static SourceLocation FromCaller(string callerFilePath, int callerLineNumber) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler through [CallerFilePath]. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler through [CallerLineNumber]. Returns SourceLocation The location, or Unknown when the compiler supplied neither. Examples public Block MoveBy(NumberValueBlock x, NumberValueBlock y, NumberValueBlock z, [CallerFilePath] String callerFilePath = null, [CallerLineNumber] Int32 callerLineNumber = 0) => new MoveByBlock(x, y, z, SourceLocation.FromCaller(callerFilePath, callerLineNumber)); GetHashCode() Returns the hash code for this instance. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int A 32-bit signed integer that is the hash code for this instance. ProjectRelativePath() The path with forward slashes and everything above the project's Assets folder removed, which is the form Unity's console resolves to an asset. public string ProjectRelativePath() Returns string The project-relative path, or an empty string when this location is unknown. Examples var path = location.ProjectRelativePath(); // "Assets/CodeSmile/.../SliceScript.cs" Remarks This allocates and is not for the run-time path. It runs when a diagnostic is produced, which is a failure path or a log call, never per frame; AGENTS.md rule 29. A path with no Assets segment is returned with its separators normalised and nothing removed, because a package or a test fixture can legitimately live elsewhere. ToString() Returns the fully qualified type name of this instance. public override string ToString() Returns string The fully qualified type name. ToUnityStackFrame(string) The location written as one Unity stack frame, which is the form Unity's console prints a frame in. public string ToUnityStackFrame(string frameLabel) Parameters Type Name Description string frameLabel What to name the frame, in Unity's Type:Method() shape. Returns string The frame line, or an empty string when this location is unknown. Examples var frame = location.ToUnityStackFrame("CountdownScript:Build()"); Remarks The format is Unity's own, produced by UnityEngine.StackTraceUtility.ExtractFormattedStackTrace: Namespace.Type:Method() (at path:line). Writing the authored location in that format is what lets LunyScriptException present it as the topmost frame, so that the Console prints the user's own line first. It does not move the row's double-click target, which Unity takes from the live call stack at log time; docs/console-navigation.md.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SpawnBuil.summary: Struct SpawnBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Object.Spawn(prefab) returns: a spawn with no placement yet. Add At(Vec3ValueBlock), ChildOf(string, string, int) and Into(string, string, int) in any order, or use it as a block, which spawns the prefab at its own pose. public readonly struct SpawnBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Sentry)); On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Sentry).At(new Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)).ChildOf().Into("Guard")); Remarks The three builder structs are a typestate: this one offers At and no frame modifier, SpawnPlacedBuilder offers the two frame modifiers and no second At, and SpawnFramedBuilder offers neither. So Object.Spawn(p).InWorldSpace() and Object.Spawn(p).At(a).At(b) and Object.Spawn(p).At(a).InWorldSpace().InLocalSpace() are all compile errors rather than run-time checks; AGENTS.md rule 41 and the settled semantics-t08 answer, which asks for conflicting space clauses to be unavailable in typestate. The implicit conversion is what AGENTS.md rule 42 asks for: every builder either converts to a block or registers its finish action before Build() returns, so an unfinished chain cannot silently drop its behaviour. Methods At(Vec3ValueBlock) Names where the produced object goes, leaving its rotation as the prefab's. public SpawnPlacedBuilder At(Vec3ValueBlock position) Parameters Type Name Description Vec3ValueBlock position Where the produced object goes. Returns SpawnPlacedBuilder A builder that can still take a frame, a parent and a name. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Sentry).At(new Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0))); Remarks The expression is evaluated where this block runs, not where the runner applies the spawn, so a position read from a variable is that variable's value at the authored line. The coordinates are the parent's until InWorldSpace() says otherwise; with no parent the two are the same coordinates. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException position is null, or this builder is a default that no Object.Spawn(prefab) call produced. At(Vec3ValueBlock, RotationValueBlock) Names where the produced object goes and how it is turned. public SpawnPlacedBuilder At(Vec3ValueBlock position, RotationValueBlock rotation) Parameters Type Name Description Vec3ValueBlock position Where the produced object goes. RotationValueBlock rotation How the produced object is turned. Returns SpawnPlacedBuilder A builder that can still take a frame, a parent and a name. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Sentry).At(Vec3.Zero, Rotation.Euler(0.0, 90.0, 0.0))); Remarks Both expressions are evaluated where this block runs. The coordinates and the rotation are the parent's until InWorldSpace() says otherwise. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Either expression is null, or this builder is a default that no Object.Spawn(prefab) call produced. ChildOf(string, string, int) Parents the produced object to the object this script runs on, or to one this script owns. public SpawnBuilder ChildOf(string name = null, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name that addresses the parent, or null for the object this script runs on. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnBuilder A builder that can still take a placement and a name. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Sentry).ChildOf()); Remarks Omitting the name parents it to the object the script runs on, which is the same "self by omission" the rest of the Object surface uses. A named parent is an object this script produced, by Object.Create(name) or by another spawn's Into(string, string, int). A parent whose slot is empty when the spawn is applied leaves the produced object at the scene root and reports it. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException name is whitespace, this chain already names a parent, or this builder is a default. Into(string, string, int) Holds the produced object in this script's owned-object slot of that name, so later blocks can address it. public SpawnBuilder Into(string name, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name this script addresses the produced object by. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns SpawnBuilder A builder that can still take a placement and a parent. Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Sentry).Into("Guard")); Remarks A held object is owned: it is destroyed when the instance that spawned it is despawned, by every path that despawns one, exactly as an Object.Create object is. A spawn with no Into is not held at all and outlives the script that spawned it. The name addresses the slot and is not the produced object's name in the scene: a prefab already carries a name, which is the difference from Object.Create(name) where the name is both. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SpawnObje.title: Class SpawnObjectBlock | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SpawnObje.summary: Class SpawnObjectBlock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Object.Spawn(prefab) and its chain build: produces an object from a declared prefab input, places it, parents it, and holds it in an owned-object slot when the chain named one. public sealed class SpawnObjectBlock : Block, IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object Block SpawnObjectBlock Implements IScriptNode Inherited Members Block.Contexts Block.Location Block.ExecuteAll(Block[], ScriptInstance) Block.AdvanceContained(ActionBlock, ScriptInstance) Block.None Examples On.Ready(Object.Spawn(Sentry).At(new Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)).ChildOf().Into("Guard")); Remarks The block records the spawn; the runner applies it after the current dispatch. A prefab can carry a LunyScriptBehaviour, and producing such an object runs its Awake inside the call, which re-enters ScriptRunner.Spawn. The runner refuses to be re-entered during dispatch, so an authored spawn takes effect between event invocations, which is also what the settled contract-dispatch-order answer asks for. Object.Create(name) is immediate instead, because a created object carries no script and can re-enter nothing. The placement expressions are evaluated here, not when the spawn is applied. A position read from a variable is that variable's value at the line the author wrote. This block itself allocates nothing. It writes one struct into the runner's request list; the object, and everything the prefab carries, is allocated when the runner applies the request, which is AGENTS.md rule 31's first boundary. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncCaden.summary: Struct SyncCadence Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll How often one synchronised variable is sent. Declared per variable, because AGENTS.md rule 46 says synchronised state is declared one variable at a time and there is no networked struct and no state object to put two variables into. public readonly struct SyncCadence Expand Details ... Examples Health = Var.DefineSynced<Number>(nameof(Health), SyncCadence.OnChangeCapped(10.0), 100.0); Remarks The cadence is a required parameter, not a default. There is no way to declare a synchronised variable without naming what it costs, which is the compile-time half of rule 46: a never-changing player name and a per-tick value cannot share a payload, because there is nowhere to put them together. A rate cap caps sends, not writes. The authority's own value is always current; a peer sees at most MaxPerSecond updates and therefore may hold a stale value between them. That is latency as a state, per rule 45, and it is reported rather than hidden. Fields EveryTick Sent every network tick, changed or not. The cadence to reach for, and still written out, because a cadence chosen by omission is a cadence nobody reviewed. public static readonly SyncCadence OnChange Field Value SyncCadence Once Sent once, the first time the value is known, and never again. For a name, a team or a colour chosen when a player joins. public static readonly SyncCadence Once Field Value SyncCadence Properties IsRateCapped Whether this cadence caps its send rate. public bool IsRateCapped { get; } Property Value bool Methods OnChangeCapped(double) Sent when the value changed, and no more often than the cap allows. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncFacto.title: Struct SyncFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.SyncFacto.summary:
Struct SyncFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Sync surface: which parts of an object's transform cross the network, and how often each one is sent. public readonly struct SyncFactory Expand Details ... Examples protected override void Build() { Sync.Position(SyncCadence.EveryTick); Sync.Rotation(SyncCadence.OnChange); Sync.Scale(SyncCadence.Once); } Remarks One call per channel, each with its own cadence, which is AGENTS.md rule 46 applied to the transform. There is no "synchronise the transform" switch, for the reason rule 46 gives for there being no networked struct: a scale that never changes would otherwise share a payload with a position that changes every tick, and the cost of the second would be paid for the first. What the channels carry crosses as one stream per authority per network tick, not as one message per object; rule 47, and docs/netcode-bandwidth.md is the measurement that rule requires. Methods Position(SyncCadence) Synchronises the object's world position. public void Position(SyncCadence cadence) Parameters Type Name Description SyncCadence cadence How often it is sent. Required, so that a position whose cost nobody chose cannot be synchronised. Examples Sync.Position(SyncCadence.EveryTick); Remarks The position is sent as the change since the last one sent, in 6 bytes, and as an absolute position in 12 whenever the change is too large to encode or a peer has just joined. Only the authority may move an object whose position is synchronised; a move on any other peer is refused, and the diagnostic names what to write instead. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cadence is unset, or this script already declared this channel. Rotation(SyncCadence) Synchronises the object's world rotation. public void Rotation(SyncCadence cadence) Parameters Type Name Description SyncCadence cadence How often it is sent. Examples Sync.Rotation(SyncCadence.OnChange); Remarks Sent as a quaternion compressed into 4 bytes: the two-bit index of its largest component and the other three at ten bits each. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cadence is unset, or this script already declared this channel. Scale(SyncCadence) Synchronises the object's local scale. public void Scale(SyncCadence cadence) Parameters Type Name Description SyncCadence cadence How often it is sent. Examples Sync.Scale(SyncCadence.Once); Remarks Sent as three half-precision values, 6 bytes. A scale that is chosen once and never changed is declared with SyncCadence.Once and then costs nothing per tick.

Each axis must be between -65504 and 65504, which is what the 16-bit encoding holds. This channel sends the value rather than a change, so unlike a position it has no second form to fall back to: an object scaled outside that range has its scale sent to nobody, every peer keeps the last scale that was inside the range, and the runner writes one warning naming the object, its scale and the bound. That warning is written once for an object and not again: a scale that leaves the range later is refused the same way and in silence, because composing the message on a path that repeats would allocate.

Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cadence is unset, or this script already declared this channel.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Text.html.summary: Struct Text Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A text literal written in a script, and the type argument that makes a text variable Var<Text>. public readonly struct Text Expand Details ... Examples var playerName = Var.DefineText("playerName"); On.Ready(playerName.Set("Player One")); // the String becomes a Text here Remarks A Text is a build-time value only. It carries a managed System.String, which is what a literal in C# source is, and it is converted into the block's fixed-capacity storage while the script type is built. No slot ever holds one and no block ever creates one, so the managed string never reaches the run-time path. The run-time storage is a Unity.Collections.FixedString chosen by the variable's declared TextCapacity. The implicit conversion from String is deliberate and does not contradict AGENTS.md rule 40, which forbids an implicit conversion from String to a variable block so that Debug.Log("msg" + variable) cannot silently become one. This conversion produces a literal value, not a block. Constructors Text(string) Creates a literal from a string. public Text(string value) Parameters Type Name Description string value The characters. Null is treated as the empty string. Fields MaxLiteralBytes Largest text literal a script can write, in UTF-8 bytes. A literal is stored in a FixedString512Bytes inside the block, whatever capacity the target variable declares. public const int MaxLiteralBytes = 509 Field Value int Properties ByteLength Number of UTF-8 bytes this literal needs, which is what MaxLiteralBytes and a variable's TextCapacity are measured in. public int ByteLength { get; } Property Value int Value The literal's characters. Never null; an uninitialised Text reads as the empty string. public string Value { get; } Property Value string Methods Equals(Text) Two literals are equal when their characters are equal. public bool Equals(Text other) Parameters Type Name Description Text other The literal to compare against. Returns bool True when both carry the same characters. Equals(object) Indicates whether this instance and a specified object are equal. public override bool Equals(object obj) Parameters Type Name Description object obj The object to compare with the current instance. Returns bool true if obj and this instance are the same type and represent the same value; otherwise, false. Format(string, params TextArgument[]) Builds a text value out of a format and the values that fill its holes, for a text variable's Set. public static TextFormat Format(string format, params TextArgument[] arguments) Parameters Type Name Description string format The text to write, with {0} where the first value goes, {1} the second, and so on. A number hole may ask for a fixed number of decimal places, written {0:2}. A literal brace is written {{ or }}. TextArgument[] arguments One value per hole: a number, a flag or a text variable. Literals of those kinds convert on their own. Returns TextFormat The parsed format, which a text variable's Set takes. Examples On.FrameUpdate(Label.Set(Text.Format("{0:1}/{1} hp", Health, MaxHealth))); Remarks What a number hole prints. With no decimal count, up to six decimal places with trailing zeros removed, so a whole number prints with no decimal point at all. With a count, exactly that many places, rounding a midpoint to the nearer even digit the way Math.Round does. NaN prints as NaN and an infinity as Infinity or -Infinity. A magnitude at or above 9,000,000,000,000,000,000 is printed through Unity's own single-precision formatter, which is the one case where the printed digits are not the Double's. What a flag hole prints is true or false. A text hole copies the variable's bytes in. The format is parsed once per script type, inside Build(). Writing the result per frame appends into a buffer the size of the destination variable and allocates nothing; text that does not fit the destination is refused the same way Set refuses a literal that is too long. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The format is null or malformed, an argument is null or carries no value, or a hole names an argument that was not passed. GetHashCode() Returns the hash code for this instance. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int A 32-bit signed integer that is the hash code for this instance. ToFixedString() Converts the literal into the fixed-capacity form a block stores. public FixedString512Bytes ToFixedString() Returns FixedString512Bytes The literal as a FixedString512Bytes. Examples var stored = new Text("hello").ToFixedString(); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The literal needs more than MaxLiteralBytes UTF-8 bytes. ToString() The literal's characters. public override string ToString() Returns string Value. Operators implicit operator Text(string) Turns a C# string literal into a LunyScript text literal. public static implicit operator Text(string value) Parameters Type Name Description string value The characters. Returns Text The literal. Examples Text greeting = "hello";

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TextCapac.title: Enum TextCapacity | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TextCapac.summary: Enum TextCapacity Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll How many bytes a text variable can hold. Declared per variable at build time, because the five capacities are five distinct Unity.Collections.FixedString types and a text variable is stored in exactly one of them. public enum TextCapacity Expand Details ... Fields Bytes128 = 128 A FixedString128Bytes slot: 128 bytes of storage, 125 usable. Bytes32 = 32 A FixedString32Bytes slot: 32 bytes of storage, 29 usable. Bytes4096 = 4096 A FixedString4096Bytes slot: 4096 bytes of storage, 4093 usable. Bytes512 = 512 A FixedString512Bytes slot: 512 bytes of storage, 509 usable. Bytes64 = 64 A FixedString64Bytes slot: 64 bytes of storage, 61 usable. Examples var playerName = Var.DefineText("playerName", TextCapacity.Bytes64); Remarks AGENTS.md rule 15: Var.DefineText defaults to Bytes64, because 64 bytes is a common cache-line size, and that default is what a caller gets when the content has no known size. Choosing a different capacity deliberately is still the right thing when the content is known to be shorter or longer than the 61 usable bytes of Bytes64; what the enum exists to prevent is one size being imposed on every text variable with no way to change it. Above Bytes4096 there is no fixed string, and that case needs a fallback that is allowed to allocate and allowed to be non-networked. Define.Text(name).Allocating(maxBytes) is that fallback. The usable payload of each size is three bytes less than the name says: two bytes hold the length and one holds a terminating zero. UsableBytes(TextCapacity) returns the usable figure rather than the name's figure.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TextLengt.title: Enum TextLength | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TextLengt.summary: Enum TextLength Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Named byte bounds for each Text entry in a list or map. Declared per collection side at build time, because the five sizes are five distinct Unity.Collections.FixedString types and every entry on that side uses exactly one of them. public enum TextLength Expand Details ... Fields L = 512 512 storage bytes, 509 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 509 one-byte characters or 127 four-byte characters. M = 128 128 storage bytes, 125 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 125 one-byte characters or 31 four-byte characters. S = 64 64 storage bytes, 61 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 61 one-byte characters or 15 four-byte characters. XL = 4096 4096 storage bytes, 4093 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 4093 one-byte characters or 1023 four-byte characters. XS = 32 32 storage bytes, 29 usable UTF-8 bytes. Fits 29 one-byte characters or 7 four-byte characters. This is the default for a collection Text side that omits KeyLength or ValueLength. Examples Scores = Define.Map<Text, Number>(nameof(Scores), 8).KeyLength(TextLength.S); Labels = Define.List<Text>(nameof(Labels), 4).ValueLength(TextLength.M); Remarks The default is XS, the smallest step. Each step documents both its storage byte count and how many UTF-8 characters fit: one-byte characters fill the usable payload, four-byte characters fill a quarter of it. Usable payload is three bytes less than storage: two bytes hold the length and one holds a terminating zero. Collection text uses these named steps through KeyLength and ValueLength. Variable text still uses TextCapacity.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TimeFacto.title: Struct TimeFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TimeFacto.summary: Struct TimeFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Time surface a script reads the game clock through, and the one place a script changes how fast that clock runs: Delta, Elapsed, Scale, IsPaused, SetScale(NumberValueBlock, string, int), Pause(string, int) and Resume(string, int). public readonly struct TimeFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.FrameUpdate(Age.Add(Time.Delta)); On.FrameUpdate(If(Health <= 0.0).Then(Time.Pause())); Remarks The scaled clock is the default and real time carries the word. Time.Delta is game time, so a game running in slow motion sees a smaller number and a paused game sees zero; Time.Delta.Unscaled() is real time, which neither the scale nor a pause changes. The modifier follows the verb and only the unusual case is written out, which is the same grammar a transform verb's frame uses. It applies to both readings and to nothing else here: a scale has no clock to choose, so Time.Scale and Time.IsPaused return types that carry no Unscaled and Time.Scale.Unscaled() does not compile. Pausing sets the runner flag and zeros the time scale. Time.IsPaused reads the flag. Pausable scripts skip process events while it is set; WhenPaused and Always scripts keep ticking. On.FixedUpdate still does not run at scale zero, because Unity's fixed step is driven by game time. A pause menu declares SetProcessMode(Process.WhenPaused) and reads Time.Delta.Unscaled(). docs/execution-model.md, "Pause and the game clock", is the whole contract. The scale is the game's, not this object's. One script pausing pauses everything, because that is what a time scale is. Nothing here is per object, and nothing here is synchronised: a peer that pauses its own game pauses only its own, and the network keeps ticking while it is paused, because the other peers are still playing. This is the running game's clock. Every member is runtime-only, so a script built for an explicitly owned editor runner cannot use them; that runner's clock governs no game and has no scale to read or stop. EditorTime.Elapsed() is the editor session's own reading, and docs/editor-foundation.md owns that boundary. Properties Delta How many seconds the previous frame took, in game time. public TimeReadBlock Delta { get; } Property Value TimeReadBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Age.Add(Time.Delta)); Remarks Scaled, so it is smaller in slow motion and zero while paused. Write Time.Delta.Unscaled() for the real-time frame length, which a pause does not change. This is the number a per-second rate is written with: Health.Add(-Drain * Time.Delta) loses Drain health per second whatever the frame rate is. Elapsed How many seconds of game time have passed since the run started. public TimeReadBlock Elapsed { get; } Property Value TimeReadBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Time.Elapsed > 60.0).Then(Overtime.Set(true))); Remarks Scaled, so it stops advancing while the game is paused and advances at half speed at a scale of one half. Write Time.Elapsed.Unscaled() for real time, which keeps advancing while paused. IsPaused True while the runner paused flag is set, which is what Time.Pause writes. public ConditionBlock IsPaused { get; } Property Value ConditionBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(!Time.IsPaused).Then(Score.Add(1.0))); Remarks This is a condition, so it goes into If(...) and is negated with !. It reads the runner flag rather than testing whether the time scale is zero: Time.SetScale(0) stops the clock and does not set the flag. Scale How fast game time runs against real time: one at ordinary speed, one half in slow motion, zero while paused. public NumberValueBlock Scale { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Time.Scale < 1.0).Then(ShowSlowMotionBadge.Set(true))); Methods Pause(string, int) Builds a block that stops game time, remembering the scale to come back to. public Block Pause(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(MenuOpen.IsTrue()).Then(Time.Pause())); Remarks Pausing an already paused game changes nothing. Pausable scripts skip process events while the flag is set; see this surface's own remarks and docs/execution-model.md. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This factory was not obtained inside Build(). Resume(string, int) Builds a block that restarts game time at the last positive scale it was set to. public Block Resume(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(!MenuOpen.IsTrue()).Then(Time.Resume())); Remarks Resuming a game that is not paused changes nothing, so a resume written on every frame does not cancel a slow-motion scale another script set. The scale it comes back to is one when nothing set another. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This factory was not obtained inside Build(). SetScale(NumberValueBlock, string, int) Builds a block that sets the game's time scale. public Block SetScale(NumberValueBlock scale, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock scale The new scale: zero stops game time, one is ordinary speed, and a value above one runs the game faster than real time. A positive value is also what Resume(string, int) comes back to afterwards. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one: it is what records the line of the script this block was written on. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Bullets == 1.0).Then(Time.SetScale(0.25))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException scale is null, or this factory was not obtained inside Build(). A scale that is negative, NaN or infinite is refused when the block runs, because an expression's value is not known until then.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TimeReadB.title: Class TimeReadBlock | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.TimeReadB.summary: Class TimeReadBlock Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What Time.Delta and Time.Elapsed return: a number expression reading one of the runner's two clocks, and the one place the clock choice is written. public sealed class TimeReadBlock : NumberValueBlock, IScriptNode Expand Details ... Inheritance object NumberValueBlock TimeReadBlock Implements IScriptNode Inherited Members NumberValueBlock.DescribeChildren(NodeDescription) NumberValueBlock.Equals(object) NumberValueBlock.GetHashCode() Examples On.FrameUpdate(Age.Add(Time.Delta)); On.FrameUpdate(RealAge.Add(Time.Delta.Unscaled())); Remarks This block type is public because Unscaled() is part of the authored grammar, not because a test needs it: a script writes Time.Delta.Unscaled(), so the type Time.Delta returns has to carry that method. Its constructor is internal like every other block's, so a script still cannot build one directly. The scaled clock is the default and real time carries the word. That is the same grammar a transform verb's frame uses - the modifier follows the verb, the common case is the default, and the unusual case is the one that is written out. It is applied to both readings and to nothing else on the Time surface: Time.Scale and Time.IsPaused are not clock readings and return types that carry no Unscaled at all, so Time.Scale.Unscaled() does not compile rather than meaning nothing. Evaluating one reads two properties - the runner's clock and one of its four values - and allocates nothing. Both clock choices cost the same; there is no cast and no branch on anything but the two readonly fields. Properties Contexts Legacy custom nodes are runtime-only until explicitly declared shared or Editor-only. public override ScriptContexts Contexts { get; } Property Value ScriptContexts Examples public override ScriptContexts Contexts => ScriptContexts.Shared; RequiredServices Services this node requires in addition to its children's requirements. public override ScriptServices RequiredServices { get; } Property Value ScriptServices Examples public override ScriptServices RequiredServices => ScriptServices.Clock; Methods Evaluate(ScriptInstance) Produces the value for one object. Must allocate nothing after warm-up; AGENTS.md rule 29. public override double Evaluate(ScriptInstance instance) Parameters Type Name Description ScriptInstance instance The object's state and host. Returns double The value this expression has for that object right now. Unscaled() The same reading taken from the real-time clock, which the game's time scale and a pause do not change. public NumberValueBlock Unscaled() Returns NumberValueBlock A number expression reading real time. Calling it on a read that is already unscaled returns an equivalent block rather than refusing, because the sentence Time.Delta.Unscaled() means the same thing however many times it is written. Examples On.FrameUpdate(MenuFade.Add(Time.Delta.Unscaled()));
