reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.title: Struct TransformFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Struct TransformFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Transform surface inside Build(): where the object a script runs on is, how it is turned and scaled, what is above and below it in the hierarchy, and what it is parented to. public readonly struct TransformFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.FrameUpdate(Transform.MoveBy(Step, 0.0, 0.0), Transform.RotateBy(0.0, 1.5, 0.0)); On.Ready(Transform.SetScale(2.0)); On.Ready(If(Transform.HasParent).Then(Transform.Unparent())); Remarks The blocks reach the object through IScriptHost, never through a UnityEngine.Transform; AGENTS.md rule 24. Every parameter is a NumberValueBlock, so a literal, a variable and an expression all work, through the implicit conversions that type declares. A displacement is in the object's own frame and an absolute value names its frame in the verb. MoveBy(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) and RotateBy(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) act along the object's own oriented axes unless the builder they return is given InWorldSpace(); SetWorldPosition(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) and SetLocalPosition(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) say which frame they mean in their names. That is the captain's answer to API-semantics row T02 on 2026-09-13, and TransformSpace states why one word covers two frames. Parent, Child(NumberValueBlock, string, int) and Root aim the same verbs at one step of the hierarchy around the object. They offer no further navigation of their own; TransformTargetFactory says why. Properties ChildCount How many children this object has. public NumberValueBlock ChildCount { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.Ready(If(Transform.ChildCount > 0.0).Then(Carrying.Set(true))); Remarks Direct children only, which is what Unity's own child count is. LocalPositionX The x of this object's position in its parent's frame. public NumberValueBlock LocalPositionX { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Offset.Set(Transform.LocalPositionX)); Remarks The same as WorldPositionX for an object at the scene root. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). LocalPositionY The y of this object's position in its parent's frame. public NumberValueBlock LocalPositionY { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Offset.Set(Transform.LocalPositionY)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). LocalPositionZ The z of this object's position in its parent's frame. public NumberValueBlock LocalPositionZ { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Offset.Set(Transform.LocalPositionZ)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). LocalRotationX The x of this object's rotation in its parent's frame, in euler degrees. public NumberValueBlock LocalRotationX { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Pitch.Set(Transform.LocalRotationX)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). LocalRotationY The y of this object's rotation in its parent's frame, in euler degrees. public NumberValueBlock LocalRotationY { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Heading.Set(Transform.LocalRotationY)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). LocalRotationZ The z of this object's rotation in its parent's frame, in euler degrees. public NumberValueBlock LocalRotationZ { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Roll.Set(Transform.LocalRotationZ)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Parent The object this one is parented to. public TransformTargetFactory Parent { get; } Property Value TransformTargetFactory Examples On.Ready(If(Transform.HasParent).Then(Siblings.Set(Transform.Parent.ChildCount))); Remarks Every verb reached through this refuses to run on an object that has no parent, and says so naming the object; guard with HasParent. ScaleX The x of this object's own scale. public NumberValueBlock ScaleX { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Width.Set(Transform.ScaleX)); Remarks The scale as it is stored on the object, which is the only scale Unity lets anything write. WorldScaleX is the derived one and is read-only. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). ScaleZ The z of this object's own scale. public NumberValueBlock ScaleZ { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Depth.Set(Transform.ScaleZ)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). WorldPositionX The x of this object's position in the scene's frame. public NumberValueBlock WorldPositionX { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Drift.Set(Transform.WorldPositionX)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). WorldPositionY The y of this object's position in the scene's frame. public NumberValueBlock WorldPositionY { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Transform.WorldPositionY < 0.0).Then(Fell.Set(true))); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). WorldPositionZ The z of this object's position in the scene's frame. public NumberValueBlock WorldPositionZ { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Depth.Set(Transform.WorldPositionZ)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException Read outside Build(). Methods Child(NumberValueBlock, string, int) One of this object's children, by index. public TransformTargetFactory Child(NumberValueBlock index, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description NumberValueBlock index Which child, counting from zero. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Struct TransformOffsetBuilder Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll What MoveBy and RotateBy return: the displacement, in the object's own frame unless a modifier says otherwise. public readonly struct TransformOffsetBuilder Expand Details ... Examples On.FrameUpdate(Transform.MoveBy(0.02, 0.0, 0.0)); // along the object's axes On.FrameUpdate(Transform.MoveBy(0.02, 0.0, 0.0).InWorldSpace()); // along the scene's axes Remarks The default is the object's own oriented axes, which is the captain's answer to API-semantics row T02 on 2026-09-13 and what the previous version of LunyScript did; docs/verification/transform-space-spelling.md is the reading of it. A move of one unit along X goes one world unit along the direction the object faces, unaffected by its own or its parent's scale, and a turn composes after the rotation the object already has. InWorldSpace() selects the scene's axes and InLocalSpace() states the default. Each returns a type that offers neither, so a second space clause does not compile; that is the typestate API-semantics row T08 asks for and AGENTS.md rule 41 requires. The conversion to a block is what AGENTS.md rule 42 asks for: a builder either converts or registers, so an unmodified MoveBy cannot silently drop its behaviour. Methods InLocalSpace() Applies the amounts along the object's own oriented axes, which is what they do without this clause. public SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder InLocalSpace() Returns SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder The finished displacement, which takes no second space clause. Examples On.FrameUpdate(Transform.MoveBy(1.0, 0.0, 0.0).InLocalSpace()); Remarks Present so a script can say the frame it means at a call site where leaving it out would read as an oversight. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default that no verb produced. InWorldSpace() Applies the amounts along the scene's axes instead of the object's own. public SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder InWorldSpace() Returns SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder The finished displacement, which takes no second space clause. Examples On.FrameUpdate(Transform.MoveBy(1.0, 0.0, 0.0).InWorldSpace()); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This builder is a default that no verb produced. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Enum TransformPart Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which of the three values of a transform a verb reads or writes. public enum TransformPart Expand Details ... Fields Position = 0 The position. Rotation = 1 The rotation, in euler degrees. Scale = 2 The scale. World reads Unity's lossy scale and cannot be written; see IScriptHost.WriteTransform. Examples host.ReadTransform(TransformRelation.Parent, 0, TransformSpace.World, TransformPart.Scale, out var x, out var y, out var z); Remarks Rotation is carried as euler degrees here, because that is what a script author writes and reads. The quaternion form the transform stream needs is the separate IScriptHost.ReadRotation and WriteRotation pair, which exists because converting a rotation to angles and back is not the same rotation once the second angle passes 90 degrees.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.title: Enum TransformRelation | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Enum TransformRelation Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which object a transform verb acts on, named relative to the object the script runs on. public enum TransformRelation Expand Details ... Fields Child = 3 One of that object's children, by index. Refused when the index is outside the child count. None = 0 No object. As a reparent destination this is the scene root, which is what Transform.Unparent() asks for; as a verb's target it resolves to nothing and is refused. Parent = 2 That object's parent. Refused when it has none. Root = 4 The topmost object of that object's hierarchy, which is the object itself when it has no parent. Self = 1 The object the script runs on. Examples host.ReadChildCount(TransformRelation.Self, 0); Remarks The hierarchy vocabulary is one step deep by design: Parent, Child and Root are reached from the object the script runs on and offer no further navigation of their own, so a chain cannot walk an arbitrary path. That is the "bounded hierarchy queries" of docs/positioning.md item C14 applied to this family. A named or bound object of any kind is not a relation and is not part of this version; it arrives with C14 itself.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.title: Enum TransformSpace | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Enum TransformSpace Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Which frame a transform verb's numbers are in. public enum TransformSpace Expand Details ... Fields Local = 1 The object's own oriented axes for a displacement, and the parent's frame for an absolute value. The default for MoveBy and RotateBy. World = 0 The scene's frame. Examples host.ReadTransform(TransformRelation.Self, 0, TransformSpace.Local, TransformPart.Position, out var x, out var y, out var z); Remarks Local names two different frames, and which one it is depends on the verb. That is deliberate and it is the captain's answer to API-semantics row T02 on 2026-09-13, which is also what the previous version of LunyScript did; docs/verification/transform-space-spelling.md is the reading of it. For a displacement - MoveBy and RotateBy - Local is the object's own oriented axes, which is Unity's Space.Self. A move of one unit along X goes one world unit along the direction the object faces, unaffected by its own or its parent's scale; a turn composes after the rotation the object already has. For an absolute value - a read or a set of a position, a rotation or a scale - Local is the parent's frame, which is Unity's localPosition, localEulerAngles and localScale. World is the scene's frame for both, and for a turn it composes before the rotation the object already has. An object at the scene root with no rotation of its own cannot tell the two apart, which is why a test that separates them gives the object both; AGENTS.md rule 56 names that as the plausible-looking wrong result.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.title: Class TransformStreamInbox | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Class TransformStreamInbox Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll Holds the transform streams that arrived since the last tick drained them, in one buffer the inbox owns. Every INetworkProvider uses one, so that the receive side of the stream is written once rather than once per backend. public sealed class TransformStreamInbox Expand Details ... Inheritance object TransformStreamInbox Remarks Why this exists rather than a queue of byte arrays. A stream arrives on every tick of every peer that is not the authority. Handing back a fresh array per stream would allocate on every one of those ticks, which AGENTS.md rule 29 forbids and which none of rule 31's five relaxations covers. The arriving bytes are copied into one buffer instead, and TryDequeue(out byte[], out int, out int) hands back the offset and length of a stream inside it. How the buffer is reused. The write cursor returns to the start on the first append after the queue has been drained. That is deliberately not "on the last dequeue": a caller reads the bytes after TryDequeue(out byte[], out int, out int) has returned, and resetting there would let the next arriving stream overwrite them while the caller was still reading. Resetting on the next append instead means a view stays readable until new bytes arrive, and a view that old is stale in any case. What it assumes about threads. Nothing here is thread safe. Both providers append from the netcode backend's own receive callback and drain from ScriptRunner.TickFrameUpdate, and both of those run on the main thread in separate phases of one frame. Fields HeaderBytes How many bytes of a payload IsStreamHeader(byte, byte, byte) reads. public const int HeaderBytes = 3 Field Value int Properties Count How many streams are waiting. public int Count { get; } Property Value int Methods Append(byte[], int, int) Copies one arrived stream in. public void Append(byte[] payload, int offset, int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The buffer the stream arrived in. int offset Where the stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Clear() Drops everything waiting. Called when a session ends, so that a stream from the previous session cannot be applied in the next one. public void Clear() IsStreamHeader(byte, byte, byte) Whether the first three bytes of an arriving payload are a transform stream's. public static bool IsStreamHeader(byte first, byte second, byte third) Parameters Type Name Description byte first The payload's first byte. byte second Its second byte. byte third Its third byte. Returns bool False for a payload some other system sent. Examples if (TransformStreamInbox.IsStreamHeader(first, second, third) == false) return; Remarks A stream travels as an unnamed message, which carries no name of its own, so a provider is handed every unnamed payload in the session including ones this product did not send. This is what lets a provider drop those before copying them: without it, another system's large payload grows the provider's receive buffer and this inbox's buffer to its size, and neither ever shrinks. It is three byte comparisons and not a parse. The reader checks the same three bytes again when it decodes; that is not a duplicate for the sake of it, because a payload can also arrive through a provider that never saw it as an unnamed message. TryDequeue(out byte[], out int, out int) The next waiting stream, as a view into the inbox's own buffer. public bool TryDequeue(out byte[] payload, out int offset, out int length) Parameters Type Name Description byte[] payload The inbox's buffer. int offset Where this stream starts in it. int length How many bytes it occupies. Returns bool False when nothing is waiting.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Transform.summary: Struct TransformSyncDeclaration Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll One Sync.Position, Sync.Rotation or Sync.Scale as the build recorded it: which channel, at which cadence, and which slots hold the per-object bookkeeping the network tick needs. Built by ScriptBuildContext and read by ScriptRunner; a script never sees one. public readonly struct TransformSyncDeclaration Expand Details ... Remarks The shadow slots are the one part worth reading twice, because they mean two things at once and that is deliberate. On the peer with authority they hold the last value it put in the stream. On every other peer they hold the last value it took out of one. Both are the same fact - the value the two ends agree on - which is exactly what a change is measured against, so the position channel's change encoding needs no second set of slots to decode with. The rotation channel uses one shadow slot, not three, and what it holds is not a coordinate. A rotation is sent whole rather than as a change, so the only thing the authority needs to remember is the 32 bits it last sent, and ShadowSlotX holds exactly those, as a Number, which carries a 32-bit integer without rounding. ShadowSlotY and ShadowSlotZ are CodeSmile.LunyScript.ScriptBuildContext.NoShadowSlot there: a negative index cannot address a slot, so a path that read one by mistake fails its bounds check rather than reading an unrelated variable. For a rotation, the slot holding the 32 bits last sent. public NumberSlot ShadowSlotX { get; } Property Value NumberSlot ShadowSlotY The slot holding the y of the value both ends agree on. public NumberSlot ShadowSlotY { get; } Property Value NumberSlot ShadowSlotZ The slot holding the z of the value both ends agree on. public NumberSlot ShadowSlotZ { get; } Property Value NumberSlot StalenessSlot How many seconds since a value for this channel arrived, which Net.SecondsSinceUpdate reads. public NumberSlot StalenessSlot { get; } Property Value NumberSlot UnencodableReportedSlot The slot latching that this object's value was already reported as outside what the stream's encoding holds. Set once and never cleared, so the report is made once for an object and not again. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.UIGateway.title: Class UIGateway | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.UIGateway.summary: Class UIGateway Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The core's one entry point to UI Toolkit. Resolves declared names to VisualElement once per instance at spawn and again on panel reload, and answers the writes, reads and occurrence tests the UI blocks make. public sealed class UIGateway Expand Details ... Inheritance object UIGateway Remarks A per-use Q is a defect. Blocks store interned names and declaration indices because the shared script tree cannot hold an element. This gateway holds the resolved element per instance. The per-frame path never queries the visual tree. The supported scene component is PanelRenderer. UIDocument is not probed. Close writes display = None and keeps this cache. Destroy is should-have and is not in this version. This file names VisualElement and VisualTreeAsset. PanelRenderer lookup lives on GameObjectHost. Blocks never name either type.

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Var-1.htm.title: Struct Var<T> | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.Var-1.htm.summary: Struct Var<T> Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll A handle to one variable of a script. Returned by Var.Define at build time; the operators and methods on it build blocks. public readonly struct Var<T> where T : struct Type Parameters T What the variable holds: Number, Flag, Text, Vec3, Rotation, Vec2 or a declared C# enum. AGENTS.md rule 12 makes Number the number type, so there is no Var<Int32> and no Var<Single>. Expand Details ... Examples var health = Var.Define<Number>("health", 100.0); On.FrameUpdate(If(health > 10).Then(health.Add(-1)).Else(health.Set(0))); Remarks The handle is an index, not a value: it says where the variable lives on every instance of the program, and the same handle reads a different number on every object running the script. A handle is valid only inside the Build that declared it. It carries a slot index and a kind and nothing that identifies its program, so a handle from one script used in another script's Build addresses that other script's slot of the same index. Take a ScoreScript holding static Var<Number> Score at index 0, and a PickupScript whose own first variable is cooldown: writing On.Ready(ScoreScript.Score.Add(10.0)) inside PickupScript.Build adds 10 to every pickup's cooldown and never moves the score. Where the borrowed index is past the end of the borrowing program's array, ScriptInstance throws LunyScriptUsageException naming this cause; where it is within range, as here, nothing detects it. Declare each script's variables in its own Build. An operation the variable's kind does not support throws at build time, not at compile time. health.Add("text") is a compile error, because Add takes T. But playerName + 1 compiles and then throws LunyScriptUsageException while the script type is built, because C# 9 has no static abstract interface members and an operator declared on a generic type therefore cannot be restricted to one instantiation of it. Build runs once per script type at launch, so a script that can throw one of these throws it on the first run. docs/slice-decisions.md records the alternative that was rejected. operator == on a handle builds a condition block; it does not compare handles. Use Equals(object) to compare two handles. Properties Capacity How many bytes a text variable holds. Meaningless when Kind is not Text. public TextCapacity Capacity { get; } Property Value TextCapacity EnumSlot This variable's enum slot. public EnumSlot EnumSlot { get; } Property Value EnumSlot Examples var slot = Equipped.EnumSlot; Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The variable is not an enum variable. FlagSlot This variable's Flag slot. public FlagSlot FlagSlot { get; } Property Value FlagSlot Examples var slot = alive.FlagSlot; Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The variable is not a Flag. Inverse The orientation that undoes this orientation variable's, as an expression. public RotationValueBlock Inverse { get; } Property Value RotationValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Facing.Set(Facing.Inverse)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This is not a Rotation variable. Kind Which slot array on the instance this variable lives in. public SlotKind Kind { get; } Property Value SlotKind Length How long this spatial variable's value is, as a number expression. public NumberValueBlock Length { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Speed.Set(Velocity.Length)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This is not a Vec3 variable. LengthSquared How long this spatial variable's value is squared, as a number expression. public NumberValueBlock LengthSquared { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(If(Offset.LengthSquared <= 4.0).Then(...)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This is not a Vec3 or Vec2 variable. Name The name the script declared, used in diagnostics and by the future runtime inspector. Never read on the run-time path. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Normalized This spatial variable's value scaled to a length of one, as an expression. A value of no length normalizes to zero rather than to a NaN. public Vec3ValueBlock Normalized { get; } Property Value Vec3ValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Heading.Set(Offset.Normalized)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This is not a Vec3 variable. NumberSlot This variable's Number slot. public NumberSlot NumberSlot { get; } Property Value NumberSlot Examples var slot = health.NumberSlot; Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The variable is not a Number. RotationSlot This variable's orientation slot. public RotationSlot RotationSlot { get; } Property Value RotationSlot Examples var slot = Facing.RotationSlot; Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The variable is not a Rotation variable. TextSlot This variable's text slot, including its declared capacity. public TextSlot TextSlot { get; } Property Value TextSlot Examples var slot = playerName.TextSlot; Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The variable is not a text variable. Vec2Slot This variable's two-component spatial slot. public Vec2Slot Vec2Slot { get; } Property Value Vec2Slot Examples var slot = Stick.Vec2Slot; Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The variable is not a Vec2 variable. Vec3Slot This variable's spatial slot. public Vec3Slot Vec3Slot { get; } Property Value Vec3Slot Examples var slot = Spawn.Vec3Slot; Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The variable is not a Vec3 variable. X This spatial variable's first component, as a number expression. public NumberValueBlock X { get; } Property Value NumberValueBlock Examples On.FrameUpdate(Height.Set(Spawn.X)); Remarks This and the members below it are one-line pass-throughs to the same members on Vec3ValueBlock and RotationValueBlock, and they exist because C# applies no user-defined conversion before a member access: without them, Spawn.Length would not compile even though Spawn converts to a spatial expression wherever one is expected. The C# operators are the one part this cannot cover. Spawn * 2.0 does not compile, because operator lookup also runs on the operands' own types and neither is a spatial expression. Put the variable in a local of the expression type first - Vec3ValueBlock spawn = Spawn; - and the operators are available on it. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This is not a Vec3 variable. Negate(string, int) Builds a block that writes this variable's own value back with the opposite sign, so a direction reverses without its magnitude being named. public Block Negate(string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. It records the line this block was written on, so a later failure names that line rather than LunyScript's own source. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns Block A block to place in an event list. Examples On.FrameUpdate(If((travelledX > 3.0) & (step > 0.0)).Then(step.Negate())); Remarks Which shape is right for a ping-pong, stated because the obvious one is wrong. Negate is not idempotent: Set(-0.02) run twice leaves the same value, Negate run twice leaves the original value. So a single condition on position alone, If(travelledX > 3.0).Then(step.Negate()) // wrong flips the sign on every frame that condition holds. An object that leaves the bound within one frame turns around once and nothing looks wrong; an object that lingers past the bound for n frames flips n times and vibrates in place. Guard on the direction of travel as well as the position, and give each bound its own condition: If((travelledX > 3.0) & (step > 0.0)).Then(step.Negate()), If((travelledX < -3.0) & (step < 0.0)).Then(step.Negate()) After the first flip step > 0.0 is false, so further frames spent past the bound change nothing, and the magnitude the flip preserves is whatever the variable held. docs/proposals/var-negate.md states the reasoning and SliceScript is written in this shape. Negating 0 produces negative zero, which compares equal to 0 in every comparison this API builds, so a step == 0.0 test answers the same before and after. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException This is not a Number variable. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.VarFactor.title: Struct VarFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.VarFactor.summary: Struct VarFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The Var surface inside Build(): declares a script's variables and hands back the typed handles the blocks are built from. public readonly struct VarFactory Expand Details ... Examples protected override void Build() { var health = Var.Define<Number>("health", 100.0); var playerName = Var.DefineText("playerName"); } Remarks This is a build-time surface. Every call runs once per script type, before any object exists, and constructs part of the shared Script program, which is why it may allocate. The blocks returned during that build execute later, per event and per Script instance. AGENTS.md rule 43; rule 25 forbids reading anything about an object here. Methods DefineAllocatingText(string, int) Declares a text variable that uses bounded heap storage rather than a FixedString. The bound is UTF-8 bytes. This variable cannot be synchronised. public Var<Text> DefineAllocatingText(string name, int maxBytes) Parameters Type Name Description string name The name, which should come from nameof. int maxBytes How many UTF-8 bytes it may hold, from 1 to 1048576. Returns Var<Text> The typed handle. Examples Log = Var.DefineAllocatingText(nameof(Log), 16384); DefineSyncedText(string, SyncCadence, TextCapacity) Declares a text variable that every peer sees. public Var<Text> DefineSyncedText(string name, SyncCadence cadence, TextCapacity capacity = TextCapacity.Bytes64) Parameters Type Name Description string name The variable's name, which should come from nameof. SyncCadence cadence How often it is sent. Required, per AGENTS.md rule 46: a synchronised variable whose cost nobody chose cannot be written. Text carries a managed string on the wire, so EveryTick is refused for it and Once is the usual choice. TextCapacity capacity How many bytes it holds. Defaults to Bytes64, which is one cache line. Returns Var<Text> The handle. Examples PlayerName = Var.DefineSyncedText(nameof(PlayerName), SyncCadence.Once); Motto = Var.DefineSyncedText(nameof(Motto), SyncCadence.OnChange, TextCapacity.Bytes512); Remarks The cadence comes before the capacity, which is the opposite of the order the proposal wrote. C# allows no required parameter after an optional one, so a defaulted capacity and a required cadence can only be written in this order. It is also the order DefineSynced<T>(string, SyncCadence, T) already uses: the name, then the cadence, then the one thing that has a sensible default. Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The cadence is unset, the cadence is EveryTick, or the name is taken. DefineSynced<T>(string, SyncCadence, T) Declares a variable that every peer sees, with the cadence that says what it costs. Its only method is Changed(params Block[]), which registers the watch with the build. public readonly struct VarWatchBuilder<T> where T : struct Type Parameters T Expand Details ... Examples When.Var(playerName).Changed(score.Set(0.0)); Remarks A watch is polled once per frame, after the frame-update blocks. It compares the variable against a second slot of the same kind, allocated at build time, that holds what the variable was the last time the watch ran. A value that changes and changes back within one frame therefore does not fire. That is the semantic, stated rather than hidden; docs/execution-model.md and docs/slice-decisions.md record why polling was chosen over notifying on write. reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ViewFacto.title: Struct ViewFactory | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.ViewFacto.summary: Struct ViewFactory Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Assembly ApiSource.dll The View surface inside Build(): what a local player sees, and which camera rig it renders. public readonly struct ViewFactory Expand Details ... Examples On.Ready(View.For(Screen).SetCamera(ChaseRig)); Remarks A view and a camera rig are two objects, not one. The view is the thing that draws part of the screen; the rig is the authored Cinemachine configuration that decides where the shot is. Keeping them separate is what lets one rig serve a group view and four separate views serve four local players, which is the accepted design's own reason for the split. Both are declared asset inputs, assigned per object in the Inspector. The core cannot name a Camera or a Cinemachine type, so a view and a rig reach the camera adapter as the object a declared input resolved to, and the adapter is what knows whether the object is one. An object that is not is reported and nothing is written. The camera family is routed through Cinemachine and nothing else. That is the captain's answer on the camera family, 2026-09-13. With the Cinemachine package absent, CodeSmile.LunyScript.Cinemachine does not compile in, no provider is installed, and every block on this surface writes nothing and says so once. This surface's shape is provisional. It implements the recorded recommendation of the open decision contract-view-routing, which keeps the view separate from its rig and its target group. The alternative that decision holds open makes the player the entry point instead. Nothing below this surface depends on which is chosen. Methods For(AssetInput, string, int) Names the view the blocks that follow act on. public ViewBuilder For(AssetInput view, string callerFilePath = null, int callerLineNumber = 0) Parameters Type Name Description AssetInput view The declared asset input holding the view. An Asset<T> converts to one on its own. string callerFilePath Supplied by the compiler. Do not pass one. int callerLineNumber Supplied by the compiler. Returns ViewBuilder A builder whose two methods produce the blocks. Examples On.Ready(View.For(Screen).SetCamera(ChaseRig)); Exceptions LunyScriptUsageException The handle is one Build() never assigned, or this factory was not obtained inside Build().

reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.html.title: Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript | LunyScript API Reference
reference/CodeSmile.LunyScript.html.summary: Namespace CodeSmile.LunyScript Classes ActionBlock A block whose objective can take more than one frame, and which therefore reports ActionResult rather than simply running to completion. ActivateObjectBlock What Object.Activate() and Object.Activate(name) build: activates the object the script runs on, or one the script created. AdapterAdmission The package and version admission table for extension blocks and optional adapters. AssetAttribute Declares an asset input whose handle is assigned before Build, in declaration order. AssetGateway Owns in-flight Asset.Load attempts and owner-acquisition records for one ScriptRunner. Bound Inspector loads complete from the instance's already resolved input. Resources loads go through IAssetLoadProvider. Script code never sees a Task or an exception type; AGENTS.md rules 50 and 51. AssetLoadBlock What Asset.Load(source).As(handle) builds: starts one asynchronous content acquisition bound to an operation handle. Completion yields an owned typed asset on that handle, or a classified failure. Failure does not fall through to an asset placeholder. AssetPlaceholders The asset placeholder every asset type falls back to when an input of that type is left unassigned, and the two ways one is configured. AssetReleaseBlock What Asset.Release(acquisition) builds: relinquishes this owner's acquisition. Bound consumers retain content they still need. Release does not destroy them and does not promise immediate physical reclamation. AssetSource Names the provider-qualified sources a declared asset input can load from. AudioGateway The runner-owned audio service: pooled one-shot voices, named bound-source control, and mixer writes. Bound playback on the object a script runs on lives on IScriptHost instead. Block One step of behaviour in a script. A block object is created once, when its script type is built, and is then shared by every object running that script; the per-object state it reads and writes lives in slots on the ScriptInstance passed to Execute(ScriptInstance). CameraGateway The core's one entry point to the camera. Owns the ICameraProvider, passes each authored operation to it, and reports a refused one once. CloudSaveGateway Owns every in-flight Cloud Save request for one ScriptRunner, keyed by the save key. Signs in when the first request arrives, queues requests made before the service is ready, coalesces duplicates, polls each operation once per frame, and classifies every failure once into an OperationFailure. No script and no block ever sees a Task or an exception type; AGENTS.md section 12. CompilationFacts What the compiler was told when this assembly was built. Read by tests and by the release gate, so that a claim about release behaviour can name the compilation it was measured in. ConditionBlock A block that answers true or false for one object. Passed to If(...) and combined with &, | and !. CreateObjectBlock What Object.Create(name) builds: creates a new, empty, active object owned by the instance that runs this block, and records it in the owned-object slot the build assigned to that name. DeactivateObjectBlock What Object.Deactivate() and Object.Deactivate(name) build: deactivates the object the script runs on, or one the script created. DespawnObjectBlock What Object.Despawn() and Object.Despawn(name) build: ends the object the script runs on, or destroys one the script created. DiagnosticBuffer Fixed-capacity, ordered storage shared by console and trace readers. DiagnosticCatalog Immutable catalog for one built program. DiagnosticCommand Caller-owned receipt. Terminal results survive target closure and are never replayed. DiagnosticFault Observed contained error or failed outer boundary, separate from enabled state. DiagnosticNode Immutable declaration metadata; never contains a live block or delegate. DiagnosticProtocol Local diagnostics protocol version. Current snapshots and optional action records are separate observations. DiagnosticSnapshot Caller-owned current state from an idle main-thread boundary, never execution history. DiagnosticTrace Explicit action capture for one instance lifetime. Disposal changes no script state. DiagnosticVariable One immutable declared variable, including whether it is internal storage. EditorScript The editor entry: a subclass whose Build() composes blocks that run in an EditorScriptSession. Game scripts subclass Script instead. A concrete EditorScript identifies the editor role without an attribute. EnumValueBlock The root of every enum expression: something that produces an integer code when the block holding it runs. FakeAssetLoadProvider An in-memory asset-load backend for tests: keys map to objects a test registered, a missing key fails as NotFound, and a registered object of another type fails as Denied. No Resources folder is required. AGENTS.md rule 52's shape applied to assets. FakeCameraProvider A camera backend that records what it was asked to do, with no Cinemachine package, no camera and no scene. FakeInputProvider An input backend that holds its actions and their values in memory, with no device, no window and no Input System package. FakeNetworkProvider A netcode backend that runs entirely in this process, with no network, no Editor and no Netcode for GameObjects. Two instances are paired with Pair(out FakeNetworkProvider, out FakeNetworkProvider) and each one's sends arrive in the other's queues. FileCloudSaveProvider The file-based Cloud Save provider: one file per key, under a directory the caller names. A first-class part of the product, not a test fixture; AGENTS.md rule 52. It is how every failure branch is tested without a network, and what makes the automated suite runnable with no credentials. FlagValueBlock A block that produces a Flag for one object: a variable read or a literal. GameObjectHost The runtime IScriptHost for a GameObject, as the blocks see it. InputGateway The core's one entry point to player input. Owns the IInputProvider, resolves each program's declared actions once, and answers the value reads and the occurrence tests the input blocks make. InstanceLayout How many slots of each kind one instance of a program owns, and what value each slot starts from. Built once per script type and never changed afterwards. LunyScriptBehaviour Assigns one GameObject to one script type. This is the component a user adds; the script is named by an explicit field rather than by a type name written as a string. LunyScriptContactBehaviour Unity physics callbacks for one managed object whose script declared at least one of the six contact events. LunyScriptBehaviour adds this component only in that case, so an object whose script declares none of them is not subscribed. LunyScriptContractException Thrown when LunyScript observes that the lifecycle ownership contract was broken: the object running a script was destroyed, reparented or otherwise changed by native Unity API rather than by a LunyScript block. LunyScriptDriverBehaviour Ticks one ScriptRunner once per frame, and sweeps instances whose object a scene unload took away. Lives on a hidden object that LunyScriptRuntime creates; a user never adds this component. LunyScriptException The root of every exception LunyScript throws. Catch this to catch everything the product raised and nothing else. LunyScriptInternalException Thrown when LunyScript's own invariant was broken on a path a user cannot reach: a null or an impossible value inside the product's internals. LunyScriptLog The one place LunyScript writes to the Unity console. Unity log lines are formatted here; the LunyScript console reads the retained structured fields. LunyScriptLogAreas The area names the product's own log records carry, so that a reader and a debugging window see the same set of words rather than one spelling per call site. LunyScriptRuntime Holds the one ScriptRunner that LunyScriptBehaviour components share, and the hidden object that ticks it once per frame. LunyScriptUsageException Thrown when script code asks LunyScript for something the API does not offer: a C# if around a condition block, an arithmetic operator on a text variable, a builder finished twice. NetworkGateway The core's one entry point to netcode. Owns the INetworkProvider, refuses the session calls that are a user mistake, and drains the provider's two queues once per tick. AGENTS.md rules 44 to 49. NodeDescription Collects named child nodes while building immutable program metadata. NumberValueBlock A block that produces a Number for one object: a variable read, a literal, or an arithmetic expression over other value blocks. ReleaseGate Gate 4. Runs inside a standalone player built without DEBUG and asserts what only that build can show: that operator true and operator false on a condition block still throw, that the [Conditional] contract guards are gone, and that the two guards written out unconditionally are not. ResourcesAssetLoadProvider The Resources backend for Asset.Load of an AssetSource.Resources key. The read happens inside the provider call, which is a start boundary, and the gateway observes the completed operation on its next poll. Blocks never name UnityEngine.Resources. RotationValueBlock The root of every orientation expression: something that produces a Rotation when the block holding it runs. RunnerDiagnostics Native diagnostics for one explicitly supplied local runner. Reads execute no authored logic. Script The runtime entry: a subclass whose Build() composes blocks that run on a game object. Editor workflows subclass EditorScript instead. ScriptBase Shared infrastructure for Script and EditorScript. One instance of a concrete subclass is compiled into one ScriptProgram, once, and every object running that script shares it. ScriptBuildContext The state one Build() accumulates: the slots its variables declared and the blocks its event registrations produced. Exists for the duration of one build and is then turned into an immutable ScriptProgram. ScriptInstance One object's state for one program: the slot arrays the program's layout asked for, and the host the blocks act on. The blocks themselves are shared by every instance of the program and hold no per-object state at all. ScriptProgram One script type, built. Holds the immutable block tree, the On.* event table and the instance layout, and is shared by every object running that script. ScriptRunner Owns the built programs, the live instances and the instance pool, and runs each event kind across every instance. SpawnObjectBlock What Object.Spawn(prefab) and its chain build: produces an object from a declared prefab input, places it, parents it, and holds it in an owned-object slot when the chain named one. TextCapacities Facts about TextCapacity that both the layout and the blocks need. TextFormat A parsed Text.Format call: the literal pieces of the format, which value fills each hole, and how many decimal places each number hole asks for. Pass it to a text variable's Set. TextLengths Facts about TextLength that collection storage needs. TimeReadBlock What Time.Delta and Time.Elapsed return: a number expression reading one of the runner's two clocks, and the one place the clock choice is written. TransformStreamInbox Holds the transform streams that arrived since the last tick drained them, in one buffer the inbox owns. Every INetworkProvider uses one, so that the receive side of the stream is written once rather than once per backend. UIGateway The core's one entry point to UI Toolkit. Resolves declared names to VisualElement once per instance at spawn and again on panel reload, and answers the writes, reads and occurrence tests the UI blocks make. VariableAttribute Declares a variable whose handle is assigned before Build, in declaration order. Vec2ValueBlock The root of every two-component spatial expression: something that produces a Vec2 when the block holding it runs. Vec3ValueBlock The root of every spatial expression: something that produces a Vec3 when the block holding it runs. Structs AdapterRegistration One extension block type an adapter registered, with the Unity package and minimum version that type needs. AimedLookAtBuilder A facing whose up direction has been named. It converts to a block and takes no further clause. AssetFactory The Asset surface inside Build(): starts and ends content acquisitions. Unity owns the asset. LunyScript owns the attempt, the owner-acquisition, and consumer retention. AssetInput One declared asset input with its type forgotten: what a surface takes when it accepts an input of any Unity type, such as the camera rig a view renders. AssetInputAssignment One row of the declared-input table a host component serializes: the name of a declared input and the asset this object assigns to it. AssetLoadBuilder What Asset.Load(source) returns: an unfinished acquisition that becomes a block when As(Operation, string, int) binds the operation handle. An unbound Load is refused when Build() finishes. AssetSource<T> One provider-qualified place a declared asset input loads from when the host assigns nothing. Asset<T> A handle to one asset input of a script. Returned by Bind.Asset at build time; reading the asset itself is an instance read, because the value belongs to the object and not to the script type. AudioFactory The Audio surface inside Build(): one-shot play, bound source control, and named mixer writes. It hides UnityEngine.AudioSource inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. AudioMixerHandle What Audio.Mixer(mixer) returns: named exposed-parameter writes. AudioPlacedOneShotBuilder A one-shot whose placement has been named. It converts to a block and takes no further placement clause. AudioPlayOneShotBuilder What Audio.PlayOneShot(clip) returns: a 2D one-shot, or one placement. AudioSourceHandle What Audio.For(source) returns: bound-source control on that object. BindFactory The Bind surface inside Build(): declares the assets a script needs and hands back the typed handles that read them. BodyFactory The Body surface inside Build(): observations of what physics actually did to the object this script runs on. CameraFactory The Camera surface inside Build(): what one camera rig tracks. It hides UnityEngine.Camera inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. CameraRigBuilder What Camera.For(rig) returns: the rig's two tracking targets and its target group. CameraTargetsBuilder What Camera.For(rig).Targets returns: the five operations on a rig's group of tracked objects. ChooseBiasedBuilder A Choose chain that already has Bias. Optional Hold(Elapsed, string, int) follows. ChooseBuilder What Choose(subject) returns. Its one call, Highest(params UtilityOption[]), names the scored options. ChooseCompleteBuilder A Choose chain that has both Bias and Hold. Used as a block it starts the selector. ChooseHeldBuilder A Choose chain that already has Hold. Optional Bias(double, string, int) follows. ChooseHighestBuilder A Choose(subject).Highest(...) chain. Optional Bias(double, string, int) and Hold(Elapsed, string, int) follow; used as a block it starts the selector. CloudFactory The Cloud surface inside Build(): builds the start blocks for Cloud Save. A start block enqueues and returns in the same call; the outcome arrives through When.Cloud(key). AGENTS.md rule 50. CloudWatchBuilder What When.Cloud(key) returns: registers blocks against one key's Cloud Save outcomes. Each registration declares a hidden counter-shadow variable at build time and is polled once per frame after On.FrameUpdate, the same shape When.Var(x).Changed has. CollectionRead A typed read of one collection entry: either At(index) or the current ForEach item. Each use reads the entry addressed by that expression, so a replacement of the current element is visible to the next read in the same body. CursorInputFactory What Input.Cursor returns: lock and visibility as two independent writes on the machine cursor. Four local players share one cursor; this surface is not on Input.ForPlayer. DefineFactory The Define surface inside Build(): declares a script's variables with the author spelling Round 06 settled, and hands back the typed handles the blocks are built from. DiagnosticIdentity Identifies one lifetime independently of pooled object reuse. DiagnosticValue A typed diagnostic value. Text is a caller-owned managed representation. Elapsed An elapsed duration written with a unit constructor: Seconds(1), Milliseconds(500), Minutes(2) or Hours(1). EnumSlot Where one declared C# enum variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. FakeCameraProvider.TargetGroupEntry One object in a rig's target group, with the weight and radius it was given. Flag A boolean literal and the type argument of a Var<Flag>. FlagBindBuilder What Bind.Flag returns. It converts to no handle; Shared is required. FlagDefineBuilder What Define.Flag returns: an object-local flag unless Shared is called. FlagSlot Where one Flag variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. ForEachListBuilder<T> What ForEach(list) returns. Its only method is Do(Func<CollectionRead, Block>). ForEachMapBuilder<TKey, TValue> What ForEach(map) returns. Its only method is Do(Func<CollectionRead, CollectionRead, Block>). GateFactory The Gate surface: named, nested, runner-wide masks of suppressed categories. IfBuilder What If(condition) returns. Its only method is Then(params Block[]), so a condition without a consequence does not compile. IfThenBuilder What If(condition).Then(...) returns: either add an Else(params Block[]) or use it as a block, which the implicit conversion does. InputButton A handle to one pressed-or-not action of one local player. Returned by Input.ForPlayer(player).Button(name) at build time; the members on it build blocks. InputFactory The Input surface inside Build(): names the local player whose actions this script reads. It hides UnityEngine.Input inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. InputNumber A handle to one single-axis action of one local player. Returned by Input.ForPlayer(player).Number(name) at build time. InputRebindBuilder What handle.Rebind() returns. Bind it with .As(operation) before Build() returns, or Finish refuses the chain naming this type and the authored line. InputVector2 A handle to one two-axis action of one local player. Returned by Input.ForPlayer(player).Vector2(name) at build time. InputVector3 A handle to one three-axis action of one local player. Returned by Input.ForPlayer(player).Vector3(name) at build time. InputWatchBuilder What When.Input(action) returns. Its three methods register the blocks that run on a frame where the action reported that occurrence. ListDefineBuilder<T> What Define.List returns: an empty list of the declared capacity. ListHandle<T> A handle to one fixed-capacity list declared with Define.List<T>. Occupancy starts at zero. The C# type is not List<T>, because that name collides with System.Collections.Generic.List. LookAtBuilder What LookAt returns: the facing, about the world up unless WithUp(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int) names another direction. LunyScriptLogRecord One thing LunyScript has to say, as structured fields rather than as a finished string. MapDefineBuilder<TKey, TValue> What Define.Map returns: an empty map of the declared capacity. MapHandle<TKey, TValue> A handle to one fixed-capacity map declared with Define.Map<TKey, TValue>. Occupancy starts at zero. Existing-key assignment replaces the value and keeps insertion order. MathFactory The core numeric functions, written as Math.Abs(...) inside a script's Build(). Every member returns an expression that is evaluated each time the block holding it runs; none of them writes anything. MotionDisplacementBuilder What Motion.MoveBy returns: a displacement along the object's own axes unless InWorldSpace() is written. MotionFaceTowardsBuilder What Motion.FaceTowards returns. Incomplete until DegreesPerSecond(NumberValueBlock, string, int). MotionFaceTowardsRatedBuilder A FaceTowards whose rate has been named. Converts to a block. MotionFactory The Motion surface inside Build(): component-directed movement, force and relocation for the object a script runs on. MotionForceBuilder What Motion.AddForce and Motion.AddImpulse return: object-local axes unless InWorldSpace() is written. MotionMoveToAtSpeedBuilder A MoveTo whose rate has been named. Converts to a block. MotionMoveToBuilder What Motion.MoveTo returns. Incomplete until AtSpeed(NumberValueBlock, string, int). MotionMoveToDurationBuilder A MoveTo whose duration amount has been named. Incomplete until an elapsed unit. MotionRotateToBuilder What Motion.RotateTo returns. Incomplete until DegreesPerSecond(NumberValueBlock, string, int). MotionRotateToDurationBuilder A RotateTo whose duration amount has been named. Incomplete until an elapsed unit. MotionRotateToRatedBuilder A RotateTo whose rate has been named. Converts to a block. MotionTeleportBuilder What Motion.TeleportTo returns: a position write, or WithRotation(RotationValueBlock, string, int) first. MotionTeleportOrientedBuilder A teleport whose orientation has been named. Converts to a block. MotionVelocityBuilder What Motion.SetVelocity returns: object-local axes unless InWorldSpace() is written. NetFactory The Net surface a script reads the session through: who has authority, whether there is a session, how many peers, how far behind a value is, and the one way to ask the authority to do something. NetSendFactory Net.Send: the one way a peer without authority asks the authority to do something. NetworkMessage One received message: which object it is about, which message it is, and which peer sent it. Sender is carried because rule 45 forbids hiding ownership, and a script that reacts to a message usually needs to know who asked. NetworkValue One value crossing the network, typed rather than boxed. NetworkVariableUpdate One received variable update: which object, which synchronised variable, and the value. Number A numeric literal and the type argument of a Var<Number>. NumberBindBuilder What Bind.Number returns. It converts to no handle; Shared is required. NumberDefineBuilder What Define.Number returns: an object-local number unless Shared is called. NumberSlot Where one Number variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. ObjectLifetimeFactory The Object surface inside Build(): builds the blocks that create, activate, deactivate and end objects this script owns. OnApplicationFactory On.Application: what Unity reported about the application as a whole, rather than about one object. OnAuthorityFactory On.Authority: the two events a script gets when this peer starts or stops being the one that may write the object's synchronised variables. OnEditorFactory The On surface on EditorScript: Ready, Created, Enabled, Disabled, Despawned, and EditorUpdate. Frame, physics and application events live on Script. OnFactory The On surface inside Build(): registers blocks against the events the runner raises. Operation A handle to one observable attempt. Declared with Operation.Define(nameof(X)) inside Build(); family start blocks bind it with .As(handle). OperationFactory The Operation surface inside Build(): declares a handle with one observable attempt at a time. OperationWatchBuilder What When.Operation(handle) returns: registers blocks against one attempt's classified outcomes. Each registration declares a hidden counter-shadow variable at build time and is polled once per frame after On.FrameUpdate, the same shape When.Cloud(key).Saved has. Operation<T> A typed operation handle. The attempt, generation, deadline and classified outcome are the same surface as Operation. A typed payload is filled by a later family that owns the result type. OrbitPointBuilder What RotateAround(point) returns: the pivot, waiting for the rotation to apply about it. OrbitRotationBuilder What RotateAround(point).By(rotation) returns: the orbit, waiting for the one thing a caller has to say about it. OtherFactory The Other surface inside Build(): the other collider of the contact event currently running. PanelCloseBuilder What Panel.Close(menu) returns. ForPlayer is required. PanelFactory The Panel surface inside Build(): typed binds, Place of a UXML fragment, and Open/Close of a menu. It hides PanelRenderer inside a Script the same way Transform hides UnityEngine.Transform. PanelHandle What Panel.For(panel) returns: typed elements on that panel's document. PanelOpenBuilder What Panel.Open(menu) returns. ForPlayer is required. PlaceAtBuilder What Panel.Place(uxml) returns. At is required; In is optional. PlayerInputFactory What Input.ForPlayer(player) returns: one method per kind of value an action produces, each declaring one action and handing back the typed handle that reads it. Prefab A handle to one prefab input of a script. Returned by Bind.Prefab at build time; what the input holds is an instance read, because the value belongs to the object and not to the script type. RandomChoiceBuilder What Random.Choice returns. Incomplete until From(RandomStream, string, int). RandomChoiceFromBuilder A choice that has named its stream. Incomplete until Into(Var<Number>). RandomFactory The Random surface inside Build(): named streams and draws that store a result. A draw consumes one sample when the block runs; later reads of the result reuse it. RandomIndexBuilder What Random.Index() returns. Incomplete until From(RandomStream). RandomIndexCountBuilder An index draw that has named its count. Incomplete until Into(Var<Number>). RandomIndexFromBuilder An index draw that has named its stream. Incomplete until In(NumberValueBlock, string, int). RandomNumberBuilder What Random.Number() returns. Incomplete until From(RandomStream). RandomNumberFromBuilder A number draw that has named its stream. Incomplete until In(NumberValueBlock, NumberValueBlock, string, int). RandomNumberRangeBuilder A number draw that has named its range. Incomplete until Into(Var<Number>). RandomStream A named random stream declared inside Build(). Mutable state lives on the instance; this handle is an index, the same way a variable handle is. RandomStreamSlot Where one named random stream's state lives on every instance of a program. RandomWeightedBuilder What Random.Weighted returns. Incomplete until WithWeights(params NumberValueBlock[]). RandomWeightedFromBuilder A weighted choice that has named its stream. Incomplete until Into(Var<Number>). RandomWeightedWeightsBuilder A weighted choice that has its weights. Incomplete until From(RandomStream, string, int). ReparentBuilder What SetParent(...) and Unparent() return: the reparent, which keeps the object's world placement unless KeepLocal() says otherwise. Rotation An orientation in three dimensions, held as a unit quaternion. RotationSlot Where one Rotation variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. RoutineBuilder What Routine(name) returns. Its one call, Run(params Block[]), takes the steps the routine runs in order and produces the block that starts an activation of it. RoutineGroupBuilder What InParallel(...) returns: a concurrent group with no ending clause yet. RoutineGroupEndingBuilder A concurrent group that carries an early-ending clause. Its one further call decides what happens to the children that had not finished when the group published its result. RoutineGroupSurvivorBuilder A concurrent group whose unfinished children the enclosing routine activation owns after the group publishes its result. The routine advances those children during its following steps and cancels them when that routine activation ends or is cancelled. RunCadenceBuilder A cadence that has named its unit. Start(string, int) runs it indefinitely; For(NumberValueBlock, string, int) adds a duration or count bound. RunEveryAmountBuilder A Run(body).Every(amount) chain. Incomplete until a unit. RunForAmountBuilder A Run(body).For(amount) chain. Incomplete until a unit or Times. RunHandle A finished Run chain. Start(string, int) starts or restarts one activation; Stop(string, int) interrupts it. RunWorkBuilder What Run(body) returns. Qualifiers name a duration, a cadence, or a repetition count; Start(string, int) starts one activation and Stop(string, int) interrupts it. SharedFactory The Shared surface inside Build(): operations on a shared store rather than on one variable. SharedStore The identity of one shared-variable store: the default store, or a named one such as the current level. SourceLocation Where in a user's script a block was authored: the file and the line of the Build() call that created it. SpacedMotionDisplacementBuilder A Motion displacement whose frame has been named. It converts to a block and takes no further clause. SpacedMotionForceBuilder A force or impulse whose frame has been named. SpacedMotionVelocityBuilder A velocity whose frame has been named. SpacedTransformOffsetBuilder A displacement whose frame has been named. It converts to a block and takes no further clause. SpawnBuilder What Object.Spawn(prefab) returns: a spawn with no placement yet. Add At(Vec3ValueBlock), ChildOf(string, string, int) and Into(string, string, int) in any order, or use it as a block, which spawns the prefab at its own pose. SpawnFramedBuilder What a frame modifier returns: a spawn whose placement and frame are both stated. It offers no second frame clause, which is what makes a conflicting pair uncompilable. SpawnPlacedBuilder What Object.Spawn(prefab).At(...) returns: a spawn whose placement is stated and whose frame is still the default, the parent's. SpawnPlacement Where an authored Object.Spawn puts the object it produces, and in which frame those coordinates are read. SpawnRequest One authored Object.Spawn that has run and has not been applied yet: which prefab input to produce from, where the produced object goes, what it is parented to, and which owned-object slot holds it. SyncCadence How often one synchronised variable is sent. Declared per variable, because AGENTS.md rule 46 says synchronised state is declared one variable at a time and there is no networked struct and no state object to put two variables into. SyncDeclaration One synchronised variable, as the script declared it: which slot holds it, how often it is sent, and the bookkeeping slots the cadence and the staleness reading need. Recorded at build time, read by the program, and never changed afterwards. SyncFactory The Sync surface: which parts of an object's transform cross the network, and how often each one is sent. Text A text literal written in a script, and the type argument that makes a text variable Var<Text>. TextArgument One value a Text.Format call fills a hole with. Numbers, flags, text variables and literals of those kinds all convert to it, so a call site writes the value and never this type's name. TextDefineBuilder What Define.Text(name) returns: a 64-byte fixed slot unless Allocating is called. TextSlot Where one text variable lives on every instance of a program, and how many bytes it holds. The capacity is part of the handle because each capacity is a separate array on the instance. TimeFactory The Time surface a script reads the game clock through, and the one place a script changes how fast that clock runs: Delta, Elapsed, Scale, IsPaused, SetScale(NumberValueBlock, string, int), Pause(string, int) and Resume(string, int). TransformFactory The Transform surface inside Build(): where the object a script runs on is, how it is turned and scaled, what is above and below it in the hierarchy, and what it is parented to. TransformOffsetBuilder What MoveBy and RotateBy return: the displacement, in the object's own frame unless a modifier says otherwise. TransformSyncDeclaration One Sync.Position, Sync.Rotation or Sync.Scale as the build recorded it: which channel, at which cadence, and which slots hold the per-object bookkeeping the network tick needs. Built by ScriptBuildContext and read by ScriptRunner; a script never sees one. TransformTargetFactory One step of the hierarchy around the object a script runs on: what Transform.Parent, Transform.Child(n) and Transform.Root return. TransformToBuilder What MoveTo, RotateTo and ScaleTo return: the destination, waiting for the duration. UiActivatedWatchBuilder What When.UI(button) returns. Activated is pointer click plus keyboard and gamepad submit. UiButton A handle to one named Button. UiGroup A handle to one named Group, for showing or hiding a cluster already in the panel UXML. Not a Place target. UiLabel A handle to one named Label. Returned by Panel.Label at build time. UiPlacement A Place fragment: the name scope for elements inside a cloned UXML, and a block so On.Ready(Panel.Place(...).At(...)) still compiles. Placement itself runs at spawn. UiProgressBar A handle to one named ProgressBar. UiText The current text of a Label or TextField, for PlayerName.Set(nameField.Text). UiTextField A handle to one named TextField. UiToggle A handle to one named Toggle. UiValueChangedWatchBuilder What When.UI(toggle), When.UI(bar) and When.UI(field) return. UtilityOption One scored option of a Choose selector: a score expression and the action that runs while that option is selected. UtilityOptionBuilder What Option(score) returns. Its one call, Then(params Block[]), names the action that runs while this option is selected. VarFactory The Var surface inside Build(): declares a script's variables and hands back the typed handles the blocks are built from. VarWatchBuilder<T> What When.Var(x) returns. Its only method is Changed(params Block[]), which registers the watch with the build. Var<T> A handle to one variable of a script. Returned by Var.Define at build time; the operators and methods on it build blocks. Vec2 A two-component spatial value: a stick deflection, a screen offset, a planar direction. Vec2Slot Where one Vec2 variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. Vec3 A three-component spatial value: a position, a direction, a displacement or a scale. Vec3Slot Where one Vec3 variable lives on every instance of a program. Allocated at build time and never at run time. ViewBuilder What View.For(view) returns: the two things a script does to a view. ViewFactory The View surface inside Build(): what a local player sees, and which camera rig it renders. WhenFactory The When surface inside Build(): registers blocks against a change in state rather than against an event the runner raises. Interfaces IAssetLoadOperation A load in flight. Adds the loaded object to IAsyncOperation. The object is meaningful only once the operation completed successfully. IAssetLoadProvider What an asset-load backend provides to AssetGateway: one load of a provider-qualified key, returned as an operation the gateway polls once per frame. Script code never sees this type; it sees Asset.Load and When.Operation. ICameraProvider What a camera backend provides to the CameraGateway: choosing which rig a view renders, sizing that view, and writing a rig's tracking targets. Script code never sees this type; it sees the View and Camera surfaces. ICloudLoadOperation A load in flight. Adds the loaded value to IAsyncOperation; the value is meaningful only once the operation completed successfully. ICloudSaveProvider What a Cloud Save backend provides to the CloudSaveGateway: sign-in, a save and a load, each returned as an operation the gateway polls once per frame. Script code never sees this type; it sees start blocks and outcome events. AGENTS.md section 12. IInputActionHandle The one thing every input action handle has in common: whether Build() produced it, and where its declaration sits in the program. IInputProvider What an input backend provides to the InputGateway: the resolution of a declared action name to something the backend can read, the four value reads, the three per-frame occurrence tests, and interactive rebind start, cancel and poll. Script code never sees this type; it sees the Input surface, When.Input and handle.Rebind().As. Cursor lock and visibility are not on this interface. INetworkProvider What a netcode backend provides to the NetworkGateway: a session to start and end, the connection facts a script is allowed to read, and two queues the gateway drains once per tick. Script code never sees this type; it sees the Net and Sync surfaces. AGENTS.md rule 49. IPackageVersionSource Answers which Unity package versions this project currently has installed. Adapter admission queries it at spawn, never per frame. IScriptAssetInputs The part of a host that carries the assets an author assigned to one object, so that two objects running the same script can hold different assets. IScriptHost The object a script runs on, as the blocks see it. Blocks reach the object through this interface and never through a GameObject, a Transform or a Component. IScriptHostCapabilities Optional explicit host capability declaration. Legacy hosts remain runtime hosts. IScriptNode Build-time requirements and child declarations for actions and expressions. IScriptObjectLifetime The part of a host that can activate, deactivate, create and destroy objects. A host that provides it declares RuntimeObjectLifetime by implementing this interface; a host that does not cannot run a script containing an Object block, and the spawn is refused with a message naming the missing service. IScriptObjectSpawner The part of a host that can produce a new object from a prefab. A host that provides it declares RuntimeObjectSpawning by implementing this interface; a host that does not cannot run a script containing an Object.Spawn block, and the spawn of that script is refused with a message naming the missing service. IScriptTrackingTarget The one thing a camera needs from the object a script runs on: something it can be told to follow or aim at. A host that can supply one implements this interface. IUiElementHandle The one thing every UI element handle has in common: whether Build() produced it, and where its declaration sits in the program. Enums ActionResult What an action reports about the objective it was given: still pending, finished having met it, or finished having failed to meet it. Anchor One of the nine reserved HUD regions a Panel.Place call can occupy: four corners, four edges, and the centre. ApplicationObservation Which of the five application observations a runner is delivering: what Unity reported about the application as a whole, rather than about one object. ArithmeticOperator Which arithmetic a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberArithmeticBlock performs. AssetPlaceholderSource Which configuration named the asset placeholder a type resolves to. AssetProvider Which provider finds an asset that a script names. CameraOperationResult What happened when the camera gateway asked its provider to do something. CameraTargetOperation What one target-group operation does to a camera rig's group of tracked objects. CameraTracking Which of a camera rig's two tracking targets an operation writes. ComparisonOperator Which comparison a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberComparisonBlock performs. DiagnosticCommandState Admission and terminal application states for one submitted command. DiagnosticRecordKind The observation represented by a console or trace record. GateCategory Systems a named gate may suppress for every script on the runner. Only input and camera exist as mute-able gateways in this version. InputActionResolution Why an input action declaration did or did not resolve to a configured action. InputPhase The three occurrences one input action reports, which are the three the accepted design names. InputRebindPoll What polling one in-flight rebind capture reports. Must allocate nothing while pending. InputRebindStart Whether an interactive rebind capture started, and why not when it did not. InputValueKind What one input action produces. The four kinds are the ones the accepted design names: Button, Number, Vector2 and Vector3. LifetimeRequest What an authored Object.Activate(), Object.Deactivate() or Object.Despawn() asked the runner to do to the object a script runs on. LunyScriptLogSeverity How serious one LunyScript log record is. MotionMechanism Which movement component ProbeMotionMechanism() selected. NetworkValueKind Which field of a NetworkValue carries the value. NumberFunction Which function a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberFunctionBlock evaluates, and which write a NumberMutateBlock applies to its slot. NumberState Which question a CodeSmile.LunyScript.NumberStateBlock asks about one number. Process Whether a script ticks while the runner is paused, and whether it ticks at all. ProcessOverride The Inspector override of Process on one LunyScriptBehaviour. RotationUnary Which orientation a CodeSmile.LunyScript.RotationUnaryBlock makes out of one. RoundingMode How Math.Round and Var<Number>.Round resolve a value exactly halfway between two whole numbers. ScriptContexts Execution contexts a node or service supports. ScriptServices Services required by composed nodes, independently of their execution contexts. SessionState What a session is doing. Read through Net.IsConnected and reported by State. SlotKind Which kind of slot a variable occupies. A slot kind is one array on ScriptInstance, so adding a kind is adding an array, a layout counter and a branch, and nothing else. SyncKind The three kinds of cadence. A rate cap is a property of OnChange rather than a fourth kind, because a capped and an uncapped OnChange send on the same condition and differ only in how often. TextArgumentKind Which kind of value one TextArgument carries. TextCapacity How many bytes a text variable can hold. Declared per variable at build time, because the five capacities are five distinct Unity.Collections.FixedString types and a text variable is stored in exactly one of them. TextLength Named byte bounds for each Text entry in a list or map. Declared per collection side at build time, because the five sizes are five distinct Unity.Collections.FixedString types and every entry on that side uses exactly one of them. TransformAxis Which component of a transform value a read produces. TransformChannel Which part of an object's transform a declaration synchronises. One channel is one declaration with one cadence, which is AGENTS.md rule 46 applied to the transform: a scale that never changes cannot share a payload with a position that changes every tick. TransformPart Which of the three values of a transform a verb reads or writes. TransformRelation Which object a transform verb acts on, named relative to the object the script runs on. TransformSpace Which frame a transform verb's numbers are in. Vec2Arithmetic Which combination a CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vec2ArithmeticBlock makes of two values. Vec2Component Which component a CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vec2WithComponentBlock replaces. Vec2Scalar Which number a CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vec2ScalarBlock takes out of one or two values. Vec2Unary Which spatial value a CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vec2UnaryBlock makes out of one. Vec3Arithmetic Which combination a CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vec3ArithmeticBlock makes of two spatial values. Vec3Component Which component a CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vec3WithComponentBlock replaces. Vec3Scalar Which number a CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vec3ScalarBlock takes out of one or two spatial values. Vec3Unary Which spatial value a CodeSmile.LunyScript.Vec3UnaryBlock makes out of one. Delegates AssetPlaceholderFactory Builds the asset placeholder for one declared asset type.
